tagline.zh: 先用一张流程图看清一次生成的全过程，再逐段展开。每个模块都有推导、可运行的练习和面试会追问的“为什么”。
tagline.en: One diagram of how a generation happens, then each part opened up in turn. Every module has derivations, runnable exercises and the why-questions interviewers keep asking.

note.zh: LLM agent 学习地图
note.en: Roadmap for LLM agents

note.zh: 从零到项目的爬虫教程
note.en: Scraping from zero to project

note.zh: 先看整体，再看局部。这个阶段把一次生成从头到尾走一遍，并说明后面每个阶段展开的是其中哪一段。
note.en: The whole first, the parts later. This stage walks through one generation from start to finish and says which part each later stage opens up.

why.zh: 没有整体图景时，后面每个部件都只是孤立的知识点，不清楚它解决的是哪个环节的问题。
why.en: Without the whole picture, every later component is an isolated fact, and it stays unclear which part of the process it serves.

what.zh: 用一句话把一次生成从头到尾走一遍，再交代训练和推理两条时间线。
what.en: Walks one sentence through a full generation, then lays out the two timelines of training and inference.

meaning.zh: 之后学到的每个概念都能放回这张流程图里找到位置。
meaning.en: Every concept learned later can be placed back on this diagram.

note.zh: 后面所有模块都建立在三件事上，即梯度怎样算出来、损失为什么是交叉熵、softmax 的梯度长什么样。
note.en: Everything later rests on three things, namely how gradients are computed, why the loss is cross-entropy, and what the gradient of softmax looks like.

why.zh: 模型的“学习”就是用梯度一点点调整参数。后面很多设计的理由都落在梯度和损失上，比如注意力为什么要缩放、为什么要有残差连接。不先弄清这两样，这些理由就无从理解。
why.en: A model learns by adjusting parameters little by little with gradients. Many later design choices are justified by gradients and the loss, such as why attention is scaled and why residual connections exist. Without these two, the justifications cannot be followed.

what.zh: 手写反向传播，从最大似然推出交叉熵损失，推出 softmax 的梯度。
what.en: Writes backpropagation by hand, derives the cross-entropy loss from maximum likelihood, and derives the gradient of softmax.

meaning.zh: 提供一套判断架构和训练设计的共同语言，即“这样做之后梯度会怎样，损失会怎样”。
meaning.en: Provides a shared language for judging architecture and training choices, namely what happens to the gradient and to the loss.

note.zh: 逐个部件手写一遍，最后拼成一个能训练的 mini-GPT。
note.en: Write each component by hand, then assemble a mini-GPT that trains.

why.zh: 阶段 0 里的“12 层”还是一个黑箱。模型的能力来自这些层怎样把上文的信息汇集到当前位置，不打开它就无法解释模型为什么能理解上下文。
why.en: The 12 layers of stage 0 are still a black box. A model's ability comes from how these layers gather information from the context into the current position, and without opening them it cannot be explained why a model understands context.

what.zh: 把一层拆成部件逐个实现，包括注意力、多头、掩码、位置编码、归一化与残差、MLP，最后分析计算代价。
what.en: Takes a layer apart and implements each component, namely attention, multiple heads, masking, positional encoding, normalization and residuals, and the MLP, then analyses the cost.

meaning.zh: 这是 LLM 的主体结构。长上下文为什么贵、训练为什么能并行、可解释性研究观察的是什么，都由这里的结构决定。
meaning.en: This is the main body of an LLM. Why long contexts are expensive, why training can be parallel and what interpretability research observes are all determined by the structure here.

note.zh: 模型看到的不是字，而是 token。很多奇怪现象的根源在这里。
note.en: The model sees tokens, not characters. Many odd behaviours start here.

why.zh: 模型只认识编号。文本怎样切分，直接决定模型看到的是什么、调用要花多少钱，以及哪些任务天生困难。
why.en: A model only knows ids. How text is split directly decides what the model sees, what a call costs and which tasks are hard by nature.

what.zh: 手写 BPE 分词，分析上下文窗口的限制，观察分词引起的典型问题。
what.en: Writes BPE tokenization by hand, analyses the limits of the context window and observes typical problems caused by tokenization.

meaning.zh: 数不清字母、算不准大数这类现象，根源多在输入的表示方式，而不在模型的推理能力。
meaning.en: Failures such as miscounting letters or large arithmetic mostly originate in how the input is represented, not in the model's reasoning ability.

note.zh: 从预训练到对齐，重点是每个损失函数从哪里来。
note.en: From pretraining to alignment, with a focus on where each loss comes from.

why.zh: 架构只是一个空壳，能力来自参数，而参数来自训练目标和数据。只看结构解释不了模型为什么会说话、为什么听指令。
why.en: The architecture is an empty shell. Ability comes from the parameters, and the parameters come from the training objective and the data. Structure alone cannot explain why a model can talk or follow instructions.

what.zh: 依次推导预训练、指令微调、RLHF、DPO 的损失函数，实现 LoRA，并讨论缩放定律。
what.en: Derives the losses of pretraining, instruction tuning, RLHF and DPO in turn, implements LoRA and discusses scaling laws.

meaning.zh: 关于模型行为的多数“为什么”，最后都要回到“它被训练去做什么”。幻觉和对齐问题的源头也在这里。
meaning.en: Most why-questions about model behaviour end at what the model was trained to do. Hallucination and alignment problems also start here.

note.zh: 同一组权重，不同的解码方式会得到很不一样的输出和速度。
note.en: Same weights, very different outputs and speeds depending on how you decode.

why.zh: 同一组参数，解码方式不同，输出的质量、随机性、速度和成本都不同。这是使用者能够直接控制的部分。
why.en: With the same parameters, different decoding gives different quality, randomness, speed and cost. This is the part a user controls directly.

what.zh: 给出各种采样策略的公式并实现，实现 KV cache，实现保证输出格式的约束解码。
what.en: Gives the formulas of the sampling strategies and implements them, implements the KV cache and implements constrained decoding that guarantees the output format.

meaning.zh: 它连接模型和产品。API 中的 temperature、top_p、max_tokens、JSON 模式等参数都作用在这一层。
meaning.en: It connects the model and the product. API parameters such as temperature, top_p, max_tokens and JSON mode all act at this layer.

note.zh: 闭源与开放权重模型的差别，以及许可证实际允许什么。
note.en: Closed versus open-weight models, and what licenses actually permit.

why.zh: 实际工作中需要在具体的模型之间做选择，而且选择受许可证约束。
why.en: Real work requires choosing between concrete models, and the choice is constrained by licenses.

what.zh: 比较闭源模型与开放权重模型，梳理常见许可证允许和禁止的用途。
what.en: Compares closed and open-weight models and sorts out what common licenses allow and forbid.

meaning.zh: 把前面的原理落实到“选哪个模型、能不能这样用”的现实决定上。
meaning.en: Brings the principles down to the practical decision of which model to pick and whether a given use is allowed.

note.zh: Prompt、RAG 和 agent，都先不用框架手写一遍。
note.en: Prompting, RAG and agents, each written without a framework first.

why.zh: 单次生成有固有的限制，包括知识有截止时间、读不到外部资料、不能执行操作。
why.en: A single generation has built-in limits, including a knowledge cutoff, no access to outside material and no ability to act.

what.zh: 不依赖框架实现 prompt 技巧、RAG 和 agent 循环，再与框架实现对比。
what.en: Implements prompting techniques, RAG and an agent loop without a framework, then compares with framework versions.

meaning.zh: 这是目前多数 LLM 应用的形态，也是外部证据进入模型的入口。
meaning.en: This is the form most LLM applications take today, and it is where outside evidence enters the model.

note.zh: 怎样知道模型好不好，以及出错时错在哪里。
note.en: How to tell whether a model is good, and where it fails.

why.zh: 输出流畅不等于正确。没有评估，就无法比较两个系统，也无法判断一次修改是否有改进。
why.en: Fluent output is not correct output. Without evaluation two systems cannot be compared, and it cannot be told whether a change is an improvement.

what.zh: 实现常用指标和 LLM 评委，分析幻觉、偏见与隐私问题，介绍欧盟、中国和美国对人工智能的监管要求。
what.en: Implements common metrics and an LLM judge, analyses hallucination, bias and privacy, and introduces how the European Union, China and the United States regulate AI.

meaning.zh: 决定一个系统能否被信任，以及能否合规地部署。
meaning.en: Decides whether a system can be trusted and deployed in compliance with the rules.

note.zh: 打开模型看内部，从观察注意力和逐层解码，到用干预检验因果作用。
note.en: Open the model up, from observing attention and decoding layer by layer to testing causal effects with interventions.

why.zh: 前面各阶段都把模型当作从输入到输出的函数。要知道它依据了什么得出回答，需要观察内部。
why.en: The earlier stages treat the model as a function from input to output. Knowing what it relied on for an answer requires looking inside.

what.zh: 实现注意力可视化、logit lens、activation patching、线性探针和引导向量。
what.en: Implements attention visualization, the logit lens, activation patching, linear probes and steering vectors.

meaning.zh: 把“模型为什么这样回答”从猜测变成可以检验的假设，是可解释性和安全研究的基础。
meaning.en: Turns the question of why a model answered as it did from a guess into a testable hypothesis, the basis of interpretability and safety research.

summary.zh: 文本进去，下一个 token 出来。把中间的六步走一遍，认识 token、logits、贪心解码和采样。
summary.en: Text goes in, the next token comes out. Walk through the six steps in between and meet tokens, logits, greedy decoding and sampling.

goals.zh: 能按顺序说出一次生成的六个步骤，以及每一步的输入和输出
goals.en: Name the six steps of one generation in order, with the input and output of each

goals.zh: 能解释 logits 是什么，贪心解码和采样各是怎样做的
goals.en: Explain what logits are and how greedy decoding and sampling work

goals.zh: 能说出为什么实际使用中多数情况采用采样
goals.en: Say why sampling is used in most practical settings

explain.zh: 大模型只做一件事，即给定一段文字，算出下一个 token 是词表里每一个候选的概率。聊天、写代码、翻译，都是把这件事重复很多次的结果。下面用 GPT-2 small 和一句话 `The capital of France is` 把这件事拆成六步。
explain.en: A large language model does one thing. Given some text, it computes the probability that the next token is each candidate in its vocabulary. Chatting, coding and translating are all the result of repeating this many times. Below, GPT-2 small and the sentence `The capital of France is` are used to split it into six steps.

explain.zh: **第一步，分词。** 模型不直接处理文字。文本先被切成小片段，称为 token，每个 token 在词表里有一个编号。这句话被切成 5 个 token，编号是 `[464, 3139, 286, 4881, 318]`，分别对应 `The`、` capital`、` of`、` France`、` is`。GPT-2 的词表有 50257 个 token。
explain.en: **Step one, tokenization.** The model does not process characters directly. Text is first cut into small pieces called tokens, and every token has an id in the vocabulary. This sentence becomes 5 tokens with ids `[464, 3139, 286, 4881, 318]`, standing for `The`, ` capital`, ` of`, ` France` and ` is`. The vocabulary of GPT-2 has 50257 tokens.

explain.zh: **第二步，嵌入。** 每个编号到一张表里查出一个向量，GPT-2 small 中是 768 个数。再加上一个表示位置的向量，让模型知道这个 token 排在第几个。到这里，5 个 token 变成了 5 个向量。
explain.en: **Step two, embedding.** Each id is looked up in a table and becomes a vector, 768 numbers in GPT-2 small. A second vector that encodes the position is added so the model knows where the token sits. At this point 5 tokens have become 5 vectors.

explain.zh: **第三步，Transformer 层。** 这 5 个向量依次通过 12 层。每一层做两件事。注意力让各个位置之间交换信息，比如让 ` is` 这个位置看到前面的 ` France`。MLP 让每个位置独自加工自己的向量。向量的形状始终不变，内容一层层被改写。
explain.en: **Step three, the Transformer layers.** The 5 vectors pass through 12 layers in turn. Each layer does two things. Attention lets positions exchange information, for example letting the position of ` is` see ` France` before it. The MLP lets each position process its own vector alone. The shape of the vectors never changes, while their content is rewritten layer by layer.

explain.zh: **第四步，logits。** 取最后一个位置的向量，乘上一个矩阵，得到 50257 个数，词表里每个 token 一个。这些数称为 **logits**，是模型给每个候选打的原始分数，可正可负，加起来也不等于 1。分数越高，表示模型越倾向于这个 token。
explain.en: **Step four, logits.** The vector at the last position is multiplied by a matrix, giving 50257 numbers, one per token in the vocabulary. These numbers are called **logits**. They are the raw scores the model gives each candidate, they can be positive or negative, and they do not sum to 1. A higher score means the model leans more towards that token.

explain.zh: **第五步，概率。** softmax 把 logits 变成概率。对这句话，GPT-2 small 给出的前五名是 ` the` 8.5%、` now` 4.8%、` a` 4.6%、` France` 3.2%、` Paris` 3.2%。可以看到模型给出的是一整个分布，而不是一个答案。
explain.en: **Step five, probabilities.** Softmax turns the logits into probabilities. For this sentence the top five of GPT-2 small are ` the` 8.5%, ` now` 4.8%, ` a` 4.6%, ` France` 3.2% and ` Paris` 3.2%. The model produces a whole distribution, not one answer.

explain.zh: **第六步，选一个 token。** 最直接的办法是每次都选概率最大的那个，称为**贪心解码** (greedy decoding)。另一种办法是按概率随机抽一个，称为**采样** (sampling)，概率 8.5% 的 token 就有 8.5% 的机会被抽中。选出的 token 接到输入后面，回到第二步再算下一个，直到模型输出结束符或者达到长度上限。这种一个接一个往后生成的方式称为**自回归** (autoregressive)。
explain.en: **Step six, choosing a token.** The most direct way is to take the most probable one every time, called **greedy decoding**. The other way is to draw one at random according to the probabilities, called **sampling**, so a token with probability 8.5% is drawn 8.5% of the time. The chosen token is appended to the input and the process returns to step two for the next one, until the model emits an end token or a length limit is reached. Generating one token after another in this way is called **autoregressive** generation.

explain.zh: **为什么需要采样。** 贪心解码看起来最合理，实际效果却常常不好。让 GPT-2 small 贪心续写 `The meaning of life is`，40 个 token 里同一句话 `not the same as the meaning of death.` 重复了三遍，这是本模块练习 2 实际跑出的结果。Holtzman 等人在 2019 年的论文中系统地描述了这一现象，即以最大化概率为目标的解码倾向于产生平淡且重复的文本。采样引入了随机性，文本更多样，代价是同一个 prompt 每次的输出不同。
explain.en: **Why sampling is needed.** Greedy decoding looks like the most reasonable choice, yet its results are often poor. When GPT-2 small continues `The meaning of life is` greedily, the same sentence `not the same as the meaning of death.` appears three times within 40 tokens, which is the actual output of exercise 2 in this module. Holtzman and colleagues described the phenomenon systematically in 2019, namely that decoding which maximizes probability tends to produce bland and repetitive text. Sampling introduces randomness and makes text more varied, at the price that the same prompt gives a different output each time.

caption.zh: 一次生成的六步。方框下方标出了详细展开这一步的阶段。虚线表示选出的 token 被接回输入，循环继续。
caption.en: The six steps of one generation. Under each box is the stage that opens it up in detail. The dashed line shows the chosen token being appended to the input so the loop continues.

title.en: The four formulas behind the six steps

note.zh: 嵌入。$x_t$ 是第 $t$ 个 token 的编号，$E$ 是 token 嵌入表，$P$ 是位置嵌入表。$h^{(0)}_t$ 是进入第一层之前的向量。
note.en: Embedding. $x_t$ is the id of token $t$, $E$ the token embedding table and $P$ the position embedding table. $h^{(0)}_t$ is the vector before the first layer.

note.zh: 依次通过 $L$ 层。每个 Block 内部是注意力加 MLP，在阶段 2 展开。
note.en: Pass through $L$ layers in turn. Inside each Block are attention and an MLP, opened up in stage 2.

note.zh: logits。最后一层的向量先做一次归一化，再乘以矩阵 $W_U$，得到词表大小 $V$ 个分数。$W_U$ 常被称为 unembedding。GPT-2 中它与 $E$ 共用同一组参数。
note.en: Logits. The vector of the last layer is normalized and multiplied by the matrix $W_U$, giving $V$ scores, one per vocabulary entry. $W_U$ is often called the unembedding. In GPT-2 it shares its parameters with $E$.

note.zh: 概率。softmax 的性质和梯度在 1.3 推导。
note.en: Probabilities. The properties and gradient of softmax are derived in 1.3.

source.text: Holtzman et al., The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration, arXiv:1904.09751

note.zh: 贪心解码。结果完全由输入决定，没有随机性。
note.en: Greedy decoding. The result is fully determined by the input, with no randomness.

note.zh: 采样。以 $p_i$ 的概率选中第 $i$ 个 token。
note.en: Sampling. Token $i$ is chosen with probability $p_i$.

note.zh: 带温度的采样。先把 logits 除以温度 $T$。$T$ 小于 1 时分布变尖，接近贪心。$T$ 大于 1 时分布变平，更随机。top-k 和 top-p 是在此基础上先去掉低概率的候选再采样，在 5.1 展开。
note.en: Sampling with temperature. The logits are first divided by the temperature $T$. Below 1 the distribution sharpens and approaches greedy. Above 1 it flattens and becomes more random. Top-k and top-p additionally remove low-probability candidates before sampling, covered in 5.1.

note.zh: 整段文本的概率是每一步概率的乘积。贪心解码每一步取最大，但每一步最大不保证乘积最大，见下一步的例子。
note.en: The probability of a whole text is the product of the per-step probabilities. Greedy decoding takes the maximum at each step, but a maximum at every step does not guarantee the largest product. See the example in the next step.

note.zh: 一个两步的例子。第一步 A 的概率是 0.6，B 是 0.4，贪心选 A。但 A 之后最好的续写只有 0.5，而 B 之后有一个 0.9 的续写。贪心得到的整句概率反而更低。beam search 通过同时保留多条候选来缓解这一点。
note.en: A two-step example. At step one A has probability 0.6 and B has 0.4, so greedy takes A. Yet the best continuation after A has only 0.5, while after B there is one with 0.9. The greedy sentence ends up less probable. Beam search eases this by keeping several candidates at once.

note.zh: 名字来自统计学。在二分类里，logit 函数把概率变成一个可以取任意实数的分数，它是 sigmoid 的反函数。
note.en: The name comes from statistics. In binary classification the logit function turns a probability into a score that can be any real number. It is the inverse of the sigmoid.

steps.tex: \log p_i = z_i - \log\sum_k e^{z_k} \;\;\Rightarrow\;\; z_i = \log p_i + C

note.zh: 多分类时沿用了这个名字。对 softmax 取对数可以看到，logits 就是对数概率加上一个对所有 token 相同的常数 $C$。所以 logits 可以理解为“还没有归一化的对数概率”。
note.en: The name was kept for the multi-class case. Taking the log of softmax shows that the logits are log-probabilities plus a constant $C$ shared by all tokens. Logits can therefore be read as log-probabilities that have not been normalized yet.

q.zh: logits 到底是什么？
q.en: What exactly are logits?

a.zh: 模型最后一层输出的原始分数，词表里每个 token 一个。它们还不是概率，经过 softmax 之后才是。两个 token 的 logit 相差 1，概率就相差约 2.7 倍。之所以保留 logits 这一层而不让模型直接输出概率，是因为在分数上做运算更方便也更稳定，温度、top-k、约束解码等操作都是直接修改 logits。
a.en: The raw scores from the last layer of the model, one per token in the vocabulary. They are not yet probabilities and become probabilities after softmax. A gap of 1 between two logits means a probability ratio of about 2.7. The logit level is kept, without having the model output probabilities directly, because arithmetic on scores is more convenient and more stable. Temperature, top-k and constrained decoding all work by editing the logits.

q.zh: 为什么模型输出的是一个概率分布，而不是直接给出一个词？
q.en: Why does the model output a distribution and not simply a word?

a.zh: 因为同一段上文后面可以接很多合理的内容。`The capital of France is` 后面可以是 ` Paris`，也可以是 ` the city of`、` a`、` located`。训练目标要求模型给训练文本中实际出现的下一个 token 尽量高的概率（见 1.2），学到的自然是一个分布。分布还把“模型怎么想”和“最后怎么选”分开了，同一个模型可以搭配不同的解码方式。
a.en: Because many reasonable things can follow the same context. After `The capital of France is` the next token can be ` Paris`, but also ` the city of`, ` a` or ` located`. The training objective asks the model to give high probability to the token that actually came next in the training text (see 1.2), so what it learns is a distribution. A distribution also separates what the model believes from how the final choice is made, so the same model can be paired with different decoding methods.

q.zh: 为什么不总是选概率最大的 token？
q.en: Why not take the most probable token every time?

a.zh: 有三个原因。贪心解码容易陷入重复，练习 2 中可以直接看到。每一步都选最大并不能保证整句概率最大，见上面的两步例子。此外很多任务本身需要多样性，比如写作和头脑风暴，每次都得到同一个回答并不合适。需要确定性的场景，比如评测和抽取短答案，贪心解码仍然常用。
a.en: There are three reasons. Greedy decoding easily falls into repetition, which exercise 2 shows directly. Taking the maximum at each step does not guarantee the most probable sentence, as the two-step example above shows. And many tasks need variety, such as writing and brainstorming, where the same answer every time is unsuitable. Where determinism is needed, such as evaluation or extracting short answers, greedy decoding is still common.

q.zh: 为什么回答是一个字一个字出来的？
q.en: Why does the answer appear piece by piece?

a.zh: 因为生成本身就是这样进行的。每生成一个 token 都要完整地做一次前向计算，新的 token 接到输入后面才能算下一个。界面上的流式输出只是把每一步的结果及时显示出来。这也是输出越长等待越久的原因。
a.en: Because generation works that way. Every new token needs one full forward pass, and the next one can only be computed after the new token has been appended to the input. Streaming in the interface simply shows each result as it arrives. This is also why longer outputs take longer.

q.zh: 为什么同样的 prompt 每次输出不一样？
q.en: Why does the same prompt give a different output each time?

a.zh: 主要原因是第六步用了采样，每一步都按概率随机抽取，前面抽到不同的 token，后面的上文就不同，差别会越来越大。固定随机种子可以复现同一次采样，练习 3 会验证这一点。把温度设为 0 相当于贪心解码，但在线上服务中仍可能有细微差别，原因涉及浮点运算和服务端的批处理，在 5.1 详细讨论。
a.en: The main reason is that step six samples. Every step draws at random according to the probabilities, and once an earlier draw differs, the context for everything after it differs, so the outputs drift apart. Fixing the random seed reproduces the same draw, which exercise 3 verifies. Setting the temperature to 0 amounts to greedy decoding, yet hosted services can still show small differences for reasons that involve floating-point arithmetic and server-side batching, discussed in detail in 5.1.

q.zh: 为什么 GPT-2 只给 Paris 3% 的概率？
q.en: Why does GPT-2 give Paris only 3%?

a.zh: 有两方面原因。GPT-2 small 是一个很小的模型，掌握的事实有限。另一方面，模型预测的是“下一个 token 是什么”，不是“问题的答案是什么”。在它见过的文本里，这句话后面接 ` the`（比如 the city of Paris）或 ` a` 同样常见。概率低不一定表示模型不知道答案，只表示这个 token 不是唯一合理的续写。
a.en: There are two sides to it. GPT-2 small is a very small model and knows a limited number of facts. Also, the model predicts what the next token is, not what the answer to a question is. In the text it has seen, this sentence is followed just as often by ` the` (as in the city of Paris) or ` a`. A low probability does not necessarily mean the model lacks the answer. It only means this token is not the sole reasonable continuation.

why.zh: 后面所有模块讲的都是这条流程中的某一步。先把整条流程走通，才知道每个细节是在解决哪里的问题。
why.en: Every later module covers one step of this pipeline. Walking the whole pipeline first shows which problem each detail solves.

plain.zh: 把模型想成手机输入法联想功能的加强版。打出“今天天气”，输入法会给出几个候选词，各有各的可能性，选一个之后，它再根据新的句子给出下一批候选。大模型做的是同一件事，只是候选是整个词表，打分的依据是许多层的计算而不是简单的词频。
plain.en: Think of the model as a much stronger version of the word suggestions on a phone keyboard. After typing the weather today, the keyboard offers a few candidate words with different likelihoods, one is chosen, and it offers the next candidates for the new sentence. A large model does the same thing, except that the candidates are the whole vocabulary and the scores come from many layers of computation and not from simple word counts.

title.zh: 模型的一生与路线设计
title.en: The life of a model and the design of this roadmap

summary.zh: 训练时和推理时是两条不同的时间线。弄清参数从哪里来、存在哪里，以及后面九个阶段为什么按这个顺序排。
summary.en: Training time and inference time are two different timelines. See where parameters come from, where they live, and why the nine later stages come in this order.

goals.zh: 能区分训练时和推理时各发生什么
goals.en: Tell apart what happens at training time and at inference time

goals.zh: 能说出参数、超参数和 checkpoint 的区别
goals.en: State the difference between parameters, hyperparameters and a checkpoint

goals.zh: 能把后面每个阶段对应到流程中的位置
goals.en: Place each later stage on the pipeline

explain.zh: 上一个模块走的是**推理时**的流程。那时模型的参数是固定的，只负责把输入算成输出。参数本身从哪里来，属于另一条时间线，即**训练时**。把这两条线分清楚，后面的内容就不容易混。
explain.en: The previous module walked through the **inference-time** pipeline. There the parameters of the model are fixed and only turn inputs into outputs. Where the parameters come from belongs to another timeline, **training time**. Keeping the two apart makes everything later easier to follow.

explain.zh: **训练时。** 先收集大量文本，并在上面训练出分词器。然后做预训练，让模型在海量文本上反复预测下一个 token。每一步都是先做一次与推理相同的前向计算得到概率，用交叉熵衡量预测与真实 token 的差距，再用反向传播算出每个参数该怎样调整。预训练得到的模型会续写，但不一定听指令，所以接着做指令微调，再用人类偏好数据做对齐，最后评估并发布。
explain.en: **Training time.** A large body of text is collected and a tokenizer is trained on it. Pretraining follows, in which the model predicts the next token over and over on vast amounts of text. Each step runs the same forward pass as inference to get probabilities, measures the gap to the true token with cross-entropy, and uses backpropagation to work out how every parameter should change. A pretrained model can continue text but does not necessarily follow instructions, so instruction tuning comes next, then alignment with human preference data, and finally evaluation and release.

explain.zh: **推理时。** 参数冻结，剩下的只有 0.1 里的循环，即前向计算、选 token、接回输入。实际应用会在这个循环外面再搭一层。prompt 决定放进去什么文字，RAG 先检索资料再放进去，agent 让模型的输出触发工具调用并把结果再放回去。
explain.en: **Inference time.** The parameters are frozen and what remains is the loop of 0.1, a forward pass, a token choice and an append. Real applications build another layer around this loop. The prompt decides what text goes in, RAG retrieves material first and puts it in, and an agent lets the model's output trigger tool calls whose results are fed back in.

explain.zh: **还有第三个视角，解剖。** 前向计算的中间结果，比如每一层的向量和注意力权重，都可以取出来研究，用来回答模型在内部依据了什么。这是可解释性研究做的事。
explain.en: **There is a third view, dissection.** The intermediate results of the forward pass, such as the vectors of each layer and the attention weights, can be taken out and studied to ask what the model relied on internally. This is what interpretability research does.

explain.zh: **路线为什么这样排。** 阶段 1 准备数学工具，因为流程里的 softmax、交叉熵和反向传播后面处处要用。阶段 2 讲模型这个函数本身。阶段 3 讲输入端，即文本怎样变成 token。阶段 4 讲参数是怎样训练出来的。阶段 5 讲输出端，即怎样选 token 以及怎样算得快。阶段 6 看训练的产物，也就是各种模型。阶段 7 讲怎样在外面搭应用。阶段 8 讲怎样检验结果。阶段 9 回到模型内部做解剖。每个阶段开头都会指出它对应流程中的哪一段。
explain.en: **Why the roadmap is ordered this way.** Stage 1 prepares the mathematics, because softmax, cross-entropy and backpropagation appear everywhere later. Stage 2 covers the model as a function. Stage 3 covers the input side, how text becomes tokens. Stage 4 covers how the parameters are trained. Stage 5 covers the output side, how tokens are chosen and how the computation is made fast. Stage 6 looks at what training produces, the models themselves. Stage 7 covers building applications around them. Stage 8 covers checking the results. Stage 9 returns inside the model for dissection. Each stage begins by pointing to its place in the pipeline.

explain.zh: **参数存在哪里。** GPT-2 small 有约 1.24 亿个参数。按部件统计，token 嵌入表占 31%，各层的 MLP 占 45.5%，各层的注意力占 22.8%，其余不到 1%。这是练习 1 要亲手数出来的结果。模型变大时，层数和宽度增加，绝大部分参数都在各层里，嵌入表的占比会降到很低。
explain.en: **Where the parameters live.** GPT-2 small has about 124 million parameters. By component, the token embedding table holds 31%, the MLPs of all layers 45.5%, the attention of all layers 22.8%, and the rest under 1%. Exercise 1 has you count this yourself. As models grow in depth and width, nearly all parameters sit in the layers and the share of the embedding table becomes small.

caption.zh: 训练时、推理时和解剖三个视角，以及各阶段的位置。圆圈里的数字是阶段编号。
caption.en: The three views of training time, inference time and dissection, with the place of each stage. The numbers in circles are stage numbers.

title.zh: 数一数 GPT-2 的参数

note.zh: token 嵌入表有 $V$ 行，位置嵌入表有 $n_{\text{ctx}}$ 行，每行 $d$ 个数。GPT-2 small 中 $V = 50257$，$n_{\text{ctx}} = 1024$，$d = 768$。
note.en: The token embedding table has $V$ rows and the position table has $n_{\text{ctx}}$ rows, each with $d$ numbers. In GPT-2 small $V = 50257$, $n_{\text{ctx}} = 1024$ and $d = 768$.

note.zh: 每层注意力有四个 $d\times d$ 的矩阵及其偏置。它们各自的作用在 2.1 和 2.2 讲。
note.en: Each attention layer has four $d\times d$ matrices with their biases. What each does is covered in 2.1 and 2.2.

note.zh: MLP 先把向量扩到 4 倍宽再压回来，所以参数量是注意力的两倍左右。
note.en: The MLP widens the vector fourfold and narrows it back, so it has about twice the parameters of attention.

steps.tex: \text{total} = V d + n_{\text{ctx}}\, d + L\,\big(12 d^2 + 13 d\big) + 2d

note.zh: 每层还有两个 LayerNorm，各 $2d$ 个参数，最后还有一个。$W_U$ 与嵌入表共用参数，不另计。
note.en: Each layer also has two LayerNorms with $2d$ parameters each, and there is one more at the end. $W_U$ shares its parameters with the embedding table and adds nothing.

note.zh: 代入 GPT-2 small 的数值，与 PyTorch 统计的结果一致。面试里常见的“估算某个模型的参数量”就是这个算法，记住每层约 $12d^2$ 即可。
note.en: Plugging in GPT-2 small matches the count from PyTorch. The common interview task of estimating the parameters of a model is this calculation, and remembering about $12d^2$ per layer is enough.

q.zh: 训练和推理有什么区别？
q.en: What is the difference between training and inference?

a.zh: 训练时参数在变，推理时参数不变。训练的每一步包含一次前向计算、一次损失计算和一次反向传播，然后更新参数。推理只有前向计算。所以训练需要保存所有中间结果和梯度，显存和算力开销都大得多（见 1.1）。
a.en: During training the parameters change and during inference they do not. A training step has a forward pass, a loss computation and a backward pass, followed by a parameter update. Inference has only the forward pass. Training therefore has to keep all intermediate results and gradients, which costs far more memory and compute (see 1.1).

q.zh: 参数、权重、超参数、checkpoint 分别指什么？
q.en: What do parameters, weights, hyperparameters and checkpoint refer to?

a.zh: 参数是模型里通过训练学到的数，比如嵌入表和各层的矩阵。权重通常是参数的同义词。超参数是训练前由人设定、训练中不会被梯度更新的量，比如层数、向量宽度、学习率、batch 大小。checkpoint 是某一时刻全部参数的存档文件，“下载模型”下载的就是它。
a.en: Parameters are the numbers a model learns through training, such as the embedding table and the matrices of each layer. Weights is usually a synonym for parameters. Hyperparameters are set by people before training and are not updated by gradients, such as the number of layers, the vector width, the learning rate and the batch size. A checkpoint is a file that stores all parameters at one moment, and downloading a model means downloading one.

q.zh: 下载下来的模型文件里有什么？
q.en: What is inside a downloaded model?

a.zh: 主要是三样东西。权重文件，即一大批带名字的张量。配置文件，记录层数、宽度等超参数，用来把网络结构搭起来。分词器文件，记录词表和切分规则。里面没有数据库，也没有训练文本，模型掌握的内容都以数值的形式分散在权重里。
a.en: Mainly three things. The weight file, a large set of named tensors. The config file, which records hyperparameters such as depth and width so the network can be built. The tokenizer files, which record the vocabulary and the splitting rules. There is no database and no training text inside. What the model knows is spread across the weights as numbers.

q.zh: 为什么模型不能在对话中边用边学？
q.en: Why can a model not learn while it is being used?

a.zh: 因为推理时参数是冻结的，对话不会改变它们。模型在一次对话中表现出的“记住”，来自前面的内容仍然在输入里，每一步都被重新读了一遍。超出上下文窗口的内容就读不到了，这在 3.2 讨论。产品层面的记忆功能是把信息存在外部，再在需要时放回输入。
a.en: Because the parameters are frozen at inference time and a conversation does not change them. What looks like remembering within a conversation comes from the earlier content still being in the input and being read again at every step. Content beyond the context window can no longer be read, which 3.2 discusses. Memory features in products store information outside the model and put it back into the input when needed.

q.zh: kernel 是什么意思？
q.en: What does kernel mean?

a.zh: 这个词在不同场合指不同的东西。在 Jupyter 和 Colab 里，kernel 是在后台执行代码的进程，“restart kernel” 就是重启它并清空所有变量。在卷积网络里，kernel 指卷积核。在 GPU 编程里，kernel 指在 GPU 上运行的一段函数。本路线的练习中遇到的基本是第一种。更多基础术语见页面上的术语表。
a.en: The word means different things in different places. In Jupyter and Colab the kernel is the background process that runs the code, and restarting the kernel clears all variables. In convolutional networks a kernel is the convolution filter. In GPU programming a kernel is a function that runs on the GPU. The exercises of this roadmap mostly meet the first meaning. The glossary on this page has more basic terms.

why.zh: 同一个模型在训练时和推理时做的事不同，很多困惑来自把两者混在一起。这个模块把它们分开，并说明整条路线的编排理由。
why.en: The same model does different things at training time and at inference time, and much confusion comes from mixing the two. This module separates them and gives the reasons for the order of the roadmap.

plain.zh: 模型的一生可以类比为一个人先上学、再工作。训练相当于上学，通过大量练习题不断修改脑中的参数。推理相当于毕业后上岗，知识已经定型，只是拿来用。对话中告诉它的新东西像写在便签上，便签被拿走（对话结束或超出窗口）就没有了，它本身并没有因此改变。
plain.en: The life of a model resembles a person who first goes to school and then to work. Training is school, where the parameters in the head are revised through a great many practice questions. Inference is the job after graduation, where the knowledge is fixed and merely applied. New things told to it in a conversation are like notes on a slip of paper. Once the slip is taken away (the conversation ends or the window is exceeded) they are gone, and the model itself has not changed.

summary.zh: 手写一个 100 行的标量 autograd，弄清 loss.backward() 到底做了什么。
summary.en: Write a 100-line scalar autograd and see what loss.backward() really does.

goals.zh: 能在纸上对一个小计算图做反向传播
goals.en: Backpropagate through a small graph on paper

goals.zh: 能解释梯度为什么要累加，为什么要按拓扑序
goals.en: Explain why gradients accumulate and why topological order matters

goals.zh: 能说明反向模式相对前向模式的优势和代价
goals.en: State what reverse mode buys over forward mode, and what it costs

explain.zh: 张量就是带形状的多维数组。标量是 0 维张量，向量是 1 维，矩阵是 2 维，一批 token 的隐藏状态是 3 维 `(batch, seq, dim)`。神经网络的全部计算都是张量之间的加法、乘法和少数几个非线性函数。
explain.en: A tensor is a multi-dimensional array with a shape. A scalar is 0-D, a vector 1-D, a matrix 2-D, and a batch of hidden states is 3-D `(batch, seq, dim)`. Everything a neural network computes is additions, multiplications and a few nonlinear functions on tensors.

explain.zh: 训练只做一件事，就是把每个参数朝着让损失变小的方向挪一点。要知道朝哪边挪，需要损失对每一个参数的导数，也就是梯度。GPT 级别的模型有几十亿个参数，手推是不现实的。
explain.en: Training does one thing. It nudges every parameter in the direction that lowers the loss. Knowing the direction means knowing the derivative of the loss with respect to every parameter, the gradient. A GPT-scale model has billions of parameters, so nobody derives these by hand.

explain.zh: 自动求导的思路很朴素。前向计算时，每做一步基本运算就顺手记下两件事，即这个结果是由谁算出来的，以及这一步的**局部导数**是多少。记下来的这张图叫计算图。
explain.en: Automatic differentiation is a simple idea. During the forward pass, each elementary operation records two things. One is which values produced the result. The other is the **local derivative** of that step. The record is called the computational graph.

explain.zh: 反向传播从损失出发，沿着图倒着走。每个节点把自己收到的梯度乘上局部导数，再交给它的输入。如果一个值被用了不止一次，各条路径送回来的梯度相加。整个算法就是链式法则加上一个合适的遍历顺序。
explain.en: Backpropagation starts at the loss and walks the graph backwards. Each node multiplies the gradient it received by its local derivative and hands the product to its inputs. When a value is used more than once, the gradients arriving along each path are added. The whole algorithm is the chain rule plus a suitable traversal order.

explain.zh: PyTorch 的 `loss.backward()` 做的是同一件事，区别只在于节点是张量而不是单个数。本模块先用标量把机制写清楚，后面的模块再回到张量。
explain.en: `loss.backward()` in PyTorch does the same thing. The only difference is that nodes are tensors instead of single numbers. This module makes the mechanism clear with scalars, and later modules return to tensors.

caption.zh: 表达式 L = (a·b + c)·a 的计算图。每个方框上面一行是前向算出的值，下面一行是反向传回的梯度。a 有两条出边，所以它的梯度是两条路径之和。
caption.en: The graph of L = (a·b + c)·a. In each box the top line is the forward value and the bottom line is the gradient that flows back. Node a has two outgoing edges, so its gradient is the sum over both paths.

steps.tex: e = a\,b,\qquad d = e + c,\qquad L = d\,a

note.zh: 把表达式拆成基本运算。取 $a=2,\ b=-3,\ c=10$，前向得到 $e=-6,\ d=4,\ L=8$。
note.en: Split the expression into elementary steps. With $a=2,\ b=-3,\ c=10$ the forward pass gives $e=-6,\ d=4,\ L=8$.

note.zh: 反向传播的起点。
note.en: The starting point of the backward pass.

note.zh: $L = d\cdot a$ 是乘法，对其中一个因子求导得到另一个因子。
note.en: $L = d\cdot a$ is a product, so the derivative with respect to one factor is the other factor.

steps.tex: \frac{\partial L}{\partial e} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial d}\cdot 1 = 2,\qquad \frac{\partial L}{\partial c} = \frac{\partial L}{\partial d}\cdot 1 = 2

note.zh: 加法的局部导数是 1，梯度原样传给两个输入。
note.en: The local derivative of addition is 1, so the gradient passes unchanged to both inputs.

note.zh: $e = a\cdot b$，对 $b$ 的局部导数是 $a$。
note.en: $e = a\cdot b$, and its local derivative with respect to $b$ is $a$.

steps.tex: \frac{\partial L}{\partial a} = \underbrace{d}_{\text{via } L = d\,a} + \underbrace{\frac{\partial L}{\partial e}\cdot b}_{\text{via } e = a\,b} = 4 + 2\cdot(-3) = -2

note.zh: $a$ 被用了两次，两条路径的贡献相加。这就是代码里写 `+=` 而不是 `=` 的原因。
note.en: $a$ is used twice and the two contributions add. This is why the code says `+=` and not `=`.

steps.tex: L = a^2 b + a c \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{\partial L}{\partial a} = 2ab + c = -12 + 10 = -2

note.zh: 直接展开求导来核对，结果一致。
note.en: Check by expanding and differentiating directly. The results agree.

title.zh: 一般规则与局部导数表
title.en: The general rule and the table of local derivatives

steps.tex: \frac{\partial L}{\partial v} \;=\; \sum_{u \,\in\, \mathrm{users}(v)} \frac{\partial L}{\partial u}\,\frac{\partial u}{\partial v}

note.zh: 多元链式法则。$\mathrm{users}(v)$ 是直接用到 $v$ 的所有节点。求和号对应代码里的 `+=`。
note.en: The multivariate chain rule. $\mathrm{users}(v)$ are the nodes that use $v$ directly. The sum is the `+=` in the code.

steps.tex: \begin{array}{l|l} u = x + y & \partial u/\partial x = 1,\ \ \partial u/\partial y = 1 \\ u = x\,y & \partial u/\partial x = y,\ \ \partial u/\partial y = x \\ u = x^{k} & \partial u/\partial x = k\,x^{k-1} \\ u = \tanh x & \partial u/\partial x = 1 - u^{2} \\ u = e^{x} & \partial u/\partial x = u \end{array}

note.zh: 每种基本运算只需要知道自己的局部导数。练习 1 要实现的就是这张表。
note.en: Each elementary operation only needs its own local derivative. Exercise 1 implements exactly this table.

note.zh: 处理 $v$ 之前，所有用到它的节点都要先处理完，否则 $\partial L/\partial v$ 还没加全。拓扑排序后倒序遍历可以满足这个条件。
note.en: Before $v$ is processed, every node that uses it must be finished, otherwise $\partial L/\partial v$ is still incomplete. A reversed topological order satisfies this.

source.text: Baydin et al., Automatic differentiation in machine learning: a survey, arXiv:1502.05767

note.zh: 把网络看成从 $n$ 个参数到 $m$ 个输出的函数，$J$ 是雅可比矩阵。
note.en: View the network as a function from $n$ parameters to $m$ outputs, with Jacobian $J$.

steps.tex: \text{forward mode: one pass} \to J\,v \quad(\text{one column when } v = e_j)

note.zh: 前向模式一次传播得到一个输入方向上的导数，要拿到完整梯度需要 $n$ 次。
note.en: Forward mode gives the derivative along one input direction per pass. The full gradient needs $n$ passes.

steps.tex: \text{reverse mode: one pass} \to u^{\top} J \quad(\text{one row when } u = e_i)

note.zh: 反向模式一次传播得到一个输出对所有输入的导数，需要 $m$ 次。
note.en: Reverse mode gives the derivative of one output with respect to all inputs per pass. It needs $m$ passes.

note.zh: 损失是标量，所以反向模式一次就够。代价是前向的中间结果要全部保留到反向结束，这是训练显存远高于推理的主要原因之一。
note.en: The loss is a scalar, so one reverse pass is enough. The price is that every intermediate value of the forward pass must be kept until the backward pass ends, one of the main reasons training needs far more memory than inference.

q.zh: 为什么每个训练步都要调用 optimizer.zero_grad()？
q.en: Why call optimizer.zero_grad() at every training step?

a.zh: 因为 `backward()` 对梯度做的是累加。累加是算法本身需要的，同一个参数在图里被用到多次时各条路径必须相加。框架分不清一次反向传播里的多条路径和上一步遗留的旧值，所以清零交给使用者。这个行为也有用处，显存不够时可以连续几个小 batch 只做 `backward()`、隔几步再更新，等效于更大的 batch，这就是梯度累积。
a.en: Because `backward()` adds to the stored gradient. The algorithm needs this, since a parameter used several times in the graph must sum the contributions of every path. The framework cannot tell paths within one backward pass from stale values left by the previous step, so clearing is left to the user. The behaviour is also useful. When memory is short, several small batches can call `backward()` before a single update, which behaves like a larger batch. This is gradient accumulation.

q.zh: 为什么推理时要加 torch.no_grad()？
q.en: Why wrap inference in torch.no_grad()?

a.zh: 反向模式需要保留前向的中间结果。推理不做反向传播，这些结果没有用处。`no_grad()` 让 PyTorch 不建计算图，中间张量用完即可释放，显存和时间都会下降。
a.en: Reverse mode keeps the intermediate values of the forward pass. Inference runs no backward pass, so they serve no purpose. Under `no_grad()` PyTorch builds no graph and intermediate tensors are freed as soon as they are used, which lowers both memory and time.

q.zh: 为什么训练比推理占用的显存多得多？
q.en: Why does training need so much more memory than inference?

a.zh: 主要有三部分。每一层的激活都要保留到反向传播结束。每个参数还要存一份同样大小的梯度。Adam 这类优化器为每个参数再存两份统计量。推理只需要权重和当前层的激活。
a.en: There are three main parts. The activations of every layer are kept until the backward pass ends. Each parameter stores a gradient of the same size. Optimizers such as Adam store two more statistics per parameter. Inference only needs the weights and the activations of the current layer.

q.zh: 为什么深度学习用反向模式，而不是更直观的前向模式？
q.en: Why does deep learning use reverse mode and not the more intuitive forward mode?

a.zh: 前向模式每次传播只能得到一个参数方向上的导数，十亿个参数就要传播十亿次。反向模式每次得到一个输出对全部参数的导数，而损失只有一个数，所以一次就够。见上面第三个推导。
a.en: Forward mode yields the derivative along one parameter direction per pass, so a billion parameters would need a billion passes. Reverse mode yields the derivative of one output with respect to all parameters, and the loss is a single number, so one pass is enough. See the third derivation above.

why.zh: 模型有上亿个参数，每个参数该往哪个方向调，全靠反向传播算出来。不理解它，训练就是一个黑箱，梯度消失、显存不足这类问题也无从排查。
why.en: A model has hundreds of millions of parameters, and backpropagation works out the direction in which each one should move. Without understanding it, training is a black box, and problems such as vanishing gradients or running out of memory cannot be diagnosed.

plain.zh: 设想一条流水线出了次品，要查清每个工位各负多少责任。从成品出发往回走，每个工位只需要回答一个问题，即我的输出变动一点，下一道工序的结果会变动多少，再把下游传来的责任乘上这个数，继续往上游传。反向传播就是这样逐站分摊责任。一个工位如果同时给两条线供货，两边传回来的责任相加。
plain.en: Imagine an assembly line that has produced a faulty item, and the share of blame of every station has to be found. Walking back from the finished item, every station answers one question, namely how much the result of the next step changes when my output changes a little, multiplies the blame handed back from downstream by that number and passes it further upstream. Backpropagation distributes blame station by station in this way. A station that supplies two lines adds up the blame returned from both.

title.zh: 交叉熵、最大似然与困惑度

summary.zh: 三个名字，同一件事。弄清它们之间只差一个负号、一个平均和一个指数。
summary.en: Three names for one thing. They differ by a minus sign, an average and an exponential.

goals.zh: 能从最大似然推出交叉熵损失
goals.en: Derive the cross-entropy loss from maximum likelihood

goals.zh: 能解释困惑度的含义并手算
goals.en: Explain perplexity and compute it by hand

goals.zh: 能说出困惑度在比较模型时的限制
goals.en: State the limits of perplexity when comparing models

explain.zh: 语言模型在每个位置给出词表上的一个概率分布，表示它认为下一个 token 是什么。训练文本告诉我们真正的下一个 token。打分的办法很直接，看模型给正确 token 分了多少概率 $p$，损失取 $-\log p$。$p$ 接近 1 时损失接近 0，$p$ 很小时损失很大。
explain.en: At every position a language model outputs a probability distribution over the vocabulary, its belief about the next token. The training text tells us the true next token. Scoring is direct. Look at the probability $p$ the model gave to the correct token and take $-\log p$ as the loss. When $p$ is near 1 the loss is near 0, and when $p$ is small the loss is large.

explain.zh: 这个损失有三个常见的名字。**最大似然**说的是调整参数让训练数据出现的概率尽量大。**交叉熵**是把这个概率取对数、取负号、再按 token 取平均后的结果。**困惑度**是对交叉熵取指数，让数字更容易解读。三者优化的是同一个目标。
explain.en: This loss goes by three common names. **Maximum likelihood** means adjusting the parameters so the training data becomes as probable as possible. **Cross-entropy** is what remains after taking the log of that probability, negating it and averaging over tokens. **Perplexity** exponentiates the cross-entropy so the number is easier to read. All three optimize the same objective.

explain.zh: 困惑度可以这样理解。困惑度为 10，相当于模型每一步都在 10 个同样可能的候选里随机挑一个。一个什么都没学到的模型对词表里每个 token 一视同仁，困惑度等于词表大小 $V$，对应的损失是 $\ln V$。这给了一个很实用的检查，刚初始化的 GPT-2 损失应当在 $\ln 50257 \approx 10.82$ 附近。
explain.en: Perplexity can be read this way. A perplexity of 10 means the model is, at each step, as uncertain as if it were choosing uniformly among 10 candidates. A model that has learned nothing treats every token alike, so its perplexity equals the vocabulary size $V$ and its loss is $\ln V$. This gives a practical sanity check. A freshly initialized GPT-2 should start near $\ln 50257 \approx 10.82$.

explain.zh: 困惑度是按 token 计算的，所以它依赖分词器，也依赖评测时给了多少上下文。Hugging Face 文档用 GPT-2 large 在 WikiText-2 上做过对比，窗口不重叠时困惑度约为 19.44，改用步幅 512 的滑动窗口后约为 16.44。同一个模型、同一份数据，只是上下文给法不同。
explain.en: Perplexity is computed per token, so it depends on the tokenizer and on how much context is given during evaluation. The Hugging Face documentation compares both settings for GPT-2 large on WikiText-2. The result is about 19.44 with non-overlapping windows and about 16.44 with a sliding window of stride 512. Same model, same data, only the context differs.

caption.zh: 损失 −ln p 随正确 token 的概率 p 变化。给正确答案 90% 的概率只损失 0.11，给 1% 则损失 4.6。曲线在 p 接近 0 时很陡，模型自信地答错时受到的惩罚最重。
caption.en: The loss −ln p against the probability p of the correct token. Giving the right answer 90% costs 0.11, giving it 1% costs 4.6. The curve is steep near p = 0, so confident mistakes are punished most.

source.text: Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville, Deep Learning, §5.5

note.zh: 最大似然。假设 $N$ 个样本独立，找让它们同时出现的概率最大的参数。
note.en: Maximum likelihood. Assume the $N$ samples are independent and find the parameters that make them jointly most probable.

note.zh: 取对数。$\log$ 单调递增，不改变最大值的位置，同时把连乘变成求和，避免很多小概率相乘后下溢。
note.en: Take the log. $\log$ is increasing, so the maximizer stays the same, and the product becomes a sum, which avoids underflow from multiplying many small probabilities.

note.zh: 加负号把最大化变成最小化，除以 $N$ 让损失不随数据量变化。这就是平均负对数似然 (NLL)。
note.en: Negate to turn the maximization into a minimization and divide by $N$ so the loss does not grow with the dataset. This is the average negative log-likelihood (NLL).

note.zh: 样本平均趋近期望。这个期望正是交叉熵 $H(p,q) = -\sum_x p(x)\log q(x)$ 的定义。
note.en: The sample average approaches an expectation. That expectation is the definition of cross-entropy, $H(p,q) = -\sum_x p(x)\log q(x)$.

note.zh: 在 $-\sum p\log q$ 里加一项再减一项 $\sum p\log p$ 即得。$H(p_{\text{data}})$ 与 $\theta$ 无关，所以最小化交叉熵、最小化 KL 散度和最大似然得到同一组参数。
note.en: Add and subtract $\sum p\log p$ inside $-\sum p\log q$. $H(p_{\text{data}})$ does not depend on $\theta$, so minimizing cross-entropy, minimizing KL divergence and maximum likelihood all give the same parameters.

title.zh: 语言模型的逐 token 损失
title.en: The per-token loss of a language model

note.zh: 概率的链式法则，是恒等式，没有做任何近似。自回归模型正是按这个分解来建模的。
note.en: The chain rule of probability, an identity with no approximation. Autoregressive models are built on this factorization.

note.zh: 取负对数后，整句的损失是每个位置损失的和。
note.en: After the negative log, the loss of the sequence is the sum of the per-position losses.

note.zh: 每个位置的目标是 one-hot 向量，交叉熵的求和里只剩正确 token 那一项。所以 `F.cross_entropy` 的标签只需要传类别下标。
note.en: The target at each position is one-hot, so only the correct token's term survives in the sum. This is why `F.cross_entropy` takes a class index as the label.

note.zh: 按 token 取平均，就是训练日志里看到的 loss，单位是 nat。
note.en: Average over tokens. This is the loss shown in training logs, measured in nats.

source.text: Jurafsky & Martin, Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft), ch. 3

note.zh: 定义。对平均负对数似然取指数。
note.en: The definition. Exponentiate the average negative log-likelihood.

note.zh: 把指数和求和交换，得到正确 token 概率的几何平均的倒数。
note.en: Move the exponential inside the sum. The result is the reciprocal of the geometric mean of the correct-token probabilities.

note.zh: 均匀分布的困惑度等于词表大小。困惑度可以理解为等效的候选个数。
note.en: A uniform distribution has perplexity equal to the vocabulary size. Perplexity can be read as an effective number of candidates.

note.zh: 换成以 2 为底的对数就是每个 token 的比特数。它和压缩直接对应，损失越低，文本可以被压得越短。
note.en: Switching to base 2 gives bits per token. This links directly to compression. The lower the loss, the shorter the text can be encoded.

q.zh: 为什么刚初始化的模型 loss 大约是 ln V？
q.en: Why does a freshly initialized model start with a loss near ln V?

a.zh: 初始化良好的模型输出的 logits 都接近 0，softmax 之后接近均匀分布，每个 token 的概率约为 $1/V$，损失就是 $\ln V$。如果第一步的 loss 远高于这个值，通常说明初始化或数据管线有问题，这是调试训练时值得先看的数字。
a.en: A well-initialized model outputs logits near 0, so softmax gives a nearly uniform distribution with probability about $1/V$ per token and a loss of $\ln V$. If the first loss is far above this, the initialization or the data pipeline is usually at fault. It is a good first number to check when debugging training.

q.zh: 为什么语言模型用交叉熵，而不用准确率或均方误差？
q.en: Why cross-entropy and not accuracy or mean squared error?

a.zh: 准确率只看排第一的 token 对不对，对参数几乎处处导数为零，无法用梯度下降优化，也丢掉了概率信息。均方误差可导，但模型自信地答错时 softmax 已经饱和，梯度里带着 $p(1-p)$ 这样的因子，会变得很小。交叉熵是最大似然的直接结果，它对 logits 的梯度是 $p - y$（见 1.3），错得越多梯度越大。
a.en: Accuracy only checks whether the top token is right. Its derivative with respect to the parameters is zero almost everywhere, so gradient descent cannot optimize it, and it throws away the probabilities. Squared error is differentiable, but when the model is confidently wrong the softmax is saturated and the gradient carries a factor like $p(1-p)$ that becomes tiny. Cross-entropy follows directly from maximum likelihood, and its gradient with respect to the logits is $p - y$ (see 1.3), which grows with the size of the mistake.

q.zh: 为什么两个模型的困惑度不能直接比较？
q.en: Why can the perplexities of two models not be compared directly?

a.zh: 困惑度是按 token 平均的。分词器不同，同一段文本被切成的 token 数就不同，每个 token 的难度也不同。切得粗的分词器 token 更少，但每一步要猜的内容更多。比较不同词表的模型时，通常换算成每字符或每字节的比特数。此外上下文长度和滑动窗口的步幅也会影响结果，报告困惑度时应一并说明。
a.en: Perplexity is averaged per token. With different tokenizers the same text splits into a different number of tokens, each with a different difficulty. A coarser tokenizer has fewer tokens but more to guess at each step. Models with different vocabularies are usually compared in bits per character or per byte. Context length and the stride of the sliding window also change the result and should be reported together with the number.

q.zh: 困惑度低就说明模型好用吗？
q.en: Does low perplexity mean a model is good to use?

a.zh: 不一定。困惑度衡量的是模型对某个文本分布拟合得多好，它不直接衡量是否听从指令、事实是否正确或回答是否有用。它适合用来跟踪训练过程和比较同一词表下的模型，面向任务的评估方法放在阶段 8。
a.en: Not necessarily. Perplexity measures how well a model fits a text distribution. It does not directly measure whether instructions are followed, whether facts are right or whether answers are useful. It suits tracking training and comparing models that share a vocabulary. Task-oriented evaluation is covered in stage 8.

q.zh: 为什么模型会把错误的内容说得很流畅？
q.en: Why can a model state something wrong so fluently?

a.zh: 训练目标奖励的是给训练文本里实际出现的下一个 token 更高的概率，也就是续写得像真实文本。目标函数里没有单独衡量陈述是否为真的一项。这是幻觉的成因之一，完整的讨论在 8.2。
a.en: The training objective rewards assigning high probability to the token that actually came next in the training text, that is, continuing in a way that resembles real text. No term in the objective separately measures whether a statement is true. This is one source of hallucination, and 8.2 discusses it in full.

why.zh: 训练需要一个数来衡量预测的好坏，这个数就是损失。语言模型的损失为什么是交叉熵，决定了模型最终学到的是什么，也是理解幻觉等现象的起点。
why.en: Training needs one number that measures how good a prediction is, the loss. Why the loss of a language model is cross-entropy determines what the model ends up learning, and it is the starting point for understanding phenomena such as hallucination.

plain.zh: 把模型想成一位每天预报降水概率的预报员。今天下了雨，如果他昨天报的是 90%，几乎不扣分，报的是 10% 就要扣很多分，扣分的规则是对实际发生的事所报概率取负对数。困惑度是把平均扣分换成一个更直观的数。困惑度为 10，意思是他平均每次都像在 10 个同样可能的选项里蒙一个。
plain.en: Think of the model as a forecaster who announces a probability of rain every day. If it rains today and yesterday's forecast was 90%, almost nothing is deducted, and if it was 10% a great deal is deducted, the rule being the negative logarithm of the probability given to what actually happened. Perplexity turns the average deduction into a more intuitive number. A perplexity of 10 means that on average the forecaster is in effect guessing among 10 equally likely options.

summary.zh: 推出 p − y 这个结果，并写一个不会溢出的 softmax。
summary.en: Derive the p − y result and write a softmax that does not overflow.

goals.zh: 能推导 softmax 的雅可比矩阵和交叉熵对 logits 的梯度
goals.en: Derive the softmax Jacobian and the gradient of cross-entropy with respect to the logits

goals.zh: 能解释并实现 log-sum-exp 技巧
goals.en: Explain and implement the log-sum-exp trick

goals.zh: 能手写一层线性层加交叉熵的反向传播
goals.en: Backpropagate through a linear layer plus cross-entropy by hand

explain.zh: 网络最后一层给词表里每个 token 打一个分，叫 logit，可以是任意实数。softmax 把这些分数变成概率，做法是先取指数让它们都变成正数，再除以总和让它们加起来等于 1。
explain.en: The last layer of the network assigns every token in the vocabulary a score called a logit, which can be any real number. Softmax turns the scores into probabilities by exponentiating them so they are positive and dividing by the sum so they add up to 1.

explain.zh: 指数有两个值得记住的后果。其一，起作用的是 logit 之间的**差**，两个 token 的 logit 差 1，概率就差 $e \approx 2.72$ 倍。其二，给所有 logit 加同一个常数，结果不变。
explain.en: The exponential has two consequences worth remembering. First, what matters is the **difference** between logits. A gap of 1 means a probability ratio of $e \approx 2.72$. Second, adding the same constant to every logit changes nothing.

explain.zh: softmax 接上交叉熵之后，损失对 logits 的梯度非常简单，就是 $p - y$，即预测概率减去真实标签。正确 token 的概率不到 1，它的 logit 会被往上推。其余 token 的概率大于 0，它们的 logit 会被往下压，压的力度正比于模型错给它们的概率。
explain.en: With cross-entropy on top of softmax, the gradient of the loss with respect to the logits is very simple. It is $p - y$, predicted probability minus true label. The correct token has probability below 1, so its logit is pushed up. Every other token has probability above 0, so its logit is pushed down, in proportion to the probability wrongly given to it.

explain.zh: 实现上有一个坑。先算 softmax 再取 log，遇到大的 logit 时 $e^{z}$ 会溢出成 inf，遇到很负的 logit 时概率下溢成 0，再取 log 得到 -inf。解决办法是始终在对数空间里计算，用 log-sum-exp 技巧。PyTorch 的 `F.cross_entropy` 接收 logits 而不是概率，原因就在这里。
explain.en: There is a trap in the implementation. Computing softmax and then the log overflows to inf when a logit is large, and underflows to 0 followed by -inf when a logit is very negative. The fix is to stay in log space and use the log-sum-exp trick. This is why `F.cross_entropy` in PyTorch takes logits and not probabilities.

caption.zh: 三个候选 token 的 logits 经过 softmax 变成概率，再与 one-hot 标签相减得到梯度。正确 token 的梯度为负，梯度下降会把它的 logit 往上推。
caption.en: Logits of three candidate tokens become probabilities through softmax. Subtracting the one-hot label gives the gradient. The correct token has a negative gradient, so gradient descent pushes its logit up.

note.zh: 定义。注意每个 $p_i$ 都通过分母 $S$ 依赖于所有的 $z_j$。
note.en: The definition. Note that every $p_i$ depends on all $z_j$ through the denominator $S$.

steps.tex: i = j:\quad \frac{\partial p_i}{\partial z_i} = \frac{e^{z_i} S - e^{z_i} e^{z_i}}{S^2} = p_i\,(1 - p_i)

note.zh: 商的求导法则。分子和分母都含 $z_i$。
note.en: The quotient rule. Both numerator and denominator contain $z_i$.

steps.tex: i \neq j:\quad \frac{\partial p_i}{\partial z_j} = \frac{0\cdot S - e^{z_i} e^{z_j}}{S^2} = -\,p_i\,p_j

note.zh: 分子不含 $z_j$，只有分母起作用。抬高别的 token 的 logit 会压低 $p_i$。
note.en: The numerator does not contain $z_j$, so only the denominator contributes. Raising another token's logit lowers $p_i$.

steps.tex: \frac{\partial p_i}{\partial z_j} = p_i\,(\delta_{ij} - p_j) \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad J = \mathrm{diag}(p) - p\,p^{\top}

note.zh: 用 $\delta_{ij}$（$i=j$ 时为 1，否则为 0）把两种情况合并。当某个 $p_i$ 接近 1 时，$J$ 的所有元素都接近 0，这就是 softmax 饱和。
note.en: Merge both cases with $\delta_{ij}$ (1 when $i=j$, else 0). When some $p_i$ approaches 1, every entry of $J$ approaches 0. This is softmax saturation.

title.zh: 交叉熵对 logits 的梯度
title.en: The gradient of cross-entropy with respect to the logits

note.zh: 单个位置的交叉熵，$y$ 是 one-hot 标签。
note.en: Cross-entropy at one position, with one-hot label $y$.

note.zh: 链式法则。$z_j$ 影响所有的 $p_k$，所以要对 $k$ 求和。
note.en: The chain rule. $z_j$ affects every $p_k$, hence the sum over $k$.

note.zh: 代入雅可比矩阵，$p_k$ 约掉。
note.en: Substitute the Jacobian. The $p_k$ cancels.

note.zh: 用到 $\sum_k y_k = 1$。这个结果对任何和为 1 的目标分布都成立，不限于 one-hot，所以 label smoothing 和知识蒸馏的梯度形式相同。
note.en: Uses $\sum_k y_k = 1$. The result holds for any target distribution that sums to 1, not only one-hot, so label smoothing and distillation have the same gradient form.

note.zh: 更快的路线。先把 $\log p_c$ 展开再求导，一步得到同样的结果。面试时推荐写这一种。
note.en: A faster route. Expand $\log p_c$ first and differentiate. One step gives the same result, and it is the version to write in an interview.

note.zh: 对 softmax 取对数。难点在第二项，$z_k = 1000$ 时 $e^{1000}$ 已经超出浮点数范围。
note.en: Take the log of softmax. The hard part is the second term. With $z_k = 1000$, $e^{1000}$ already exceeds the floating-point range.

steps.tex: \log\sum_k e^{z_k} = \log\Big(e^{m}\sum_k e^{z_k - m}\Big) = m + \log\sum_k e^{z_k - m},\qquad m = \max_k z_k

note.zh: 提出最大的那一项。这是恒等变形，结果不变。
note.en: Factor out the largest term. This is an identity, so the value is unchanged.

steps.tex: z_k - m \le 0 \;\Rightarrow\; 0 < e^{z_k - m} \le 1,\qquad \sum_k e^{z_k - m} \ge 1

note.zh: 指数的输入都不大于 0，不会上溢。求和里至少有一项等于 1，所以对数的输入不小于 1，不会出现 $\log 0$。
note.en: Every exponent is at most 0, so nothing overflows. At least one term of the sum equals 1, so the argument of the log is at least 1 and $\log 0$ cannot occur.

source.text: Hinton, Vinyals, Dean, Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network, arXiv:1503.02531

note.zh: 先把 logits 除以温度 $T$ 再做 softmax。
note.en: Divide the logits by the temperature $T$ before softmax.

note.zh: 令 $u = z/T$，对 $u$ 的梯度仍是 $p - y$，再乘上 $\partial u_j/\partial z_j = 1/T$。
note.en: Let $u = z/T$. The gradient with respect to $u$ is still $p - y$, multiplied by $\partial u_j/\partial z_j = 1/T$.

steps.tex: T \to 0:\ p \to \text{one-hot at } \arg\max z \qquad\qquad T \to \infty:\ p \to \text{uniform}

note.zh: 温度低，差距被放大，分布变尖。温度高，差距被缩小，分布变平。采样时的 temperature 参数就是这个 $T$，在 5.1 展开。
note.en: A low temperature amplifies the gaps and sharpens the distribution. A high temperature shrinks the gaps and flattens it. The temperature parameter in sampling is this $T$, covered in 5.1.

q.zh: 为什么 F.cross_entropy 要传 logits，而不是先做 softmax 再传概率？
q.en: Why does F.cross_entropy take logits and not probabilities after softmax?

a.zh: 有两个原因。数值上，先 softmax 再取 log 在 logit 很大或很小时会得到 inf 或 -inf，在对数空间里用 log-sum-exp 直接计算则是稳定的。另外，如果传进去的已经是概率，函数会把它当作 logits 再做一次 softmax，代码不会报错，但训练效果会明显变差，这是一个常见的隐蔽错误。
a.en: There are two reasons. Numerically, softmax followed by log gives inf or -inf when logits are large or small, while computing in log space with log-sum-exp is stable. Also, if probabilities are passed in, the function treats them as logits and applies softmax again. The code raises no error but training gets clearly worse, a common silent bug.

q.zh: 为什么归一化要用指数，而不是直接除以总和？
q.en: Why normalize with an exponential and not by dividing by the sum?

a.zh: logits 可以是负数，直接除以总和得不到合法的概率。取指数保证结果为正，并且让模型只需要学习 token 之间的相对分数。它与交叉熵配合时梯度恰好是 $p - y$，形式简单且不会因为饱和而消失。
a.en: Logits can be negative, so dividing by their sum does not give valid probabilities. Exponentiating guarantees positive values and means the model only has to learn relative scores between tokens. Paired with cross-entropy the gradient is exactly $p - y$, which is simple and does not vanish through saturation.

q.zh: 为什么把 temperature 调高，输出会更随机？
q.en: Why does a higher temperature make outputs more random?

a.zh: 温度 $T$ 把 logits 之间的差距缩小为原来的 $1/T$。两个 token 的概率比从 $e^{\Delta}$ 变成 $e^{\Delta/T}$，$T$ 越大，原本落后的 token 被采到的机会越多。$T$ 趋近 0 时分布集中到 logit 最大的 token 上，等价于贪心解码。
a.en: Temperature $T$ shrinks the gaps between logits by a factor of $1/T$. The probability ratio of two tokens changes from $e^{\Delta}$ to $e^{\Delta/T}$, so with a larger $T$ the trailing tokens are sampled more often. As $T$ approaches 0 the distribution concentrates on the token with the largest logit, which is greedy decoding.

q.zh: softmax 输出的概率能直接当作模型的置信度吗？
q.en: Can the softmax probability be read as the model's confidence?

a.zh: 需要谨慎。softmax 只是把相对分数归一化，无论模型是否真的知道答案，输出的概率加起来都等于 1。概率与实际正确率是否一致属于校准问题，需要单独测量，在 8.2 讨论。
a.en: With caution. Softmax only normalizes relative scores, and the probabilities sum to 1 whether or not the model actually knows the answer. Whether probabilities match real accuracy is a question of calibration, which has to be measured separately and is discussed in 8.2.

q.zh: 什么是 softmax 饱和，它为什么重要？
q.en: What is softmax saturation and why does it matter?

a.zh: 当某个 logit 远大于其他 logit 时，对应的概率接近 1，雅可比矩阵 $\mathrm{diag}(p) - pp^{\top}$ 的元素全部接近 0，梯度几乎传不回去。注意力里也有一个 softmax，点积过大时会出现同样的问题，这是注意力要除以 $\sqrt{d_k}$ 的原因，在 2.1 推导。
a.en: When one logit is far larger than the rest, its probability approaches 1 and every entry of the Jacobian $\mathrm{diag}(p) - pp^{\top}$ approaches 0, so almost no gradient flows back. Attention also contains a softmax, and the same problem appears when dot products grow too large. This is the reason attention divides by $\sqrt{d_k}$, derived in 2.1.

why.zh: softmax 出现在模型的两个关键位置，即输出端把 logits 变成概率，以及注意力内部把分数变成权重。它的梯度性质直接解释了后面多个设计，比如注意力为什么要除以 √d_k。
why.en: Softmax appears at two key places in a model, at the output where logits become probabilities and inside attention where scores become weights. The behaviour of its gradient directly explains several later designs, such as why attention divides by √d_k.

plain.zh: softmax 像按得票分蛋糕，只是先把票数做了指数放大，所以领先一点的人会多分很多，而所有份额加起来正好是一整块。梯度 $p - y$ 可以这样记。正确答案本该拿到整块蛋糕，实际只拿到 $p$，差多少就往上补多少。其余选项多拿了多少，就被扣回多少。
plain.en: Softmax is like dividing a cake by votes, except that the votes are first amplified exponentially, so a small lead earns a much larger slice, and all slices together make exactly one cake. The gradient $p - y$ can be remembered as follows. The correct answer should have received the whole cake and received only $p$, so it is topped up by the shortfall. Whatever the other options received in excess is taken back from them.

summary.zh: 位置之间交换信息的唯一途径。实现它，并从方差推出为什么要除以 √d_k。
summary.en: The only way positions exchange information. Implement it and derive from the variance why it divides by √d_k.

why.zh: 嵌入之后，每个位置的向量只包含它自己那个 token 的信息。要预测 `The capital of France is` 的下一个 token，` is` 这个位置需要知道前面出现过 ` France` 和 ` capital`。注意力就是让一个位置去读取其他位置信息的机制，也是 Transformer 中各位置之间唯一的信息通道。没有它，模型对每个 token 的处理都与上下文无关。
why.en: After embedding, the vector at each position holds only the information of its own token. To predict the token after `The capital of France is`, the position of ` is` has to know that ` France` and ` capital` came before. Attention is the mechanism by which one position reads information from others, and it is the only channel between positions in a Transformer. Without it, every token would be processed with no regard to context.

goals.zh: 能写出注意力的公式并说明每个张量的形状
goals.en: Write the attention formula and state the shape of every tensor

goals.zh: 能从方差的角度推导除以 √d_k 的理由
goals.en: Derive the reason for dividing by √d_k from the variance

goals.zh: 能解释不缩放时会发生什么
goals.en: Explain what happens without the scaling

explain.zh: 可以把注意力想成一次查资料。当前位置带着一个问题，称为 **query**。每个位置都挂着一个标签，说明自己能提供什么，称为 **key**，同时还准备了一份真正要交出去的内容，称为 **value**。当前位置拿自己的 query 和所有位置的 key 逐个比对，匹配程度高的，就多取一些它的 value。
explain.en: Attention can be pictured as looking something up. The current position carries a question, called the **query**. Every position has a label that says what it can offer, called the **key**, and also a piece of content it will actually hand over, called the **value**. The current position compares its query with the key of every position and takes more of the value where the match is better.

explain.zh: “比对”用的是**点积**。两个向量方向越一致，点积越大。query 与每个 key 做点积，得到一组分数。分数经过 softmax 变成一组和为 1 的权重，称为注意力权重。最后把所有位置的 value 按这组权重加权平均，就是当前位置这一层注意力的输出。
explain.en: The comparison is a **dot product**. The more two vectors point the same way, the larger their dot product. The dot products of the query with every key give a set of scores. Softmax turns the scores into weights that sum to 1, the attention weights. The values of all positions are then averaged with these weights, and the result is the output of this attention layer at the current position.

explain.zh: query、key、value 都由同一个输入向量乘以三个不同的矩阵得到，这三个矩阵是要学习的参数。因为三者都来自同一段序列，所以叫**自注意力** (self-attention)。所有位置的计算可以写成矩阵乘法一次完成，这是 Transformer 能够高效并行的原因。
explain.en: Query, key and value are all obtained from the same input vector by multiplying with three different matrices, which are learned parameters. Because all three come from the same sequence, this is called **self-attention**. The computation for all positions can be written as matrix multiplications and done at once, which is why a Transformer parallelizes so well.

explain.zh: 公式里还有一个除以 $\sqrt{d_k}$ 的操作，$d_k$ 是 key 向量的维度。原因是点积的大小会随维度增长。维度越高，分数的波动越大，softmax 之后的权重几乎全部落在一个位置上，这种状态称为**饱和**。饱和的 softmax 梯度接近 0（见 1.3），训练会很困难。除以 $\sqrt{d_k}$ 正好把分数的波动拉回到与维度无关的水平。下面的第二个推导给出完整的计算，练习 2 用实验验证。
explain.en: The formula also divides by $\sqrt{d_k}$, where $d_k$ is the dimension of the key vectors. The reason is that dot products grow with the dimension. The higher the dimension, the more the scores fluctuate, and after softmax almost all the weight falls on a single position, a state called **saturation**. A saturated softmax has gradients near 0 (see 1.3), which makes training hard. Dividing by $\sqrt{d_k}$ brings the fluctuation of the scores back to a level that does not depend on the dimension. The second derivation below gives the full calculation and exercise 2 checks it by experiment.

caption.zh: 位置 ` is` 的一次注意力计算，数值为示意。query 与五个 key 的点积经缩放后得到分数，softmax 把分数变成权重，输出是五个 value 的加权平均。
caption.en: One attention computation at the position of ` is`, with illustrative numbers. The dot products of the query with five keys are scaled into scores, softmax turns the scores into weights, and the output is the weighted average of the five values.

source.text: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762, §3.2.1

steps.tex: Q = X W_Q,\qquad K = X W_K,\qquad V = X W_V

note.zh: $X$ 是输入，形状 $(T, d)$，每行是一个位置的向量。三个矩阵把它投影成 query、key、value。$Q$ 和 $K$ 的形状是 $(T, d_k)$，$V$ 是 $(T, d_v)$。
note.en: $X$ is the input of shape $(T, d)$, one row per position. Three matrices project it into queries, keys and values. $Q$ and $K$ have shape $(T, d_k)$ and $V$ has $(T, d_v)$.

note.zh: 分数矩阵，形状 $(T, T)$。第 $i$ 行第 $j$ 列是位置 $i$ 的 query 与位置 $j$ 的 key 的点积，表示 $i$ 有多想读取 $j$。
note.en: The score matrix of shape $(T, T)$. Entry $(i, j)$ is the dot product of the query at position $i$ with the key at position $j$, how much $i$ wants to read from $j$.

note.zh: 对每一行做 softmax，得到注意力权重。每一行是当前位置在所有位置上的一个分配。
note.en: Softmax over each row gives the attention weights. Each row is how the current position distributes its attention over all positions.

steps.tex: \mathrm{Attention}(Q, K, V) = A\,V,\qquad o_i = \sum_j A_{ij}\, v_j

note.zh: 输出的形状是 $(T, d_v)$。每个位置的输出是所有 value 的加权平均。
note.en: The output has shape $(T, d_v)$. The output at each position is a weighted average of all values.

source.text: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762, §3.2.1 footnote 4

steps.tex: q \cdot k = \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} q_m k_m,\qquad q_m,\ k_m \ \text{independent},\ \ \mathbb{E} = 0,\ \ \mathrm{Var} = 1

note.zh: 假设 query 和 key 的各个分量相互独立，均值为 0，方差为 1。这是对初始化附近状态的简化描述。
note.en: Assume the components of query and key are independent with mean 0 and variance 1. This is a simplified description of the state near initialization.

note.zh: 独立变量乘积的期望等于期望的乘积。
note.en: The expectation of a product of independent variables is the product of the expectations.

note.zh: 均值为 0 时方差等于平方的期望。$\mathbb{E}[q_m^2] = \mathrm{Var}(q_m) = 1$。
note.en: With mean 0 the variance equals the expectation of the square, and $\mathbb{E}[q_m^2] = \mathrm{Var}(q_m) = 1$.

note.zh: 各项相互独立，和的方差等于方差的和。点积的标准差是 $\sqrt{d_k}$，会随维度增大。GPT-2 small 每个头的 $d_k = 64$，标准差就是 8。
note.en: The terms are independent, so the variance of the sum is the sum of the variances. The standard deviation of the dot product is $\sqrt{d_k}$ and grows with the dimension. Each head of GPT-2 small has $d_k = 64$, giving a standard deviation of 8.

note.zh: 除以 $\sqrt{d_k}$ 后方差回到 1，不再依赖维度。除以 $d_k$ 则会使方差变成 $1/d_k$，分数几乎全部相同，注意力退化成简单平均。
note.en: After dividing by $\sqrt{d_k}$ the variance returns to 1 and no longer depends on the dimension. Dividing by $d_k$ would make it $1/d_k$, the scores would be almost identical and attention would degrade into a plain average.

steps.tex: \frac{\partial A_{ij}}{\partial S_{il}} = A_{ij}\,(\delta_{jl} - A_{il}) \;\longrightarrow\; 0 \quad \text{when one } A_{ij} \to 1

note.zh: 这是 1.3 推出的 softmax 雅可比矩阵。分数波动大时，某个权重接近 1，所有偏导数都接近 0，梯度无法通过注意力传回去。缩放的目的就是避免这种饱和。
note.en: This is the softmax Jacobian derived in 1.3. When the scores fluctuate strongly, one weight approaches 1 and all partial derivatives approach 0, so no gradient passes back through attention. The scaling exists to avoid this saturation.

q.zh: 为什么除以 √d_k，而不是 d_k 或者别的数？
q.en: Why divide by √d_k and not by d_k or something else?

a.zh: 因为点积的方差是 $d_k$，标准差是 $\sqrt{d_k}$。除以标准差正好让分数的方差变成 1，与维度无关。除以 $d_k$ 会缩得过头，分数之间几乎没有差别，模型很难把注意力集中到某个位置。不缩放则分数差距过大，softmax 饱和，梯度消失。
a.en: Because the variance of the dot product is $d_k$ and its standard deviation is $\sqrt{d_k}$. Dividing by the standard deviation makes the variance of the scores exactly 1, whatever the dimension. Dividing by $d_k$ shrinks too far, the scores barely differ and the model can hardly focus on a position. Without any scaling the gaps are too large, softmax saturates and the gradient vanishes.

q.zh: 为什么需要 Q、K、V 三个不同的矩阵？
q.en: Why are three different matrices for Q, K and V needed?

a.zh: 因为“我在找什么”“我能提供什么”“我实际交出什么”是三件不同的事。如果 query 和 key 用同一个矩阵，分数矩阵是对称的，位置 $i$ 关注 $j$ 的程度就等于 $j$ 关注 $i$ 的程度，而语言中的依赖关系通常是不对称的。value 与 key 分开，则让“凭什么被选中”和“被选中后传递什么”可以各自学习。
a.en: Because what a position is looking for, what it can offer and what it actually hands over are three different things. If query and key shared one matrix the score matrix would be symmetric, so position $i$ would attend to $j$ exactly as much as $j$ to $i$, while dependencies in language are usually asymmetric. Separating value from key lets the reason for being chosen and the content passed on be learned independently.

q.zh: 为什么用点积来衡量相关性？
q.en: Why is relevance measured with a dot product?

a.zh: 点积可以对所有位置对用一次矩阵乘法算完，在 GPU 上非常快。原论文比较过另一种做法，即用一个小网络来算分数的加性注意力，两者理论复杂度相近，但点积在实践中更快也更省空间。
a.en: The dot product for all pairs of positions is a single matrix multiplication, which is very fast on a GPU. The original paper compares it with additive attention, where a small network computes the score. The two have similar theoretical complexity, but the dot product is faster and more space-efficient in practice.

q.zh: 注意力权重大，就说明模型“依据”了那个 token 吗？
q.en: Does a large attention weight mean the model relied on that token?

a.zh: 不能直接这样推断。权重只说明这一层这个头从哪里取了信息，取来的信息在后面的层里是否真正影响了输出，需要另外验证。把注意力权重当作解释使用时需要谨慎，更可靠的做法是做干预实验，在 9.1 和 9.3 讨论。
a.en: That cannot be inferred directly. The weight only says where this head in this layer took information from. Whether that information really affected the output in later layers has to be verified separately. Caution is needed when attention weights are used as explanations, and intervention experiments are more reliable, as 9.1 and 9.3 discuss.

q.zh: 为什么输入越长，计算越贵？
q.en: Why does a longer input cost more?

a.zh: 分数矩阵的形状是 $(T, T)$，每个位置都要和所有位置比对一次。序列长度翻倍，这个矩阵就变成四倍。完整的代价分析在 2.6。
a.en: The score matrix has shape $(T, T)$ because every position is compared with every position. Doubling the sequence length quadruples this matrix. The full cost analysis is in 2.6.

plain.zh: 像在图书馆查资料。心里有一个问题（query），每本书的书脊上有标签（key），书里的内容是 value。拿问题去对照所有的标签，越对得上的书读得越多，最后把读到的内容按比例合在一起。在句子“小猫没有过马路，因为它太累了”里，“它”这个位置发出的问题大致是“我指的是谁”，“小猫”的标签最匹配，于是“它”的表示里就混入了“小猫”的信息。
plain.en: It is like looking things up in a library. There is a question in mind (the query), every book carries a label on its spine (the key), and the content of the book is the value. The question is compared with all labels, the better a label matches the more of that book is read, and what was read is blended in proportion. In the sentence the cat did not cross the road because it was too tired, the position of it sends out roughly the question of whom it refers to, the label of cat matches best, and information about the cat is mixed into the representation of it.

summary.zh: 把一次注意力拆成并行的若干个头。实现它，并亲手复现 GPT-2 的注意力层。
summary.en: Split one attention into several parallel heads. Implement it and reproduce GPT-2's attention layer yourself.

why.zh: 一组注意力权重只能表达一种关注方式。但理解一句话往往同时需要几种关系，比如代词指向谁、动词的主语是谁、当前在句子的什么位置。多头注意力让同一层里并行存在多组权重，各自关注不同的东西。它几乎不增加参数和计算量，所以所有主流模型都采用。
why.en: One set of attention weights can express only one way of attending. Understanding a sentence often needs several relations at once, such as what a pronoun refers to, which word is the subject of a verb, and where in the sentence the current position is. Multi-head attention lets several sets of weights exist in parallel in the same layer, each attending to something different. It adds almost no parameters or computation, so every mainstream model uses it.

goals.zh: 能说清多头注意力中每一步的张量形状
goals.en: State the tensor shape at every step of multi-head attention

goals.zh: 能计算一层注意力的参数量，并说明它与头数无关
goals.en: Compute the parameter count of an attention layer and explain why it does not depend on the number of heads

goals.zh: 能用 GPT-2 的权重复现其注意力层的输出
goals.en: Reproduce the output of GPT-2's attention layer from its weights

explain.zh: 做法是把宽度为 $d$ 的向量平均分成 $h$ 份，每份宽度为 $d/h$。每一份独立做一次 2.1 中的注意力，有自己的 query、key、value 和自己的权重矩阵，称为一个**头** (head)。$h$ 个头的输出拼接起来，宽度回到 $d$，再乘一个输出矩阵 $W_O$。GPT-2 small 中 $d = 768$，$h = 12$，每个头的宽度是 64。
explain.en: The vector of width $d$ is split evenly into $h$ parts of width $d/h$. Each part runs the attention of 2.1 independently with its own queries, keys, values and its own weight matrix, and is called a **head**. The outputs of the $h$ heads are concatenated back to width $d$ and multiplied by an output matrix $W_O$. In GPT-2 small $d = 768$ and $h = 12$, so each head has width 64.

explain.zh: 实现时并不会真的写 $h$ 个循环。通常用一个大矩阵一次算出所有头的 query、key、value，再用 `view` 和 `transpose` 把形状从 $(B, T, d)$ 变成 $(B, h, T, d/h)$。这样“头”成了一个普通的批量维度，所有头的注意力用同一次矩阵乘法完成。这一串形状变换是实现中最容易出错的地方，也是面试手写代码时的常见考点。
explain.en: An implementation does not really loop over $h$ heads. A single large matrix usually computes the queries, keys and values of all heads at once, and `view` with `transpose` changes the shape from $(B, T, d)$ to $(B, h, T, d/h)$. The head then becomes an ordinary batch dimension and the attention of all heads is one matrix multiplication. This chain of shape changes is where implementations most often go wrong, and it is a common point in interview coding.

explain.zh: 一个容易忽略的事实是，参数量和计算量都与头数无关。头数增加，每个头的宽度按比例减小，两者相互抵消。所以多头是把同样的容量分成几份独立使用，而不是增加容量。头数过多时每个头太窄，表达能力会受限。
explain.en: An easily missed fact is that neither the parameter count nor the computation depends on the number of heads. More heads means proportionally narrower heads, and the two cancel. Multiple heads therefore divide the same capacity into independently used parts and do not add capacity. With too many heads each becomes too narrow and its expressive power is limited.

caption.zh: 多头注意力中张量形状的变化。B 是批量大小，T 是序列长度，d 是向量宽度，h 是头数。
caption.en: How tensor shapes change in multi-head attention. B is the batch size, T the sequence length, d the vector width and h the number of heads.

source.text: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762, §3.2.2

steps.tex: \mathrm{head}_i = \mathrm{Attention}\big(X W_Q^{i},\; X W_K^{i},\; X W_V^{i}\big),\qquad W^{i}_{Q,K,V} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_h},\ \ d_h = d/h

note.zh: 每个头有自己的三个投影矩阵，把宽度 $d$ 的输入投影到宽度 $d_h$。
note.en: Each head has its own three projection matrices that map the input of width $d$ to width $d_h$.

note.zh: 把 $h$ 个头的输出拼接成宽度 $d$，再做一次线性变换。
note.en: The outputs of the $h$ heads are concatenated to width $d$ and passed through one more linear map.

note.zh: 参数量（含偏置）。代入 $d_h = d/h$ 后 $h$ 被约掉。GPT-2 small 中是 $4 \cdot 768^2 + 4 \cdot 768 = 2{,}362{,}368$，与 0.2 的统计一致。
note.en: The parameter count with biases. Substituting $d_h = d/h$ cancels $h$. In GPT-2 small this is $4 \cdot 768^2 + 4 \cdot 768 = 2{,}362{,}368$, matching the count in 0.2.

note.zh: 计算分数矩阵的乘法次数。同样与 $h$ 无关，和宽度为 $d$ 的单头注意力相同。
note.en: The number of multiplications for the score matrices. It is also independent of $h$ and equals that of a single head of width $d$.

note.zh: 把 $W_O$ 按行切成 $h$ 块 $W_O^{i}$，拼接再相乘就等于各头分别相乘再相加。也就是说每个头独立地往输出里加上自己的贡献。这个视角是可解释性研究分析单个头的基础。
note.en: Cutting $W_O$ row-wise into $h$ blocks $W_O^{i}$ shows that concatenating and multiplying equals multiplying per head and adding. Each head therefore adds its own contribution to the output independently. This view is the basis for analysing single heads in interpretability research.

q.zh: 为什么要用多个头，一个大的头不行吗？
q.en: Why several heads and not one large head?

a.zh: 一个头在每个位置只产生一组权重，softmax 又倾向于把权重集中到少数位置，所以一个头很难同时关注几种不同的关系。多个头各有一组权重，可以分别关注不同的东西。代价是每个头变窄，原论文中的实验显示头数过少或过多效果都会下降。
a.en: One head produces a single set of weights per position, and softmax tends to concentrate weight on a few positions, so one head can hardly attend to several different relations at once. Several heads each have their own weights and can attend to different things. The price is narrower heads, and the experiments in the original paper show quality dropping with too few or too many heads.

q.zh: 头越多，参数就越多吗？
q.en: Do more heads mean more parameters?

a.zh: 不会。向量宽度 $d$ 固定时，头数增加，每个头的宽度 $d/h$ 相应减小，总参数量始终是 $4d^2 + 4d$。练习 1 会用不同的头数验证这一点。
a.en: No. With the vector width $d$ fixed, more heads means a smaller width $d/h$ per head, and the total stays at $4d^2 + 4d$. Exercise 1 verifies this for several head counts.

q.zh: 每个头都有用吗？
q.en: Is every head useful?

a.zh: 不一定。Michel 等人在 2019 年的研究中发现，训练好的模型在测试时去掉相当一部分头，性能下降很小，有些层甚至只留一个头也可以。这说明头之间存在冗余，但并不说明训练时也可以用同样少的头。
a.en: Not necessarily. A 2019 study by Michel and colleagues found that a large share of the heads of a trained model can be removed at test time with little loss, and some layers work with a single head. This shows redundancy among heads. It does not show that training could use equally few heads.

q.zh: 拼接之后为什么还要乘一个 W_O？
q.en: Why multiply by W_O after concatenating?

a.zh: 拼接只是把各个头的输出并排放在一起，每个头只占据输出向量中固定的一段。$W_O$ 把各头的结果重新混合，让每个头都能写到输出向量的任意方向上，后面的层才能方便地使用这些信息。
a.en: Concatenation only places the head outputs side by side, with each head occupying a fixed segment of the output vector. $W_O$ mixes the results so that each head can write to any direction of the output vector, which lets later layers use the information conveniently.

q.zh: 为什么我的 mask 传给 PyTorch 之后结果是反的？
q.en: Why does my mask give the opposite result in PyTorch?

a.zh: PyTorch 里有两种相反的约定。`F.scaled_dot_product_attention` 的布尔 mask 中 True 表示允许关注。`nn.MultiheadAttention` 的布尔 `attn_mask` 中 True 表示禁止关注。两者混用时不会报错，但结果是错的。练习 1 的测试里两种约定都出现了，可以对照。
a.en: PyTorch has two opposite conventions. In the boolean mask of `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` True means attention is allowed. In the boolean `attn_mask` of `nn.MultiheadAttention` True means attention is forbidden. Mixing them raises no error and gives wrong results. The tests of exercise 1 use both conventions, for comparison.

plain.zh: 读同一句话时，可以让几位读者各带一个问题去读。一位专看前一个词是什么，一位专看代词指的是谁，一位专看句子的主语，最后把各自的笔记并排放在一起。多头注意力就是这几位读者。读者增加时，每人分到的笔记本相应变薄，总页数不变。这是帮助理解的说法，实际模型中只有一部分头的分工能说得这样清楚，9.1 会实际找出几个。
plain.en: The same sentence can be read by several readers, each with a question of their own. One looks only at what the previous word is, one at whom a pronoun refers to, one at the subject of the sentence, and their notes are finally laid side by side. Multi-head attention is these readers. With more readers every notebook becomes thinner in proportion and the total number of pages stays the same. This is an aid to understanding. In a real model only some heads have a division of labour as clear as this, and 9.1 finds a few of them.

title.en: Causal masking and the three architectures

summary.zh: 一个三角形的掩码让模型不能偷看答案，也决定了 GPT、BERT 和 T5 的区别。
summary.en: A triangular mask keeps the model from peeking at the answer, and it also defines the difference between GPT, BERT and T5.

why.zh: 训练时，一段文本被整个送进模型，每个位置都要预测自己的下一个 token。如果位置 $t$ 能通过注意力看到位置 $t+1$，它就可以直接抄答案，损失会很低，但什么也没学到。因果掩码禁止每个位置读取它后面的内容，使训练时的条件与生成时一致。是否使用这个掩码，也正是 decoder-only、encoder-only 和 encoder-decoder 三类架构的分界。
why.en: During training a whole piece of text is fed into the model and every position has to predict its own next token. If position $t$ could see position $t+1$ through attention, it could copy the answer, the loss would be low and nothing would be learned. The causal mask forbids every position from reading what comes after it, which makes the conditions of training match those of generation. Whether this mask is used is also what separates the decoder-only, encoder-only and encoder-decoder architectures.

goals.zh: 能实现因果掩码并说明它为什么加在 softmax 之前
goals.en: Implement a causal mask and explain why it is applied before softmax

goals.zh: 能用扰动实验验证一个模型没有泄漏未来信息
goals.en: Verify with a perturbation experiment that a model leaks no future information

goals.zh: 能说出三类架构的区别和各自适合的任务
goals.en: State the differences between the three architectures and the tasks each suits

explain.zh: 掩码的做法很简单。在分数矩阵里，把所有“位置 $i$ 看位置 $j$，且 $j$ 在 $i$ 之后”的分数设成负无穷，再做 softmax。负无穷取指数是 0，这些位置的权重就严格为 0，剩下的权重在允许的位置之间重新归一化。允许的位置构成一个下三角形，所以这个掩码也叫下三角掩码。
explain.en: The mask is simple. In the score matrix, every score where position $i$ looks at a position $j$ that comes after $i$ is set to negative infinity before softmax. The exponential of negative infinity is 0, so those positions get exactly zero weight and the remaining weight is renormalized over the allowed positions. The allowed positions form a lower triangle, which is why this is also called a lower-triangular mask.

explain.zh: 掩码必须加在 softmax 之前。如果先做 softmax 再把不允许的权重改成 0，剩下的权重加起来就不再等于 1。
explain.en: The mask has to be applied before softmax. Setting the forbidden weights to 0 after softmax would leave the remaining weights no longer summing to 1.
