explain.zh: 有了因果掩码，位置 $t$ 的输出只依赖前 $t$ 个 token。因此一次前向计算就能同时得到 $T$ 个互不干扰的预测，每个都对应一个训练信号。这是 GPT 类模型训练效率高的关键。使用因果掩码、只有这一种层的模型称为 **decoder-only**，GPT 系列以及目前多数大语言模型都属于这一类。
explain.en: With the causal mask, the output at position $t$ depends only on the first $t$ tokens. One forward pass therefore yields $T$ predictions that do not interfere with each other, each providing a training signal. This is the key to the training efficiency of GPT-style models. A model that uses the causal mask and only this kind of layer is called **decoder-only**. The GPT series and most current large language models belong to this class.

explain.zh: 不加掩码时，每个位置可以看到整段文本，左右两边都能读。这样的模型称为 **encoder-only**，代表是 BERT。它不能用“预测下一个 token”来训练，因为答案就在输入里，所以改用掩码语言模型，即随机遮住一部分 token，让模型根据两侧的上下文把它们填回来。这类模型适合理解类任务，比如分类、抽取，以及把文本变成用于检索的向量。
explain.en: Without the mask, every position sees the whole text and reads both to the left and to the right. Such a model is called **encoder-only**, with BERT as the standard example. It cannot be trained by predicting the next token, because the answer is in the input, so it uses masked language modeling instead, where a random share of the tokens is hidden and the model fills them back in from the context on both sides. These models suit understanding tasks such as classification, extraction and turning text into vectors for retrieval.

explain.zh: 第三类是 **encoder-decoder**，原始的 Transformer 和 T5 属于这一类。encoder 不加掩码地读完输入，decoder 带因果掩码逐个生成输出，并通过**交叉注意力**读取 encoder 的结果。交叉注意力与自注意力的公式相同，区别只在于 query 来自 decoder，key 和 value 来自 encoder。这类结构适合输入和输出是两段不同文本的任务，比如翻译和摘要。
explain.en: The third class is **encoder-decoder**, to which the original Transformer and T5 belong. The encoder reads the input without a mask, and the decoder generates the output token by token with a causal mask while reading the encoder's result through **cross-attention**. Cross-attention has the same formula as self-attention. The only difference is that the queries come from the decoder and the keys and values from the encoder. This structure suits tasks whose input and output are two different texts, such as translation and summarization.

caption.zh: 三种注意力的可见范围。行是发出 query 的位置，列是被读取的位置，深色表示允许。
caption.en: What three kinds of attention can see. Rows are the positions that issue queries, columns the positions being read, and dark cells are allowed.

title.zh: 掩码怎样阻断未来信息
title.en: How the mask blocks future information

steps.tex: \tilde S_{ij} = S_{ij} + M_{ij},\qquad M_{ij} = \begin{cases} 0 & j \le i \\ -\infty & j > i \end{cases}

note.zh: 在分数上加一个掩码矩阵。允许的位置加 0，不允许的位置加负无穷。
note.en: A mask matrix is added to the scores, 0 for allowed positions and negative infinity for forbidden ones.

steps.tex: A_{ij} = \frac{e^{\tilde S_{ij}}}{\sum_{l} e^{\tilde S_{il}}} = \begin{cases} \dfrac{e^{S_{ij}}}{\sum_{l \le i} e^{S_{il}}} & j \le i \\[2ex] 0 & j > i \end{cases}

note.zh: $e^{-\infty} = 0$，未来位置的权重严格为 0，分母里也只剩下允许的位置，所以每一行仍然和为 1。
note.en: $e^{-\infty} = 0$, so future positions get exactly zero weight and only allowed positions remain in the denominator. Each row still sums to 1.

steps.tex: o_i = \sum_{j \le i} A_{ij}\, v_j \quad\Rightarrow\quad o_i \ \text{depends only on}\ x_1, \dots, x_i

note.zh: 一层注意力之后，位置 $i$ 的输出只用到前 $i$ 个位置的输入。MLP 和归一化都是逐位置的运算，不会引入其他位置的信息。
note.en: After one attention layer the output at position $i$ uses only the inputs of the first $i$ positions. The MLP and the normalization act per position and bring in nothing from other positions.

steps.tex: h^{(\ell)}_i = f\big(h^{(\ell-1)}_1, \dots, h^{(\ell-1)}_i\big) \quad\Rightarrow\quad h^{(L)}_i \ \text{depends only on}\ x_{\le i}

note.zh: 对层数做归纳。每一层都保持这个性质，所以无论叠多少层，位置 $i$ 都看不到后面的 token。练习 1 在 GPT-2 上用实验确认了这一点。
note.en: Induction over the layers. Every layer preserves the property, so however many layers are stacked, position $i$ never sees later tokens. Exercise 1 confirms this on GPT-2 by experiment.

note.zh: 于是一次前向得到的 $T$ 行 logits 各自是一个合法的预测，可以同时计算损失。
note.en: The $T$ rows of logits from one forward pass are therefore each a valid prediction, and their losses can be computed together.

title.en: The training objectives of the three architectures

source.text: Devlin et al., BERT, arXiv:1810.04805

note.zh: 因果语言模型。每个位置根据左侧的上文预测下一个 token。
note.en: Causal language modeling. Every position predicts the next token from the context on its left.

note.zh: 掩码语言模型。$\mathcal{M}$ 是被遮住的位置集合，BERT 中约占 15%。只有这些位置产生训练信号，模型可以同时利用左右两侧的上下文。
note.en: Masked language modeling. $\mathcal{M}$ is the set of hidden positions, about 15% in BERT. Only these positions give a training signal, and the model can use context on both sides.

note.zh: 条件生成。输出 $y$ 的每个 token 依赖已生成的部分和完整的输入 $x$，后者通过交叉注意力读取。
note.en: Conditional generation. Every token of the output $y$ depends on the part already generated and on the full input $x$, which is read through cross-attention.

q.zh: 为什么现在的大语言模型几乎都是 decoder-only？
q.en: Why are almost all current large language models decoder-only?

a.zh: 这是工程实践中逐步收敛的结果，常见的解释有几条。任何任务都可以写成“给一段文字，接着往下写”，一种结构和一个训练目标就能覆盖所有任务。每个位置都产生训练信号，数据利用率高。生成时前面位置的结果不随后续 token 改变，可以缓存（见 5.2）。结构单一，容易扩大规模。这些是优势的归纳，并不是 decoder-only 在所有任务上都更优的证明。
a.en: This is a convergence reached step by step in engineering practice, and several explanations are commonly given. Any task can be written as text to be continued, so one structure and one objective cover all tasks. Every position gives a training signal, so data is used efficiently. During generation the results of earlier positions do not change with later tokens and can be cached (see 5.2). The structure is uniform and scales easily. These are a summary of advantages, not a proof that decoder-only is better on every task.

q.zh: BERT 为什么不能像 GPT 那样生成文本？
q.en: Why can BERT not generate text the way GPT does?

a.zh: BERT 训练时每个位置都能看到两侧的上下文，学到的是根据完整句子填空。生成时右侧还不存在，这与它训练时见到的条件不一致。它的输出层也不是为逐个预测下一个 token 设计的。
a.en: During training every position of BERT sees context on both sides, so it learns to fill gaps given a complete sentence. During generation the right side does not exist yet, which does not match the conditions it was trained under. Its output layer is also not designed to predict the next token one at a time.

q.zh: 推理时后面本来就没有 token，为什么还需要掩码？
q.en: At inference there are no later tokens anyway, so why is the mask still needed?

a.zh: 只看最后一个位置时确实没有区别。但生成过程中前面的位置也在计算，如果不加掩码，它们会看到后来追加的 token，中间结果就与训练时不同了。保留掩码还能保证前面位置的结果在追加新 token 后不变，这正是 KV cache 可以成立的前提。
a.en: For the last position alone there is indeed no difference. Yet earlier positions are computed during generation too, and without the mask they would see tokens appended later, making their intermediate results differ from training. Keeping the mask also guarantees that the results at earlier positions stay unchanged when a new token is appended, which is exactly what makes the KV cache possible.

q.zh: 做文本检索用的 embedding 模型是哪种架构？
q.en: Which architecture do embedding models for text retrieval use?

a.zh: 传统上多是 encoder-only，因为每个位置都能看到整段文本，适合把一段话压缩成一个向量。近年也有不少基于 decoder-only 大模型改造的 embedding 模型。检索中的 bi-encoder 与 cross-encoder 在 7.2 展开。
a.en: Traditionally most are encoder-only, because every position sees the whole text, which suits compressing a passage into one vector. In recent years many embedding models have also been adapted from decoder-only large models. Bi-encoders and cross-encoders in retrieval are covered in 7.2.

plain.zh: 因果掩码像考试时用一张纸盖住后面的内容，做第 5 题时看不到第 6 题及以后。三类架构可以用三种读写方式来记。BERT 像做完形填空，整句话都能看，只猜被挖掉的词。GPT 像文字接龙，只能看前面，一个词一个词往后写。T5 像翻译，先把原文完整读完，再逐词写出译文，写的时候可以随时回看原文。
plain.en: The causal mask is like a sheet of paper covering what comes later in an exam, so that question 6 and beyond cannot be seen while question 5 is being answered. The three families can be remembered as three ways of reading and writing. BERT fills in blanks, seeing the whole sentence and guessing only the words that were removed. GPT continues a text, seeing only what came before and writing one word after another. T5 translates, reading the whole source first and then writing the translation word by word while free to look back at the source.

caption.zh: 三类架构的对照。近年也有基于 decoder-only 模型改造的嵌入模型，表中列出的是各类最典型的用途。
caption.en: The three architecture families side by side. Embedding models adapted from decoder-only models have also appeared in recent years, and the table lists the most typical uses of each family.

rows.zh: 掩码语言模型，根据两侧的上下文预测被遮住的 token
rows.en: masked language modelling, predicting hidden tokens from both sides

rows.zh: 分类、抽取、文本嵌入、检索与重排
rows.en: classification, extraction, embeddings, retrieval and reranking

rows.zh: BERT、RoBERTa，以及 7.2 中使用的嵌入模型和重排模型
rows.en: BERT, RoBERTa, and the embedding and rerank models used in 7.2

rows.zh: encoder 双向。decoder 因果，并通过交叉注意力读取 encoder 的输出
rows.en: encoder bidirectional. Decoder causal, reading the encoder output through cross-attention

rows.zh: 序列到序列，根据源序列生成目标序列
rows.en: sequence to sequence, producing the target from the source
the original Transformer, T5, BART, Whisper

rows.zh: 通用的文本生成、对话、代码

rows.en: the GPT family, Llama, Qwen, SmolLM2

summary.zh: 注意力本身分不清词序。看三种告诉模型位置的办法，并推导 RoPE 的旋转矩阵。
summary.en: Attention alone cannot tell word order. Three ways of telling the model about position, with the rotation matrix of RoPE derived.

why.zh: 注意力只按内容比对 query 和 key，公式里没有任何一项与位置有关。把输入的顺序打乱，每个 token 得到的输出不变，只是跟着换了位置。也就是说，仅靠注意力，模型无法区分“狗咬人”和“人咬狗”。位置编码的作用是把顺序信息补进去。它是 Transformer 中位置信息的唯一来源，也直接影响模型处理长文本的能力。
why.en: Attention compares queries and keys by content only, and no term in the formula depends on position. Shuffling the input leaves the output of every token unchanged, merely moved along with it. With attention alone a model therefore cannot tell “dog bites man” from “man bites dog”. Positional encoding adds the order back in. It is the only source of positional information in a Transformer and directly affects how well a model handles long text.

goals.zh: 能证明不带位置信息的自注意力对输入顺序不敏感
goals.en: Show that self-attention without positional information is insensitive to input order

goals.zh: 能写出正弦位置编码并解释相对位置为什么是线性变换
goals.en: Write the sinusoidal encoding and explain why a relative shift is a linear map

goals.zh: 能推导 RoPE 的旋转矩阵，并说明注意力分数为什么只依赖相对位置
goals.en: Derive the rotation matrix of RoPE and explain why the attention score depends only on relative position

explain.zh: 最早的做法是**绝对位置编码**，即给每个位置准备一个向量，加到 token 的嵌入上。这个向量可以是固定的，也可以是学出来的。原始 Transformer 用的是固定的正弦函数，不同维度对应不同的频率，位置就像被写成了一组不同快慢的波的读数。GPT-2 用的是可学习的位置嵌入表，也就是 0.1 中见过的 `wpe`，它有 1024 行，所以 GPT-2 最多只能处理 1024 个 token。
explain.en: The earliest approach is **absolute positional encoding**, in which every position has a vector that is added to the token embedding. The vector can be fixed or learned. The original Transformer uses fixed sine functions, with different dimensions at different frequencies, so that a position is written as the readings of waves of different speeds. GPT-2 uses a learned position table, the `wpe` seen in 0.1, which has 1024 rows, and this is why GPT-2 handles at most 1024 tokens.

explain.zh: 绝对位置编码有两个不足。语言中更重要的往往是相对位置，比如“前一个词”“隔了三个词”，而不是“第 57 个词”。另外，可学习的位置表长度固定，超出训练时见过的长度就没有对应的向量。
explain.en: Absolute encodings have two shortcomings. What matters in language is often relative position, such as the previous word or three words apart, and not the 57th word. In addition, a learned table has a fixed length, and positions beyond those seen in training have no vector.

explain.zh: **RoPE**（旋转位置编码）换了一种思路。它不往嵌入上加东西，而是在每一层计算注意力分数之前，把 query 和 key 各自旋转一个角度，角度与位置成正比。两个向量的点积只取决于它们之间的夹角，所以位置 $m$ 的 query 与位置 $n$ 的 key 的分数，只与 $m - n$ 有关。相对位置就这样直接进入了注意力分数，而且不需要任何新增的参数。LLaMA 等许多开放权重模型采用的都是 RoPE。
explain.en: **RoPE** (rotary position embedding) takes a different route. It adds nothing to the embeddings. Before the attention scores are computed in each layer, the query and the key are each rotated by an angle proportional to their position. The dot product of two vectors depends only on the angle between them, so the score between the query at position $m$ and the key at position $n$ depends only on $m - n$. Relative position thus enters the attention score directly, with no added parameters. LLaMA and many other open-weight models use RoPE.

explain.zh: 具体做法是把向量的 $d$ 个分量两两配对，每一对看成平面上的一个点，各自按不同的速度旋转。频率的取法与正弦位置编码相同。练习 2 实现它，并验证把所有位置同时平移 1000，注意力分数不变。
explain.en: Concretely, the $d$ components of a vector are grouped into pairs, each pair is treated as a point in a plane, and each pair rotates at its own speed. The frequencies are chosen as in the sinusoidal encoding. Exercise 2 implements this and verifies that shifting every position by 1000 leaves the attention scores unchanged.

caption.zh: RoPE 的二维示意。query 和 key 各按自己的位置旋转。左右两种情况的位置差都是 2，所以两个向量的夹角相同，点积也相同。
caption.en: RoPE in two dimensions. The query and the key are each rotated according to their own position. The position gap is 2 in both cases, so the angle between the two vectors is the same and so is their dot product.

title.zh: 自注意力对顺序不敏感

note.zh: $P$ 是一个置换矩阵，作用是把 $X$ 的各行重新排列，也就是打乱 token 的顺序。
note.en: $P$ is a permutation matrix that reorders the rows of $X$, that is, shuffles the tokens.

steps.tex: S' = (P X W_Q)(P X W_K)^{\top} = P\,(Q K^{\top})\,P^{\top} = P S P^{\top}

note.zh: 分数矩阵的行和列被同样地重新排列。
note.en: The rows and columns of the score matrix are reordered in the same way.

steps.tex: A' = \mathrm{softmax}(P S P^{\top}) = P\,\mathrm{softmax}(S)\,P^{\top} = P A P^{\top}

note.zh: softmax 是逐行计算的，行内元素换位置不影响数值，所以可以与置换交换。
note.en: Softmax acts row by row and reordering the entries within a row does not change their values, so it commutes with the permutation.

steps.tex: O' = A' V' = P A P^{\top} P V = P A V = P\,O

note.zh: 用到 $P^{\top} P = I$。输出只是跟着输入一起换了顺序，每个 token 得到的向量与原来相同。这个性质称为置换等变。
note.en: Uses $P^{\top} P = I$. The output is merely reordered along with the input, and every token gets the same vector as before. This property is called permutation equivariance.

source.text: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762, §3.5

note.zh: 位置 $p$ 的编码。第 $i$ 对分量使用频率 $\omega_i$，$i$ 越大频率越低，波长从 $2\pi$ 一直增加到约 $10000 \cdot 2\pi$。
note.en: The encoding of position $p$. Pair $i$ uses frequency $\omega_i$, lower for larger $i$, with wavelengths from $2\pi$ up to about $10000 \cdot 2\pi$.

steps.tex: \begin{pmatrix} \sin\omega_i(p+k) \\ \cos\omega_i(p+k) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\omega_i k & \sin\omega_i k \\ -\sin\omega_i k & \cos\omega_i k \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \sin\omega_i p \\ \cos\omega_i p \end{pmatrix}

note.zh: 和角公式。位置 $p + k$ 的编码等于位置 $p$ 的编码乘以一个只与 $k$ 有关的矩阵，所以模型有可能用线性运算表达“往后 $k$ 个位置”。这是原论文选择正弦函数的理由。
note.en: The angle-sum identities. The encoding of position $p + k$ equals that of position $p$ times a matrix that depends only on $k$, so a model can express a shift of $k$ positions with a linear operation. This is the reason the original paper gives for choosing sine functions.

note.zh: 两个位置编码的点积只取决于距离 $k$。练习 1 的测试检查的就是这一条。
note.en: The dot product of two encodings depends only on the distance $k$. The tests of exercise 1 check exactly this.

source.text: Su et al., RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding, arXiv:2104.09864

steps.tex: \big\langle f(q, m),\, f(k, n) \big\rangle = g(q,\, k,\, m - n)

note.zh: 目标。希望找到一种把位置编入 query 和 key 的方式 $f$，使两者的内积只依赖内容和相对位置 $m - n$。
note.en: The goal. Find a way $f$ of encoding position into query and key such that their inner product depends only on the content and the relative position $m - n$.

note.zh: 先看二维的情形。取 $f$ 为把向量旋转 $m\theta$ 的角度，$\theta$ 是一个固定的常数。
note.en: Start with two dimensions. Let $f$ rotate the vector by the angle $m\theta$, with $\theta$ a fixed constant.

steps.tex: \big\langle R(m\theta) q,\; R(n\theta) k \big\rangle = q^{\top} R(m\theta)^{\top} R(n\theta)\, k = q^{\top} R\big((n - m)\theta\big)\, k

note.zh: 旋转矩阵的转置是反方向的旋转，两次旋转的角度相加。结果只含 $n - m$，目标达成。
note.en: The transpose of a rotation matrix is the rotation in the opposite direction, and the angles of two rotations add. The result contains only $n - m$, so the goal is met.

note.zh: 推广到 $d$ 维。把分量两两配对，每一对用自己的频率 $\theta_i$ 旋转，整个变换是一个分块对角矩阵。
note.en: The extension to $d$ dimensions. The components are paired, each pair rotates with its own frequency $\theta_i$, and the whole map is a block-diagonal matrix.

steps.tex: S_{mn} = (R_m q_m)^{\top} (R_n k_n) = q_m^{\top}\, R_{n-m}\, k_n

note.zh: 每一块都满足上一步的性质，所以整体也满足。注意力分数只依赖相对位置。旋转只作用在 query 和 key 上，不作用在 value 上，并且每一层都做一次。
note.en: Every block has the property of the previous step, so the whole has it too. The attention score depends only on relative position. The rotation is applied to queries and keys only, not to values, and once in every layer.

steps.tex: \begin{pmatrix} x_{2i}' \\ x_{2i+1}' \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} x_{2i}\cos m\theta_i - x_{2i+1}\sin m\theta_i \\ x_{2i}\sin m\theta_i + x_{2i+1}\cos m\theta_i \end{pmatrix}

note.zh: 实现时不需要真的构造矩阵，对每一对分量直接套这个公式即可，这就是练习 2 要写的代码。旋转不改变向量的长度。
note.en: An implementation does not need to build the matrix. The formula is applied to each pair directly, which is the code of exercise 2. A rotation does not change the length of a vector.

q.zh: 为什么需要位置编码？
q.en: Why is positional encoding needed?

a.zh: 因为自注意力是置换等变的，见上面第一个推导。把句子里的词打乱，每个词得到的表示完全不变，模型也就无从知道词序。循环神经网络按顺序逐个读入，顺序信息是结构自带的。Transformer 同时处理所有位置，换来了并行，代价是位置信息需要另外提供。
a.en: Because self-attention is permutation equivariant, as the first derivation shows. Shuffling the words of a sentence leaves the representation of every word unchanged, so the model has no way of knowing the order. A recurrent network reads tokens one after another and gets order from its structure. A Transformer processes all positions at once, which buys parallelism at the price of having to supply position separately.

q.zh: RoPE 为什么被广泛采用？
q.en: Why is RoPE so widely used?

a.zh: 常见的理由有几条。它让注意力分数直接依赖相对位置，这与语言的规律更相符。它不引入任何参数，也没有长度固定的位置表。它在每一层都起作用，位置信息不会像加在输入上的编码那样随着层数加深而被稀释。实现也很简单。需要说明的是，这些是它被采用的理由，模型在远超训练长度的文本上能否保持效果，仍然取决于训练时见过的长度。
a.en: Several reasons are commonly given. It makes the attention score depend directly on relative position, which fits the regularities of language better. It adds no parameters and has no table of fixed length. It acts in every layer, so positional information is not diluted with depth the way an encoding added at the input can be. It is also simple to implement. These are the reasons for its adoption. Whether a model keeps its quality on text far longer than in training still depends on the lengths seen during training.

q.zh: 正弦编码和可学习的位置嵌入哪个更好？
q.en: Which is better, sinusoidal encoding or learned position embeddings?

a.zh: 原论文报告两者的结果几乎相同。可学习的嵌入更灵活，但只能覆盖训练时设定的最大长度。正弦编码是公式算出来的，任意位置都有定义。两者都属于绝对位置编码，现在的大模型多数已改用 RoPE 这类相对位置方法。
a.en: The original paper reports nearly identical results for the two. Learned embeddings are more flexible but cover only the maximum length set at training time. Sinusoidal encodings come from a formula and are defined for any position. Both are absolute encodings, and most current large models have moved to relative methods such as RoPE.

q.zh: GPT-2 为什么最多只能处理 1024 个 token？
q.en: Why can GPT-2 handle at most 1024 tokens?

a.zh: 因为它的位置嵌入表 `wpe` 只有 1024 行，第 1025 个位置没有对应的向量。这是可学习绝对位置编码的直接后果。上下文窗口的一般性讨论在 3.2。
a.en: Because its position table `wpe` has only 1024 rows and position 1025 has no vector. This is a direct consequence of learned absolute positions. The context window in general is discussed in 3.2.

q.zh: RoPE 为什么只旋转 query 和 key，不旋转 value？
q.en: Why does RoPE rotate only queries and keys and not values?

a.zh: 位置信息需要影响的是“该读谁”，也就是注意力分数，而分数只由 query 和 key 决定。value 是被读取的内容，如果也旋转，输出里会混入与绝对位置有关的成分，相对位置的性质就被破坏了。
a.en: Position has to influence whom to read from, which is the attention score, and the score is determined by queries and keys alone. The value is the content being read. Rotating it as well would mix a component that depends on absolute position into the output and break the relative-position property.

plain.zh: 没有位置信息的注意力，像把一句话的词倒进袋子里摇匀，“狗咬人”和“人咬狗”成了同一袋词。绝对位置编码相当于给每个词贴上座位号。RoPE 更像钟表，每个词按自己的位置把指针拨过相应的角度，两个词比较时只看两根指针之间的夹角，而夹角只取决于它们相隔多远，与各自坐在第几排无关。
plain.en: Attention without position information is like pouring the words of a sentence into a bag and shaking it, so that dog bites man and man bites dog become the same bag of words. Absolute position encoding gives every word a seat number. RoPE is more like a clock. Every word turns its hand by an angle according to its position, and when two words are compared only the angle between the two hands counts, which depends on how far apart they are and not on which row each sits in.

summary.zh: 让几十层网络训得动的三样东西。最后把所有部件拼起来，完整复现 GPT-2 的前向计算，并训练一个 mini-GPT。
summary.en: The three things that make dozens of layers trainable. At the end all components are assembled to reproduce GPT-2's forward pass in full and to train a mini-GPT.

why.zh: 只有注意力还不够。注意力对 value 做的是加权平均，本身没有逐位置的非线性加工，这一步由 MLP 完成。更要紧的是，把几十层直接叠起来几乎无法训练，信号和梯度会在层与层之间不断放大或缩小。残差连接给梯度留出一条不经过任何变换的通路，归一化把每层输入的数值范围固定下来。有了这两样，深层 Transformer 才训练得起来。
why.en: Attention alone is not enough. Attention takes a weighted average of values and has no nonlinear processing per position, which is the job of the MLP. More importantly, dozens of layers stacked directly are nearly impossible to train, because signals and gradients keep growing or shrinking from layer to layer. Residual connections leave gradients a path that passes through no transformation, and normalization fixes the numerical range of the input of each layer. With these two, deep Transformers become trainable.

goals.zh: 能写出 LayerNorm 和 RMSNorm 的公式并说明区别
goals.en: Write the formulas of LayerNorm and RMSNorm and state the difference

goals.zh: 能解释残差连接为什么让深层网络可训练，以及 Pre-Norm 与 Post-Norm 的区别
goals.en: Explain why residual connections make deep networks trainable, and the difference between Pre-Norm and Post-Norm

goals.zh: 能把各部件拼成一个完整的 Transformer block
goals.en: Assemble the components into a complete Transformer block

explain.zh: **残差连接。** 每个子层不直接输出新的向量，而是算出一个修改量，加到原来的向量上，即 $x + F(x)$。这样从第一层到最后一层有一条一直做加法的主干道，每一层只是往上面添一点东西。可解释性研究把这条主干道称为残差流。梯度沿着它可以原样传回去，不会因为层数多而消失。
explain.en: **Residual connections.** A sublayer does not output a new vector directly. It computes a modification that is added to the original vector, $x + F(x)$. From the first layer to the last there is then a main road of additions, and each layer only adds something to it. Interpretability research calls this main road the residual stream. Gradients travel back along it unchanged and do not vanish with depth.

explain.zh: **归一化。** LayerNorm 对每个位置的向量单独操作，减去它的均值，除以它的标准差，再乘上可学习的缩放、加上可学习的偏移。无论上一层的输出数值多大，进入下一层之前都被拉回到相近的范围。RMSNorm 是它的简化版，不减均值，只除以均方根，也没有偏移。RMSNorm 的作者认为 LayerNorm 中减均值这一步并不是必需的，去掉后计算更简单。
explain.en: **Normalization.** LayerNorm acts on the vector of each position separately. It subtracts the mean, divides by the standard deviation, multiplies by a learned scale and adds a learned shift. However large the outputs of the previous layer are, they are brought back to a similar range before entering the next layer. RMSNorm is a simplification that skips the mean subtraction, divides by the root mean square only and has no shift. Its authors argue that the mean subtraction in LayerNorm is not essential, and dropping it makes the computation simpler.

explain.zh: **归一化放在哪里。** 原始 Transformer 把归一化放在残差相加之后，称为 Post-Norm。现在的模型几乎都放在子层的入口，称为 Pre-Norm。区别在于 Pre-Norm 下主干道上没有任何归一化，梯度的直通路径是完整的。Xiong 等人的分析指出，Post-Norm 在初始化时靠近输出的参数梯度偏大，需要学习率预热来稳定训练，而 Pre-Norm 可以去掉预热。
explain.en: **Where the normalization goes.** The original Transformer places it after the residual addition, called Post-Norm. Nearly all current models place it at the entrance of the sublayer, called Pre-Norm. The difference is that under Pre-Norm the main road carries no normalization at all, so the direct path of the gradient is intact. The analysis of Xiong and colleagues shows that with Post-Norm the gradients of parameters near the output are large at initialization and learning-rate warm-up is needed for stability, while Pre-Norm can do without warm-up.

explain.zh: **FFN，也叫 MLP。** 每个位置的向量单独通过一个两层的小网络，先扩到 4 倍宽，过一个非线性函数，再压回原来的宽度。0.2 中数过，它占了每层约三分之二的参数。GPT-2 使用的非线性函数是 GELU。LLaMA 一类的模型改用 SwiGLU，它多了一条门控支路，用一个向量逐元素地控制另一个向量通过多少。为了保持参数量不变，隐藏层宽度相应缩小为 4 倍的三分之二。
explain.en: **The FFN, also called the MLP.** The vector of each position passes alone through a small two-layer network that widens it fourfold, applies a nonlinear function and narrows it back. As counted in 0.2, it holds about two thirds of the parameters of each layer. GPT-2 uses GELU as the nonlinearity. Models of the LLaMA family use SwiGLU, which adds a gating branch where one vector controls element by element how much of another passes. To keep the parameter count unchanged, the hidden width is reduced to two thirds of the fourfold width.

explain.zh: **拼起来。** 一个 Pre-Norm 的 block 就是两行，先是 $x = x + \mathrm{Attn}(\mathrm{LN}(x))$，再是 $x = x + \mathrm{MLP}(\mathrm{LN}(x))$。练习 3 用这两行加上前面写好的注意力和 MLP，不调用 GPT-2 任何一层的前向函数，算出与 GPT-2 完全一致的 logits。到这一步，阶段 0 流程图里从嵌入到 logits 的每一格都已经亲手实现过。练习 4 再用同样的结构从零训练一个字符级的小模型。
explain.en: **Putting it together.** A Pre-Norm block is two lines, first $x = x + \mathrm{Attn}(\mathrm{LN}(x))$ and then $x = x + \mathrm{MLP}(\mathrm{LN}(x))$. Exercise 3 uses these two lines with the attention and MLP written earlier and, without calling the forward function of any GPT-2 layer, computes logits identical to those of GPT-2. At that point every box of the stage 0 diagram from embedding to logits has been implemented by hand. Exercise 4 then trains a small character-level model from scratch with the same structure.

caption.zh: Post-Norm 与 Pre-Norm 的对比。上方的粗线是残差流。Post-Norm 中归一化位于主干道上，Pre-Norm 中主干道上只有加法。
caption.en: Post-Norm and Pre-Norm compared. The thick line on top is the residual stream. In Post-Norm the normalization sits on the main road, in Pre-Norm the main road carries only additions.

source.text: Zhang & Sennrich, Root Mean Square Layer Normalization, arXiv:1910.07467

note.zh: 对单个位置的向量 $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ 求均值和方差。统计量只来自这一个向量，与 batch 中的其他样本和序列中的其他位置都无关。
note.en: The mean and variance of the vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ of a single position. The statistics come from this one vector only and involve neither other samples in the batch nor other positions in the sequence.

note.zh: LayerNorm。$\gamma$ 和 $\beta$ 是可学习的参数，$\epsilon$ 是防止除以 0 的小数。
note.en: LayerNorm. $\gamma$ and $\beta$ are learned parameters and $\epsilon$ is a small number that prevents division by 0.

note.zh: RMSNorm。不减均值，没有偏移，只按均方根缩放。
note.en: RMSNorm. No mean subtraction and no shift, only scaling by the root mean square.

note.zh: 输入的均值恰好为 0 时两者相同。所以 RMSNorm 可以理解为省去了“减均值”这一步的 LayerNorm。
note.en: When the input has mean exactly 0 the two coincide. RMSNorm can therefore be read as LayerNorm without the mean-subtraction step.

note.zh: 两者都对输入的整体缩放不敏感。上一层的输出放大多少倍，归一化之后都一样，这就是它稳定训练的原因。
note.en: Both are insensitive to an overall rescaling of the input. However much the output of the previous layer is scaled up, the result after normalization is the same, which is why it stabilizes training.

source.text: He et al., Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks, arXiv:1603.05027

note.zh: 每一层输出的是输入加上一个修改量。
note.en: The output of each layer is its input plus a modification.

note.zh: 把这个式子逐层展开。最后一层的向量等于任何一层的向量加上之后所有层的修改量。
note.en: Unrolling the recursion. The vector of the last layer equals the vector of any earlier layer plus the modifications of all layers after it.

note.zh: 对 $x_\ell$ 求导。括号里的 $I$ 表示损失的梯度有一部分原封不动地传到了第 $\ell$ 层，与中间隔了多少层无关。没有残差时，梯度是许多矩阵的连乘，很容易变得极小或极大。
note.en: Differentiate with respect to $x_\ell$. The $I$ in the bracket means part of the gradient of the loss reaches layer $\ell$ unchanged, however many layers lie between. Without residuals the gradient is a product of many matrices and easily becomes tiny or huge.

source.text: Xiong et al., On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture, arXiv:2002.04745

note.zh: 原始 Transformer 的做法。归一化作用在相加之后的结果上，主干道每经过一层就被归一化一次，上一个推导中的恒等项不再成立。
note.en: The original Transformer. The normalization acts on the result of the addition, so the main road is normalized at every layer and the identity term of the previous derivation no longer holds.

note.zh: 归一化只作用在子层的输入上。主干道上只有加法，恒等项完整保留。
note.en: The normalization acts only on the input of the sublayer. The main road carries only additions and the identity term is fully preserved.

note.zh: Pre-Norm 的主干道从未被归一化，所以在最后一层之后需要补一个归一化再接输出层。这就是 GPT-2 中的 `ln_f`。
note.en: The main road of a Pre-Norm model is never normalized, so one normalization is added after the last layer before the output layer. This is `ln_f` in GPT-2.

source.text: Shazeer, GLU Variants Improve Transformer, arXiv:2002.05202

steps.tex: \mathrm{FFN}(x) = W_2\, \phi(W_1 x + b_1) + b_2,\qquad W_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{4d \times d},\ \ W_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times 4d}

note.zh: 标准的 FFN。$\phi$ 是非线性函数，原始 Transformer 用 ReLU，GPT-2 用 GELU。
note.en: The standard FFN. $\phi$ is the nonlinearity, ReLU in the original Transformer and GELU in GPT-2.

note.zh: $\Phi$ 是标准正态分布的累积分布函数，$\sigma$ 是 sigmoid。两者都是 ReLU 的平滑版本，在 0 附近不是硬折线。SiLU 也叫 Swish。
note.en: $\Phi$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function and $\sigma$ the sigmoid. Both are smooth versions of ReLU without the hard kink at 0. SiLU is also called Swish.

note.zh: SwiGLU 有三个矩阵。输入被投影两次，一路经过 SiLU 作为门，与另一路逐元素相乘（$\odot$），再投影回去。
note.en: SwiGLU has three matrices. The input is projected twice, one branch passes through SiLU as a gate and is multiplied element by element ($\odot$) with the other, and the result is projected back.

note.zh: 三个矩阵比两个多，要保持参数量与隐藏宽度为 $4d$ 的标准 FFN 相同，隐藏宽度 $h$ 需要取 $\tfrac{2}{3}\cdot 4d$。LLaMA 的配置正是这样取的。
note.en: Three matrices are more than two. To keep the parameter count equal to a standard FFN of hidden width $4d$, the hidden width $h$ has to be $\tfrac{2}{3}\cdot 4d$. This is exactly the choice in LLaMA's configuration.

q.zh: 为什么 Transformer 用 LayerNorm，而较少用 BatchNorm？
q.en: Why do Transformers use LayerNorm and rarely BatchNorm?

a.zh: BatchNorm 的统计量来自同一个 batch 里的其他样本。文本序列长短不一，需要填充，batch 较小时统计量也不稳定，而且训练和推理时的行为不同。LayerNorm 只用单个位置自己的向量来计算，与 batch 大小和序列长度都无关，训练和推理完全一致，逐个 token 生成时也不受影响。
a.en: The statistics of BatchNorm come from the other samples of the same batch. Text sequences vary in length and need padding, the statistics are unstable for small batches, and behaviour differs between training and inference. LayerNorm computes from the vector of a single position alone, independent of batch size and sequence length, behaves identically in training and inference and is unaffected by token-by-token generation.

q.zh: 为什么 Pre-Norm 成为主流？
q.en: Why did Pre-Norm become standard?

a.zh: 主要是训练更稳定。Pre-Norm 下残差主干道上只有加法，梯度可以不受阻碍地传到底层。Xiong 等人的工作从理论和实验两方面说明，Post-Norm 对学习率预热很敏感，而 Pre-Norm 去掉预热也能训练，调参更省事。层数越多，这一点越重要。
a.en: Mainly because training is more stable. Under Pre-Norm the residual main road carries only additions and gradients reach the lower layers unobstructed. The work of Xiong and colleagues shows in theory and experiment that Post-Norm is sensitive to learning-rate warm-up, while Pre-Norm trains without warm-up and needs less tuning. The deeper the model, the more this matters.

q.zh: 有了注意力，为什么还需要 MLP？
q.en: With attention, why is an MLP still needed?

a.zh: 两者分工不同。注意力负责在位置之间搬运信息，但它对 value 做的只是加权平均。MLP 负责在每个位置内部对汇集来的信息做非线性加工。去掉 MLP，模型的表达能力会大幅下降。可解释性方面的研究也常把 MLP 看作存储事实性知识的主要位置，这一点在阶段 9 会用到。
a.en: The two have different jobs. Attention moves information between positions, yet what it does to the values is only a weighted average. The MLP processes the gathered information nonlinearly within each position. Without the MLP the expressive power of the model drops sharply. Interpretability research also often regards the MLPs as the main place where factual knowledge is stored, which stage 9 will use.

q.zh: 残差连接为什么能让深层网络训练起来？
q.en: Why do residual connections make deep networks trainable?

a.zh: 见上面第二个推导。损失对任意一层输入的梯度里有一个恒等项，这部分梯度不经过任何中间层的变换直接到达。没有残差时梯度是很多层雅可比矩阵的连乘，层数一多就容易消失或爆炸。
a.en: See the second derivation above. The gradient of the loss with respect to the input of any layer contains an identity term, and this part arrives without passing through the transformation of any intermediate layer. Without residuals the gradient is a product of the Jacobians of many layers and easily vanishes or explodes as depth grows.

q.zh: 为什么不同模型的配置里，FFN 的宽度有的是 4 倍，有的是 2.67 倍？
q.en: Why is the FFN width 4x in some model configs and 2.67x in others?

a.zh: 通常是因为用了 SwiGLU。它比标准 FFN 多一个矩阵，为了让参数量相同，隐藏宽度取 4 倍的三分之二，约为 2.67 倍。见上面第四个推导的最后一步。
a.en: Usually because SwiGLU is used. It has one matrix more than the standard FFN, and to keep the parameter count equal the hidden width is two thirds of the fourfold width, about 2.67 times. See the last step of the fourth derivation above.

q.zh: 练习里的 mini-GPT 损失降到 0.2，说明它学会语言了吗？
q.en: The mini-GPT in the exercise reaches a loss of 0.2. Has it learned language?

a.zh: 没有。训练文本只有八百多个字符，模型把它背下来了。损失远低于正常语言模型的水平，恰恰是过拟合的表现。这个练习的目的是确认结构和训练循环是正确的，包括初始损失接近 $\ln V$、因果掩码有效、损失能下降。要学到可泛化的规律需要大得多的数据，这是 4.1 的内容。
a.en: No. The training text has only about eight hundred characters and the model has memorized it. A loss far below that of a normal language model is precisely a sign of overfitting. The purpose of the exercise is to confirm that the structure and the training loop are correct, including an initial loss near $\ln V$, a working causal mask and a falling loss. Learning regularities that generalize needs far more data, which is the subject of 4.1.

plain.zh: 残差连接像一份由许多人依次传阅的文件，每个人不重写全文，只在页边加批注，原文始终都在。归一化像每位审阅者动笔之前先把字号调到同样大小，免得前面的人写得太大或太小影响阅读。FFN 是每个人拿到材料之后自己消化思考的那一步。注意力负责从别的位置收集信息，FFN 负责把收集来的信息加工一遍。
plain.en: The residual connection is like a document passed along many readers in turn. Nobody rewrites the text. Everybody adds notes in the margin, and the original stays in place. Normalization is like every reviewer setting the font to the same size before starting, so that large or small writing by earlier readers does not get in the way. The FFN is the step in which each reader digests the material alone. Attention gathers information from other positions, and the FFN works over what was gathered.

summary.zh: 数清一层要做多少次乘法。输入变长时，哪部分线性增长，哪部分平方增长。
summary.en: Count the multiplications in one layer, and see which part grows linearly and which quadratically as the input gets longer.

why.zh: 模型能处理多长的输入、一次调用要花多少钱、要等多久，最终都取决于计算量和显存怎样随序列长度增长。这一模块把前面实现过的每个部件的代价加起来，得到一个可以直接用于估算的公式。它也解释了为什么长上下文昂贵，以及为什么会出现各种降低注意力代价的技术。
why.en: How long an input a model can take, what a call costs and how long it takes all come down to how computation and memory grow with sequence length. This module adds up the cost of every component implemented so far into a formula that can be used directly for estimates. It also explains why long contexts are expensive and why so many techniques for reducing the cost of attention exist.

goals.zh: 能推导一层 Transformer 的乘法次数
goals.en: Derive the number of multiplications in one Transformer layer

goals.zh: 能说出线性部分与平方部分各来自哪里，以及两者在什么长度相等
goals.en: Say where the linear and the quadratic part come from and at what length they are equal

goals.zh: 能估算注意力矩阵占用的显存
goals.en: Estimate the memory taken by the attention matrices

explain.zh: 一层里的计算可以分成两类。第一类是逐位置的运算，包括注意力中的四个投影矩阵和整个 MLP。每个位置各算各的，$T$ 个位置的总量与 $T$ 成正比。第二类是位置两两之间的运算，包括计算分数矩阵和用权重对 value 加权求和。每个位置都要与所有位置打交道，总量与 $T^2$ 成正比。
explain.en: The computation in a layer falls into two kinds. The first is per-position, namely the four projection matrices of attention and the whole MLP. Every position is computed on its own and the total over $T$ positions is proportional to $T$. The second is between pairs of positions, namely computing the score matrix and taking the weighted sum of values. Every position deals with all positions and the total is proportional to $T^2$.

explain.zh: 把两类加起来，一层大约需要 $12\,T d^2 + 2\,T^2 d$ 次乘法。前一项正好是 $T$ 乘以每层的参数量，也就是说每个参数对每个 token 使用一次。后一项是注意力特有的平方项。令两项相等，得到 $T = 6d$。序列比这个长度短时，线性部分占主导。序列比它长得多时，平方部分占主导。
explain.en: Adding the two, a layer needs about $12\,T d^2 + 2\,T^2 d$ multiplications. The first term is exactly $T$ times the parameter count of a layer, which means every parameter is used once per token. The second is the quadratic term specific to attention. Setting them equal gives $T = 6d$. For sequences shorter than this the linear part dominates. For sequences much longer the quadratic part dominates.

explain.zh: 这个结果可能与“注意力是平方复杂度所以很贵”的常见说法有些出入。对 GPT-2 small，$6d = 4608$，而它的上下文只有 1024，平方项其实只占小头。但对于上下文达到十万 token 量级的模型，即使 $d = 4096$，$6d$ 也只有两万多，平方项成为主要开销。长上下文的代价就来自这里。
explain.en: This result may differ somewhat from the common statement that attention is quadratic and therefore expensive. For GPT-2 small $6d = 4608$ while its context is only 1024, so the quadratic term is in fact the smaller share. For models whose context reaches the order of a hundred thousand tokens, even with $d = 4096$ the value of $6d$ is only about twenty-four thousand and the quadratic term becomes the main cost. This is where the price of long contexts comes from.

explain.zh: 显存方面，注意力权重矩阵的大小是每层每个头 $T \times T$。上下文 8192、32 个头时，一层的权重矩阵用半精度存储就需要约 4 GiB。实际系统会用 FlashAttention 这样的方法分块计算，避免把整个矩阵存下来。生成时还有另一个层面的重复计算，即每生成一个 token 都把整段输入重算一遍，这由 KV cache 解决，在 5.2 展开。
explain.en: For memory, the attention weight matrix is $T \times T$ per head per layer. With a context of 8192 and 32 heads, the weight matrices of a single layer take about 4 GiB in half precision. Real systems use methods such as FlashAttention that compute in blocks and avoid storing the whole matrix. Generation has a further layer of repeated work, namely recomputing the whole input for every new token, which the KV cache solves and 5.2 covers.

caption.zh: d = 768 时一层的乘法次数随序列长度的变化。线性部分来自投影和 MLP，平方部分来自注意力。两条线在 T = 6d = 4608 处相交。
caption.en: Multiplications in one layer against sequence length for d = 768. The linear part comes from the projections and the MLP, the quadratic part from attention. The two curves cross at T = 6d = 4608.

note.zh: $Q$、$K$、$V$ 和输出投影各是一个 $d \times d$ 的矩阵。一个 $d$ 维向量乘以它需要 $d^2$ 次乘法，$T$ 个位置共 $4Td^2$ 次。
note.en: $Q$, $K$, $V$ and the output projection are each a $d \times d$ matrix. Multiplying a $d$-dimensional vector by it takes $d^2$ multiplications, so $T$ positions take $4Td^2$.

note.zh: 每个头有 $T^2$ 个点积，每个点积是 $d/h$ 次乘法，共 $h$ 个头。
note.en: Each head has $T^2$ dot products of $d/h$ multiplications each, and there are $h$ heads.

note.zh: 每个头用 $T \times T$ 的权重矩阵乘 $T \times d/h$ 的 value 矩阵。
note.en: Each head multiplies the $T \times T$ weight matrix with the $T \times d/h$ value matrix.

note.zh: 先扩到 $4d$ 再压回 $d$，两个矩阵。
note.en: Widening to $4d$ and narrowing back to $d$, two matrices.

steps.tex: \text{total} \approx \underbrace{12\, T d^2}_{\text{linear in } T} + \underbrace{2\, T^2 d}_{\text{quadratic in } T}

note.zh: 线性项的系数 $12d^2$ 就是 0.2 中数出的每层参数量。
note.en: The coefficient $12d^2$ of the linear term is the per-layer parameter count from 0.2.
The sequence length at which the two terms are equal, 4608 for $d = 768$ and 24576 for $d = 4096$.

title.en: Memory and the cost of generation

note.zh: 每个头一个 $T \times T$ 的矩阵。$h = 32$、$T = 8192$、半精度时为 $32 \cdot 8192^2 \cdot 2$ 字节，即 4 GiB。
note.en: One $T \times T$ matrix per head. With $h = 32$, $T = 8192$ and half precision this is $32 \cdot 8192^2 \cdot 2$ bytes, that is 4 GiB.

note.zh: 不用缓存生成 $n$ 个 token。第 $t$ 步要对长度为 $t$ 的序列做一次完整前向，代价为 $a t + b t^2$，其中 $a = 12 d^2 L$，$b = 2 d L$。总代价多了一个 $n$ 的因子。
note.en: Generating $n$ tokens without a cache. Step $t$ runs a full forward pass on a sequence of length $t$ at a cost of $a t + b t^2$ with $a = 12 d^2 L$ and $b = 2 d L$. The total picks up an extra factor of $n$.

note.zh: 使用 KV cache。前面位置的 key 和 value 已经存好，第 $t$ 步只需计算新 token 这一个位置，它与前面 $t$ 个位置做注意力。总代价少了一个 $n$ 的因子。实现见 5.2。
note.en: With a KV cache. The keys and values of earlier positions are stored, so step $t$ computes only the one new position, which attends to the $t$ positions before it. The total loses a factor of $n$. The implementation is in 5.2.

q.zh: 为什么输入越长越贵、越慢？
q.en: Why are longer inputs slower and more expensive?

a.zh: 有两层原因。计算量本身随长度增长，其中一部分与长度成正比，注意力部分与长度的平方成正比，输入很长时后者占主导。此外输入越长，生成每个新 token 时要读取的历史也越多，即使有 KV cache，每一步的注意力计算和缓存占用的显存也随长度线性增加。
a.en: There are two layers to this. The computation itself grows with length, part of it in proportion to the length and the attention part in proportion to its square, and for very long inputs the latter dominates. In addition, the longer the input, the more history each new token has to read. Even with a KV cache, the attention computation of each step and the memory held by the cache grow linearly with length.

q.zh: 计算量是平方增长的，为什么 API 按 token 数线性收费？
q.en: Computation grows quadratically, so why do APIs charge linearly per token?

a.zh: 在常见的输入长度下，线性部分并不小，见上面 $T = 6d$ 的分析，所以线性计价是一个可用的近似。定价还包含硬件利用率、批处理和商业上的考虑，不直接等于计算量。部分服务对超过一定长度的请求采用更高的单价，也有服务对重复出现的长前缀提供缓存折扣，这些都与上面的代价结构相符。具体价格经常变化，以各家的官方页面为准。
a.en: At common input lengths the linear part is not small, as the $T = 6d$ analysis shows, so linear pricing is a workable approximation. Pricing also reflects hardware utilization, batching and commercial considerations and does not equal the computation directly. Some services charge a higher unit price beyond a certain length and some offer cache discounts for long repeated prefixes, both of which fit the cost structure above. Actual prices change often and the official pages are the reference.

q.zh: 有哪些办法降低长序列的代价？
q.en: What reduces the cost of long sequences?

a.zh: 大致有三类。不改变结果、只改进实现的方法，比如 FlashAttention 通过分块计算减少显存读写，结果与标准注意力完全相同。减少重复计算的方法，比如 KV cache。改变注意力结构的方法，比如只关注局部窗口或稀疏位置，这类方法会改变模型本身。目前主流的大模型主要依靠前两类。
a.en: Roughly three kinds of methods. Those that keep the result and improve the implementation, such as FlashAttention, which computes in blocks to reduce memory traffic and gives exactly the result of standard attention. Those that remove repeated computation, such as the KV cache. Those that change the structure of attention, such as attending only to a local window or to sparse positions, which changes the model itself. Current mainstream large models rely mainly on the first two.

q.zh: 估算一个模型推理的计算量，有没有简单的经验公式？
q.en: Is there a simple rule of thumb for the compute of inference?

a.zh: 序列不太长时，每个 token 的前向计算大约是参数量的 2 倍次浮点运算。因为每个参数对每个 token 参与一次乘法和一次加法，这与上面线性项等于“$T$ 乘以参数量”的结论一致。序列很长时还要加上注意力的平方项。
a.en: For sequences that are not too long, the forward pass costs about twice the parameter count in floating-point operations per token. Every parameter takes part in one multiplication and one addition per token, which agrees with the linear term above being $T$ times the parameter count. For very long sequences the quadratic term of attention has to be added.

plain.zh: 设想一场有 $T$ 个人的聚会。每人做一次自我介绍，总共 $T$ 次，这是线性的部分。每两个人互相握一次手，次数就与 $T$ 的平方成正比，人数翻倍，握手的次数变成四倍。注意力属于握手这一类，其余的计算属于自我介绍这一类。人少的时候自我介绍占大头，人很多的时候握手占大头。
plain.en: Picture a party with $T$ guests. Every guest introduces themselves once, $T$ times in all, which is the linear part. Every two guests shake hands once, a number proportional to the square of $T$, so doubling the guests quadruples the handshakes. Attention belongs to the handshakes and the rest of the computation to the introductions. With few guests the introductions dominate, and with very many the handshakes do.

summary.zh: 文本怎样变成编号。手写 BPE 的训练、编码和解码，再用真实的合并规则复现 GPT-2 的分词器。
summary.en: How text becomes ids. Write BPE training, encoding and decoding by hand, then reproduce GPT-2's tokenizer from its real merge rules.

why.zh: 模型的输入是一串编号，文本必须先被切成片段并换成编号。切得太细，比如一个字符一个 token，序列会很长，而注意力的代价随长度的平方增长。切得太粗，比如一个单词一个 token，词表会无限膨胀，遇到没见过的词就无法表示。子词分词是两者之间的折中，BPE 是其中使用最广的一种。分词方式一旦确定就与模型绑定，模型看到的世界由它决定。
why.en: The input of a model is a sequence of ids, so text first has to be cut into pieces and mapped to ids. Cutting too finely, one token per character, makes sequences very long, and the cost of attention grows with the square of the length. Cutting too coarsely, one token per word, lets the vocabulary grow without bound, and a word never seen before cannot be represented. Subword tokenization is the compromise between the two, and BPE is its most widely used form. Once chosen, the tokenization is tied to the model, and it determines the world the model sees.

goals.zh: 能手写 BPE 的训练、编码和解码
goals.en: Write BPE training, encoding and decoding by hand

goals.zh: 能解释同一个词带不带空格为什么是不同的 token
goals.en: Explain why the same word with and without a leading space is a different token

goals.zh: 能说出词表大小的取舍，以及 SentencePiece 与 GPT 系列分词器的区别
goals.en: State the trade-off in vocabulary size and how SentencePiece differs from the GPT-style tokenizers

explain.zh: **BPE 的训练。** 从最小的单位开始，GPT 系列用的是字节，所以初始词表正好是 256 个。统计文本中所有相邻的一对单位各出现了多少次，把出现最多的那一对合并成一个新单位，加入词表。然后在合并后的文本上重复这个过程，直到词表达到预定的大小。训练的产物是一张按顺序排列的合并规则表。常见的片段，比如 ` the` 或 `ing`，会很早被合并成一个 token，罕见的词则保持为几个较小的片段。
explain.en: **Training BPE.** Start from the smallest units. The GPT family uses bytes, so the initial vocabulary has exactly 256 entries. Count how often every adjacent pair of units occurs in the text, merge the most frequent pair into a new unit and add it to the vocabulary. Repeat on the merged text until the vocabulary reaches the intended size. The product of training is an ordered table of merge rules. Common pieces such as ` the` or `ing` are merged into one token early, while rare words stay as several smaller pieces.

explain.zh: **编码与解码。** 编码一段新文本时，先把它拆成字节，再按训练时学到的先后顺序依次应用合并规则。解码更简单，把每个 token 对应的字节拼起来即可。因为所有 256 个字节都在词表里，任何文本都能被编码，不存在“未知词”。练习 1 实现这三个函数，在一段 856 字节的文本上，词表从 256 增加到 300 时 token 数从 856 降到 499。
explain.en: **Encoding and decoding.** To encode new text, split it into bytes and apply the merge rules in the order they were learned. Decoding is simpler, just concatenate the bytes of every token. Since all 256 bytes are in the vocabulary, any text can be encoded and there is no unknown word. Exercise 1 implements these three functions. On a text of 856 bytes, growing the vocabulary from 256 to 300 reduces the token count from 856 to 499.

explain.zh: **预分词与空格。** 实际的分词器在做 BPE 之前，会先用规则把文本切成小段，合并只在段内进行，这一步称为预分词。GPT-2 的规则把空格归到后一个词的开头，所以 ` strawberry`（带前导空格）和 `strawberry` 是两个不同的预分词单位。前者在训练语料中很常见，被合并成了一个 token。后者不常见，被切成 `st`、`raw`、`berry` 三个 token。练习 2 用 GPT-2 真实的五万条合并规则复现这个结果。
explain.en: **Pre-tokenization and spaces.** Real tokenizers first cut the text into small segments by rule before running BPE, and merges happen only within a segment. This step is called pre-tokenization. GPT-2's rule attaches a space to the start of the following word, so ` strawberry` (with a leading space) and `strawberry` are two different pre-tokens. The first is common in the training corpus and was merged into a single token. The second is uncommon and is cut into the three tokens `st`, `raw` and `berry`. Exercise 2 reproduces this with the fifty thousand real merge rules of GPT-2.

explain.zh: **SentencePiece。** 这是另一个广泛使用的分词工具，T5 以及早期的 LLaMA 等模型使用它。它与 GPT 系列分词器的主要区别在于不依赖按空格切词的预处理，直接在原始文本上训练，空格被当作一个普通符号，写成可见的 `▁`。因此它对中文、日文这类不用空格分词的语言同样适用。SentencePiece 支持两种算法，一种是 BPE，另一种是 unigram 语言模型，后者从一个很大的候选词表出发，逐步删掉对整体概率贡献最小的片段。
explain.en: **SentencePiece.** This is another widely used tokenization tool, used by T5 and the early LLaMA models among others. Its main difference from the GPT-style tokenizers is that it does not rely on splitting at spaces beforehand. It trains directly on raw text and treats the space as an ordinary symbol, written as the visible `▁`. It therefore works equally for languages such as Chinese and Japanese that do not separate words with spaces. SentencePiece supports two algorithms, BPE and the unigram language model. The latter starts from a very large candidate vocabulary and gradually removes the pieces that contribute least to the overall probability.

explain.zh: **词表大小的取舍。** 词表越大，常见的长片段越可能成为单个 token，同样的文本切出的 token 越少，序列越短。代价是嵌入表按词表大小增长，而且罕见 token 在训练中出现的次数少，学得不充分。GPT-2 的词表是 50257，近年的模型多在十万到二十万之间。
explain.en: **The trade-off in vocabulary size.** With a larger vocabulary, common long pieces are more likely to be single tokens, the same text yields fewer tokens and sequences are shorter. The price is an embedding table that grows with the vocabulary, and rare tokens that occur seldom in training and are learned poorly. GPT-2 has a vocabulary of 50257, and models of recent years mostly have between one and two hundred thousand.

caption.zh: 在字符串 aaabdaaabac 上训练 BPE 的三次合并。每次把出现最多的相邻一对合并成新 token，11 个 token 最终变成 5 个。
caption.en: Three BPE merges on the string aaabdaaabac. Each step merges the most frequent adjacent pair into a new token, and 11 tokens end up as 5.

source.text: Sennrich, Haddow, Birch, Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units, arXiv:1508.07909

note.zh: 统计当前序列 $x$ 中每一对相邻单位出现的次数。
note.en: Count how often every adjacent pair of units occurs in the current sequence $x$.

note.zh: 选出出现次数最多的一对。
note.en: Pick the most frequent pair.

note.zh: 把这一对作为新 token 加入词表 $\mathcal{V}$，并把序列中所有这样的相邻对替换成新 token。
note.en: Add the pair to the vocabulary $\mathcal{V}$ as a new token and replace every such adjacent pair in the sequence by it.

note.zh: 每次合并词表恰好增加一个 token。想要多大的词表，就做多少次合并。GPT-2 做了 50000 次，再加一个文本结束符，共 50257。
note.en: Every merge adds exactly one token. The number of merges is chosen to reach the desired vocabulary size. GPT-2 uses 50000 merges plus one end-of-text token, 50257 in total.

steps.tex: \texttt{a a a b d a a a b a c}\qquad c(\texttt{a},\texttt{a}) = 4

note.zh: 初始有 11 个 token。出现最多的相邻对是 aa，共 4 次。
note.en: Initially 11 tokens. The most frequent adjacent pair is aa, 4 times.

steps.tex: \texttt{Z a b d Z a b a c}\qquad \texttt{Z} = \texttt{aa}

note.zh: 合并 aa 为 Z 后剩 9 个 token。注意合并是从左到右、不重叠地进行，aaa 变成 Za。
note.en: After merging aa into Z, 9 tokens remain. Merging goes left to right without overlap, so aaa becomes Za.

steps.tex: \texttt{Y b d Y b a c}\qquad \texttt{Y} = \texttt{Za} = \texttt{aaa}

note.zh: 此时 Za 和 ab 都出现 2 次，按先出现的优先，合并 Za。新 token 可以由已合并的 token 继续组合，片段就这样越长越长。
note.en: Now Za and ab both occur twice. Taking the one that appears first, Za is merged. New tokens can combine tokens already merged, which is how pieces grow longer.

note.zh: 第三次合并后剩 5 个 token。练习 1 的测试用的就是这个例子。
note.en: After the third merge 5 tokens remain. The tests of exercise 1 use exactly this example.

note.zh: 嵌入表每个 token 一行。$d = 768$ 时，词表 50257 对应约 3860 万个参数，词表 20 万对应约 1.54 亿个。
note.en: The embedding table has one row per token. With $d = 768$, a vocabulary of 50257 gives about 38.6 million parameters and one of 200 thousand about 154 million.

note.zh: 压缩率，即平均每个 token 覆盖多少字节。词表越大压缩率越高，同样的文本序列越短。
note.en: The compression ratio, the average number of bytes covered by a token. A larger vocabulary compresses more and makes the sequence for the same text shorter.

note.zh: 序列长度进入 2.6 中的平方项。压缩率提高一倍，注意力部分的代价降为四分之一，上下文窗口能装下的文本也多一倍。
note.en: Sequence length enters the quadratic term of 2.6. Doubling the compression cuts the attention cost to a quarter and doubles the amount of text that fits in the context window.

q.zh: 为什么同样的内容，中文和英文的 token 数不同？
q.en: Why does the same content cost a different number of tokens in Chinese and English?

a.zh: token 数取决于分词器在训练语料中见过多少这种语言。GPT-2 的分词器主要在英文上训练，一个汉字的三个 UTF-8 字节很少被合并，`北京是中国的首都` 被切成 14 个 token，对应的英文句子只有 7 个。较新的 o200k 编码在多语言语料上训练，同一句中文只有 6 个 token，比英文还少。所以哪种语言更费 token 没有固定答案，要看具体的分词器。练习 3.3 会实际测量。
a.en: The token count depends on how much of that language the tokenizer saw in its training corpus. GPT-2's tokenizer was trained mostly on English, the three UTF-8 bytes of a Chinese character were rarely merged, and `北京是中国的首都` is cut into 14 tokens, against 7 for the corresponding English sentence. The newer o200k encoding was trained on multilingual text, and the same Chinese sentence takes only 6 tokens, fewer than the English one. Which language costs more tokens therefore has no fixed answer and depends on the tokenizer. The exercise of 3.3 measures this.

q.zh: 为什么不直接按字符或者按单词切分？
q.en: Why not split by characters or by words?

a.zh: 按字符切，词表很小，但序列长度是子词方案的好几倍，注意力的代价按平方增长，模型还要自己学会把字符拼成有意义的单位。按单词切，序列短，但词表需要收录所有的词形变化、专有名词和拼写错误，仍然会遇到词表之外的词。子词方案用几万到几十万的词表覆盖了所有文本，常见词是一个 token，罕见词由几个片段拼成。
a.en: Splitting by characters gives a tiny vocabulary but sequences several times longer than with subwords, the cost of attention grows with the square, and the model must learn by itself to assemble characters into meaningful units. Splitting by words gives short sequences, yet the vocabulary would have to hold every inflection, proper noun and misspelling and would still meet words outside it. Subword schemes cover all text with a vocabulary of tens to hundreds of thousands, where common words are one token and rare words are built from a few pieces.

q.zh: 为什么 ` strawberry` 和 `strawberry` 是不同的 token？
q.en: Why are ` strawberry` and `strawberry` different tokens?

a.zh: GPT 系列的预分词把空格算在后一个词的开头。句子中间的词几乎都带前导空格，所以带空格的形式在训练语料中常见，被合并成了一个 token。不带空格的形式只出现在句首或紧跟标点等位置，出现得少，就保持为几个片段。大小写不同也是不同的 token。这是提示词的细微改动会影响结果的原因之一。
a.en: The pre-tokenization of the GPT family counts a space as the start of the following word. Words in the middle of a sentence nearly all carry a leading space, so the form with the space is common in the training corpus and was merged into a single token. The form without the space occurs only at the start of a sentence or right after punctuation, is less frequent and stays as several pieces. Different capitalization also gives different tokens. This is one reason small changes to a prompt affect the result.

q.zh: BPE、WordPiece 和 unigram 有什么区别？
q.en: How do BPE, WordPiece and unigram differ?

a.zh: 三者都是子词分词，区别在于怎样决定词表。BPE 从小到大，每次合并出现次数最多的一对。WordPiece 也是逐步合并，但选择的标准是合并后对语料概率的提升，BERT 使用它。unigram 从大到小，先准备一个很大的候选词表，再逐步删去贡献最小的片段，编码时选择整体概率最大的切分方式。面试中通常要求能说清 BPE 的流程，并指出另外两种的选择标准不同。
a.en: All three are subword tokenizers and differ in how the vocabulary is decided. BPE works bottom-up and merges the most frequent pair each time. WordPiece also merges step by step, but chooses by how much a merge raises the probability of the corpus, and BERT uses it. Unigram works top-down, starting from a very large candidate vocabulary and removing the pieces that contribute least, and at encoding time it picks the segmentation with the highest overall probability. Interviews usually expect a clear account of the BPE procedure and the statement that the other two use different selection criteria.

q.zh: 训练好的模型可以换一个分词器吗？
q.en: Can a trained model be given a different tokenizer?

a.zh: 不能直接换。嵌入表的每一行对应词表中一个确定的 token，模型的所有参数都是在这套编号上训练出来的。换了分词器，同一个编号指向不同的内容，模型的输入就全乱了。所以下载模型时分词器文件总是和权重一起发布。
a.en: Not directly. Every row of the embedding table belongs to one specific token of the vocabulary, and all parameters of the model were trained on these ids. With another tokenizer the same id would point to different content and the input of the model would be scrambled. This is why tokenizer files are always released together with the weights.

plain.zh: BPE 像发明速记符号。先把文章用最小的单位写出来，再看哪两个符号最常连在一起出现，就给这一对发明一个新符号，如此反复。常用的词很快有了专属的符号，生僻的词仍然要用几个小符号拼出来。积木也是这个道理，常见的形状有现成的大块，少见的形状用小块拼。
plain.en: BPE is like inventing shorthand. A text is first written in the smallest units, the two symbols that most often occur together are given a new symbol of their own, and this is repeated. Frequent words soon have a dedicated symbol, and rare words still have to be spelled with several small ones. Building blocks work the same way, with ready-made large pieces for common shapes and small pieces put together for uncommon ones.

summary.zh: 模型一次能读多少，读不下时会怎样，以及为什么对话越长每一轮越贵。
summary.en: How much a model can read at once, what happens when it does not fit, and why each turn of a longer conversation costs more.

why.zh: 模型对当前对话的全部了解，都来自这一次输入里的 token。参数在推理时不变，没有放进输入的内容，对模型来说就不存在。上下文窗口是这份输入的长度上限，它决定了模型能同时考虑多少材料，也直接决定了调用的成本。长对话中模型“忘记”前面的内容、长文档问答答非所问，多数都要从这里找原因。
why.en: Everything a model knows about the current conversation comes from the tokens of this one input. The parameters do not change at inference time, and content that is not in the input does not exist for the model. The context window is the upper limit on the length of this input. It determines how much material the model can consider at once and directly determines the cost of a call. When a model forgets earlier content in a long conversation or answers beside the point over a long document, the cause is mostly to be found here.

goals.zh: 能说明上下文窗口包含什么，以及它为什么有上限
goals.en: Explain what the context window contains and why it has a limit

goals.zh: 能计算多轮对话累计计费的 token 数
goals.en: Compute the tokens billed over a multi-turn conversation

goals.zh: 能说出模型“忘记”前文的几种不同原因
goals.en: Name the different reasons a model forgets earlier content

explain.zh: **窗口里有什么。** 上下文窗口指模型生成回答时能够参考的全部文本，包括 system prompt、历史上的每一条消息、工具返回的结果、文档，以及正在生成的回答本身。所有这些加起来不能超过窗口大小。
explain.en: **What is in the window.** The context window is all the text a model can refer to while generating a response, including the system prompt, every past message, tool results, documents and the response being generated. Together these cannot exceed the window size.

explain.zh: **为什么有上限。** 原因来自前面几个模块。位置编码只在一定长度范围内训练过（2.4）。计算量中有随长度平方增长的部分（2.6）。生成时每个已读入的 token 都要在显存中保留它的 key 和 value（5.2）。窗口大小是模型设计和训练时确定的，不能在使用时随意调大。
explain.en: **Why there is a limit.** The reasons come from earlier modules. Positional encodings are trained only over a certain range of lengths (2.4). Part of the computation grows with the square of the length (2.6). During generation the keys and values of every token read so far are kept in memory (5.2). The window size is fixed by design and training and cannot be enlarged at will during use.

explain.zh: **对话为什么越来越贵。** 模型没有跨请求的记忆。聊天界面中每发一条新消息，程序都会把此前的全部对话连同新消息一起重新发给模型。第 10 轮的输入里包含前 9 轮的所有内容。因此累计的输入 token 数随轮数的平方增长。按每轮用户 50 个 token、回答 200 个 token 计算，10 轮累计输入 11750 个 token，20 轮是 48500 个，约为 4 倍。
explain.en: **Why a conversation gets more expensive.** A model has no memory across requests. In a chat interface, every new message makes the program send the whole conversation so far together with the new message. The input of turn 10 contains everything from the first 9 turns. The cumulative number of input tokens therefore grows with the square of the number of turns. With 50 user tokens and 200 answer tokens per turn, 10 turns add up to 11750 input tokens and 20 turns to 48500, about four times as many.

explain.zh: **装不下时怎么办。** 对话超过窗口后，应用程序需要丢掉一部分内容。常见的做法是丢弃最早的消息，或者把较早的对话压缩成一段摘要。无论哪种，被丢掉或被概括掉的细节，模型之后就读不到了。
explain.en: **What happens when it does not fit.** Once a conversation exceeds the window, the application has to drop something. Common approaches are discarding the oldest messages or compressing the earlier conversation into a summary. Either way, the model can no longer read the details that were dropped or summarized away.

explain.zh: **装得下也不等于用得好。** Liu 等人的研究发现，相关信息位于长输入的开头或结尾时模型表现最好，位于中间时明显下降，这一现象被称为 lost in the middle。Chroma 在 2025 年对 18 个模型的测试也显示，即使任务难度不变，输入越长，表现越不稳定。练习 2 在 GPT-2 上做了一个小规模的版本。这个小模型表现出的是很强的近因偏好，位于末尾的事实几乎都能取回，位于开头的几乎取不回，与大模型上报告的两端高、中间低并不相同，但共同点是信息的位置会影响它能否被用上。
explain.en: **Fitting is not the same as being used well.** Liu and colleagues found that models perform best when the relevant information is at the beginning or the end of a long input and clearly worse when it is in the middle, a phenomenon called lost in the middle. A 2025 test of 18 models by Chroma likewise showed that performance becomes less reliable as the input grows, even at constant task difficulty. Exercise 2 runs a small version on GPT-2. This small model shows a strong recency preference, retrieving a fact at the end almost every time and one at the start almost never, which differs from the high-ends, low-middle pattern reported for large models. What they share is that the position of a piece of information affects whether it gets used.

caption.zh: 多轮对话中每一轮的输入。浅色部分是重新发送的历史，深色部分是新的用户消息。历史随轮数线性增长，累计输入因此按平方增长。
caption.en: The input of each turn of a multi-turn conversation. The light part is the history sent again and the dark part the new user message. The history grows linearly with the turns, so the cumulative input grows quadratically.

title.zh: 多轮对话的累计 token 数
title.en: Cumulative tokens of a multi-turn conversation

note.zh: 第 $i$ 轮的输入。$s$ 是 system prompt 的长度，$u_k$ 和 $a_k$ 是第 $k$ 轮用户消息和回答的长度。
note.en: The input of turn $i$. $s$ is the length of the system prompt, and $u_k$ and $a_k$ are the lengths of the user message and the answer of turn $k$.

note.zh: 假设每轮的长度相同，分别为 $u$ 和 $a$。单轮输入随轮数线性增长。
note.en: Assume every turn has the same lengths $u$ and $a$. The input of a single turn grows linearly with the turn number.
The cumulative input over $n$ turns. Summing the arithmetic series brings in $n^2$. With $u = 50$, $a = 200$, $s = 0$ and $n = 10$ this gives $50 \cdot 55 + 200 \cdot 45 = 11750$.

note.zh: 输出只随轮数线性增长。长对话的费用因此主要来自反复发送的历史，而不是生成的内容。服务商提供的前缀缓存折扣针对的正是这一部分。
note.en: The output grows only linearly with the turns. The cost of a long conversation therefore comes mainly from the repeatedly sent history and not from the generated content. The prefix-cache discounts offered by providers target exactly this part.

note.zh: 窗口约束。输入与本轮输出之和不能超过窗口大小 $W$，所以输入不能把窗口占满，需要给回答留出空间。
note.en: The window constraint. Input plus the output of this turn cannot exceed the window size $W$, so the input must leave room for the answer.

q.zh: 为什么长对话中模型会“忘记”前面的内容？
q.en: Why do models forget earlier parts of a long conversation?

a.zh: 至少有三种不同的原因，表现相似但机制不同。第一种是内容已经不在输入里了，对话超过窗口后较早的消息被丢弃或被压缩成摘要。第二种是内容还在输入里，但没有被用上，输入越长，位于中间或较早位置的信息越容易被忽略。第三种是使用者以为模型会“学到”对话中的内容，实际上参数没有变化，开启新对话后一切从头开始。排查时先确认是哪一种，对应的办法分别是控制历史长度、把关键信息放在靠近结尾的位置或重新提及，以及使用外部记忆。
a.en: There are at least three different causes that look alike but work differently. In the first, the content is no longer in the input, because the conversation exceeded the window and earlier messages were dropped or compressed into a summary. In the second, the content is still in the input but is not used, since information in the middle or early part is more easily ignored as the input grows. In the third, the user assumes the model learns from the conversation, while in fact no parameter changes and a new conversation starts from nothing. When diagnosing, first find out which one applies. The respective remedies are controlling the length of the history, placing key information near the end or mentioning it again, and using external memory.

q.zh: 上下文窗口是不是越大越好？
q.en: Is a larger context window always better?

a.zh: 更大的窗口让模型能同时处理更多材料，但放进去的内容越多，成本越高，速度越慢，表现也可能变得不稳定。Anthropic 的文档把这种随 token 数增加而准确率和召回下降的现象称为 context rot，并指出筛选放进上下文的内容与窗口有多大同样重要。实际使用中，只放与当前任务相关的内容通常比把所有材料都塞进去效果好，这也是 RAG 存在的理由之一。
a.en: A larger window lets a model handle more material at once, yet the more is put in, the higher the cost, the lower the speed and the less stable the performance may become. Anthropic's documentation calls this decline of accuracy and recall with growing token count context rot and states that curating what goes into the context matters as much as the size of the window. In practice, including only what is relevant to the task usually works better than putting in everything, which is one reason RAG exists.

q.zh: 为什么对话越长，每一轮越贵？
q.en: Why does each turn of a longer conversation cost more?

a.zh: 因为每一轮都要把全部历史重新发送并重新计费。单轮的输入随轮数线性增长，累计输入随轮数的平方增长，见上面的推导。输出 token 的单价通常更高，但在长对话里总费用往往由反复发送的输入决定。
a.en: Because every turn sends and bills the whole history again. The input of a single turn grows linearly with the turn number and the cumulative input with its square, as derived above. Output tokens usually have a higher unit price, yet in long conversations the total is often determined by the repeatedly sent input.

q.zh: lost in the middle 在所有模型上都一样吗？
q.en: Is lost in the middle the same for every model?

a.zh: 不一样。位置效应的具体形状取决于模型、任务和输入长度。练习 2 中的 GPT-2 只表现出近因偏好，没有开头的优势。较新的模型在这方面有改进，但输入变长后表现下降的趋势在近期的测试中仍然存在。稳妥的做法是把它当作需要实际测量的性质，而不是假定某个固定的规律。
a.en: No. The exact shape of the position effect depends on the model, the task and the input length. GPT-2 in exercise 2 shows only a recency preference without an advantage at the start. Newer models have improved in this respect, yet the trend of declining performance with longer input is still present in recent tests. The prudent approach is to treat it as a property to be measured and not to assume a fixed pattern.

plain.zh: 上下文窗口像一张大小固定的书桌，模型只能看到桌上的纸。对话每进行一轮，桌上就多几张纸。桌子满了，就得把最早的纸拿走，或者压缩成一张摘要。模型没有抽屉，拿走的纸它就再也看不到了。桌上的纸越多，要找的那一张也越容易被忽略。
plain.en: The context window is like a desk of fixed size, and the model sees only the papers on the desk. Every turn of a conversation adds a few sheets. When the desk is full the oldest sheets have to be removed or condensed into one sheet of summary. The model has no drawer, and what is removed it never sees again. The more paper lies on the desk, the more easily the one sheet needed is overlooked.

summary.zh: 字母、数字和多语言在分词后变成了什么样子，以及这怎样影响模型的表现。
summary.en: What letters, digits and other languages look like after tokenization, and how this affects model behaviour.

why.zh: 模型在一些看起来很简单的任务上会出错，比如数一个单词里有几个字母、做多位数加法。只从“模型不够聪明”去理解，无法判断该怎样改进。看一眼这些输入被切成了什么样的 token，很多现象就有了具体的解释，也能据此决定是换一种写法、让模型调用工具，还是换一个模型。
why.en: Models make mistakes on some tasks that look very simple, such as counting the letters of a word or adding multi-digit numbers. Reading this only as the model not being clever enough gives no guidance on how to improve it. A look at the tokens these inputs are cut into gives many of the phenomena a concrete explanation and a basis for deciding whether to write the input differently, let the model call a tool, or change the model.

goals.zh: 能说明模型为什么看不到单词的拼写
goals.en: Explain why a model does not see the spelling of a word

goals.zh: 能说明数字的切分方式为什么给算术带来困难
goals.en: Explain why the way digits are cut makes arithmetic hard

goals.zh: 能针对这类问题提出对应的处理办法
goals.en: Propose suitable remedies for problems of this kind

explain.zh: **字母。** `strawberry` 在 GPT-2 中被切成 `st`、`raw`、`berry` 三个 token，带前导空格时是一个 token。模型收到的是这几个 token 的编号，每个编号查表得到一个向量，其中没有任何一处直接写着这个 token 由哪几个字母组成。拼写信息只能从训练语料中间接学到，比如见过把单词逐个字母拼出来的文本。如果把单词写成字母之间带空格的形式，每个字母就成了单独的 token，字母对模型就是可见的了。
explain.en: **Letters.** GPT-2 cuts `strawberry` into the three tokens `st`, `raw` and `berry`, and into a single token when it has a leading space. The model receives the ids of these tokens, each id is looked up as a vector, and nowhere is it written directly which letters the token consists of. Spelling can only be learned indirectly from the training corpus, for example from text where words are spelled out letter by letter. When a word is written with spaces between the letters, every letter becomes a token of its own and the letters are visible to the model.

explain.zh: **数字。** 数字被切成长短不一的片段。GPT-2 把 `1234567` 切成 `123`、`45`、`67`，把 `12345678` 切成 `123`、`45`、`678`。多一位数字，后面的切法就变了。较新的 o200k 编码从左往右每三位一切，`1234567` 是 `123`、`456`、`7`。而加法的进位是从右往左进行的，个位在哪个 token 里取决于数字的总长度。模型要学会的不是一套统一的竖式规则，而是大量依赖长度和切法的特殊情况。
explain.en: **Digits.** Numbers are cut into pieces of varying length. GPT-2 cuts `1234567` into `123`, `45` and `67` and `12345678` into `123`, `45` and `678`. One more digit changes how the rest is cut. The newer o200k encoding cuts in threes from the left, giving `123`, `456` and `7` for `1234567`. Carrying in addition proceeds from right to left, however, and which token holds the units digit depends on the total length of the number. What the model has to learn is not one uniform column procedure but many special cases that depend on length and cutting.

explain.zh: **多语言。** 不同语言在同一个分词器下的效率差别很大。GPT-2 中一个汉字平均要用接近两个 token，而且一个字的三个字节可能被切到不同的 token 里，这样的 token 单独拿出来甚至不是合法的文字。较新的分词器在多语言上好得多。token 数的差别直接体现为费用、速度和上下文窗口中能放下的内容量。
explain.en: **Other languages.** The efficiency of the same tokenizer varies widely across languages. In GPT-2 a Chinese character needs close to two tokens on average, and the three bytes of one character may land in different tokens, which on their own are not even valid text. Newer tokenizers do much better on multilingual text. The difference in token count shows up directly as cost, speed and the amount of content that fits in the context window.

explain.zh: **需要谨慎的地方。** 分词是这些现象的一个重要原因，但未必是唯一的原因。关于字母计数的研究结论并不一致。有研究把问题直接归因于分词。也有研究在大量单词上统计后发现，错误与单词被切成几个 token 的相关性不强，更相关的是单词的长度以及某个字母重复出现的次数，模型能认出字母，困难在于计数本身。所以更准确的说法是，分词使字符层面的信息不直接可见，而逐项计数对这类模型本来就是弱项，两者叠加造成了这类错误。
explain.en: **Where caution is needed.** Tokenization is an important cause of these phenomena but not necessarily the only one. Studies of letter counting do not agree. Some attribute the problem directly to tokenization. Others, after statistics over many words, find that errors correlate only weakly with the number of tokens a word is cut into and more strongly with the length of the word and with how often a letter repeats. The models can recognize the letters, and the difficulty lies in the counting itself. A more accurate statement is therefore that tokenization makes character-level information not directly visible, that item-by-item counting is a weak point of such models anyway, and that the two together produce these errors.

caption.zh: 同样的文本在两种分词器下的切分。每个方框是一个 token。
caption.en: The same texts under two tokenizers. Each box is one token.

title.zh: 为什么切分方式让加法变难
title.en: Why the cutting makes addition hard

source.text: Singh & Strouse, Tokenization counts: the impact of tokenization on arithmetic in frontier LLMs, arXiv:2402.14903

note.zh: 从左往右每三位一切。两个数的前两个 token 完全相同，但它们代表的数量级不同。
note.en: Cutting in threes from the left. The first two tokens of the two numbers are identical but stand for different orders of magnitude.

note.zh: 第一个 token 实际代表多大的数，取决于整个数字的位数 $n$。模型读到 `123` 时还不知道后面有多少位。
note.en: How large a number the first token stands for depends on the total number of digits $n$. When the model reads `123` it does not yet know how many digits follow.

note.zh: 左边是人按右对齐做加法的方式，右边是模型看到的 token。同一列的 token 并不对应相同的数位，进位需要跨越不对齐的片段。
note.en: On the left is how a person adds with right alignment, on the right the tokens the model sees. Tokens in the same column do not correspond to the same place values, and carries have to cross misaligned pieces.

note.zh: 如果用逗号从右往左每三位分隔，token 的边界就与数位对齐了。Singh 和 Strouse 的实验表明，这样做使 GPT-3.5 和 GPT-4 的算术表现明显提高，并且这种差距随模型变大而缩小。
note.en: Separating with commas in threes from the right aligns the token boundaries with the place values. The experiments of Singh and Strouse show that this clearly improves the arithmetic of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, and that the gap shrinks as models grow.

q.zh: 为什么模型数不清单词里有几个字母？
q.en: Why can a model not count the letters in a word?

a.zh: 有两方面的原因。模型看到的是 token 的编号，一个 token 往往包含好几个字母，拼写没有直接写在输入里。另一方面，逐个清点并累加本身就不是这类模型擅长的操作，有研究发现模型能认出单词里有哪些字母，出错主要在计数，尤其是同一个字母出现多次的时候。让模型先把单词逐个字母拼出来再数，或者让它写一行代码来数，通常就能得到正确的结果。
a.en: There are two sides to it. The model sees token ids, a token often contains several letters, and the spelling is not written directly in the input. In addition, going through items one by one and keeping a count is not an operation such models are good at. Some studies find that models can recognize which letters a word contains and that errors arise mainly in counting, especially when a letter occurs several times. Having the model first spell the word letter by letter and then count, or having it write a line of code to count, usually gives the correct result.

q.zh: 为什么模型算不准大数？
q.en: Why does a model get large numbers wrong?

a.zh: 数字被切成与数位不对齐的片段，见上面的推导。另外，模型从左往右生成答案，而加法的进位从右往左传递，写最高位时需要已经知道后面所有位的进位情况。Nogueira 等人的实验表明，数字的书写方式对模型能否学会加减法影响很大，而且模型难以把规则推广到比训练时更长的数字。实际应用中的可靠做法是让模型调用计算器或执行代码，这是 7.3 的内容。
a.en: Numbers are cut into pieces that do not align with the place values, as derived above. Moreover, a model generates the answer from left to right, while carries in addition travel from right to left, so writing the leading digit requires already knowing the carries of all later digits. The experiments of Nogueira and colleagues show that how a number is written strongly affects whether a model can learn addition and subtraction, and that models struggle to extend the rules to numbers longer than those seen in training. The reliable approach in applications is to let the model call a calculator or run code, which is the subject of 7.3.

q.zh: 现在的模型还会犯这些错吗？
q.en: Do current models still make these mistakes?

a.zh: 比早期的模型少得多。较新的模型分词器更好，训练数据中这类任务更多，还可以在回答前先做一段逐步的推理，或者直接调用代码执行工具。但在不使用工具、要求直接给出答案的情况下，字符级任务和长数字运算仍然是相对薄弱的环节。具体到某个模型的表现需要实际测试。
a.en: Far fewer than early models. Newer models have better tokenizers, more of such tasks in their training data, and can reason step by step before answering or call a code-execution tool directly. Yet without tools and when a direct answer is demanded, character-level tasks and long-number arithmetic remain comparatively weak spots. How a specific model performs has to be tested.

q.zh: 为什么同一个问题换个说法，结果会差很多？
q.en: Why does rephrasing a question change the answer so much?

a.zh: 从分词的角度看，这是其中一个原因。大小写、有没有前导空格、是否换行，都会让同一个词变成不同的 token 序列，进入模型的向量也就不同。更主要的原因在于模型是按训练语料的统计规律续写的，不同的措辞对应语料中不同的上下文，这部分在 7.1 讨论。
a.en: From the point of view of tokenization this is one of the reasons. Capitalization, a leading space or a line break turn the same word into a different token sequence, and the vectors entering the model differ accordingly. The more important reason is that a model continues text according to the statistics of its training corpus and different wordings correspond to different contexts in that corpus, which 7.1 discusses.

plain.zh: 设想有人把单词 strawberry 拆开印在三张卡片上递过来，卡片上印的不是字母，而是三个编号。问其中有几个 r，就只能凭以前的经验回忆这几个编号各自对应怎样的拼写。数字也是这样，1234567 被切成 123、456、7 三张卡片，而做加法要从个位对齐，卡片的边界与数位对不上。
plain.en: Imagine the word strawberry handed over split across three cards that show three code numbers and no letters. Asked how many times r occurs, one can only recall from experience what spelling each code stands for. Numbers fare the same. 1234567 is cut into the three cards 123, 456 and 7, while addition has to be aligned from the units digit, and the edges of the cards do not line up with the digits.

summary.zh: 参数怎样从随机数变成有用的权重。看训练数据怎样构造、损失怎样计算、优化器每一步做了什么。
summary.en: How parameters turn from random numbers into useful weights. How training data is built, how the loss is computed and what the optimizer does at each step.

why.zh: 阶段 2 搭好了结构，但刚初始化的模型只会输出均匀的概率，没有任何能力。模型知道的所有事实、掌握的所有语言规律，都来自预训练这一步。预训练的目标只有一个，即预测下一个 token。理解这个目标，才能理解模型为什么会续写、为什么有知识截止时间、为什么会把语料中的错误也学进去。
why.en: Stage 2 built the structure, yet a freshly initialized model outputs uniform probabilities and has no ability at all. Every fact a model knows and every regularity of language it masters comes from pretraining. Pretraining has a single objective, predicting the next token. Understanding this objective is what explains why a model continues text, why it has a knowledge cutoff and why it also learns the errors in its corpus.

goals.zh: 能说明预训练的数据和标签是怎样从原始文本构造的
goals.en: Explain how the data and labels of pretraining are built from raw text

goals.zh: 能写出 AdamW 的更新公式并解释每一项
goals.en: Write the AdamW update and explain every term

goals.zh: 能解释为什么预测下一个 token 可以学到知识
goals.en: Explain why predicting the next token can teach knowledge

explain.zh: **标签从哪里来。** 预训练不需要人工标注。从语料中截取一段长度为 $T+1$ 的 token，前 $T$ 个作为输入，后 $T$ 个作为目标，目标就是输入向后错开一位。这种由数据自身提供标签的方式称为**自监督学习**。因为不需要标注，互联网上的大量文本都可以直接用来训练。
explain.en: **Where the labels come from.** Pretraining needs no human annotation. A span of $T+1$ tokens is cut from the corpus. The first $T$ are the input and the last $T$ the targets, so the target is the input shifted by one position. Supervision that the data provides for itself is called **self-supervised learning**. Since no annotation is needed, vast amounts of text from the internet can be used directly.

explain.zh: **一次前向，$T$ 个训练信号。** 由于因果掩码（2.3），位置 $t$ 的输出只依赖前 $t$ 个 token，所以一段长度为 $T$ 的输入一次前向就给出 $T$ 个预测，每个预测都与真实的下一个 token 比较并计算交叉熵（1.2）。训练时输入的始终是语料中真实的前文，而不是模型自己生成的内容，这种做法称为 **teacher forcing**。
explain.en: **One forward pass, $T$ training signals.** Because of the causal mask (2.3) the output at position $t$ depends only on the first $t$ tokens, so one forward pass over an input of length $T$ gives $T$ predictions, each compared with the true next token through cross-entropy (1.2). During training the input is the real preceding text from the corpus and never the model's own output, a practice called **teacher forcing**.

explain.zh: **为什么这样能学到知识。** 要把 `法国的首都是` 后面的 token 预测对，模型需要以某种形式记住这个事实。要把一段证明的下一步预测对，需要掌握其中的推理模式。要把一篇文章的下一句预测对，需要理解上文。预测得越准，损失越低，梯度下降就会推动参数朝着能够表示这些规律的方向变化。知识并不是被显式地存进去的，而是作为降低预测损失的副产品出现在权重里。
explain.en: **Why this teaches knowledge.** To predict the token after `The capital of France is` correctly, the model has to hold this fact in some form. To predict the next step of a proof, it has to master the pattern of reasoning. To predict the next sentence of an article, it has to understand what came before. The more accurate the prediction, the lower the loss, and gradient descent pushes the parameters towards representing these regularities. Knowledge is not stored explicitly. It appears in the weights as a by-product of lowering the prediction loss.

explain.zh: **优化器。** 有了损失和梯度（1.1），还需要决定每个参数具体挪多少。大模型训练几乎都使用 AdamW。它为每个参数分别记录梯度的滑动平均和梯度平方的滑动平均，用前者除以后者的平方根作为更新方向。这样每个参数的步长被自动归一化，梯度一直很小的参数和梯度很大的参数都能以相近的速度更新。权重衰减则在每一步把参数向 0 拉回一点，起正则化作用。
explain.en: **The optimizer.** With a loss and gradients (1.1) in hand, it remains to decide how far each parameter moves. Large models are trained almost exclusively with AdamW. For every parameter it keeps a running average of the gradient and one of the squared gradient and uses the first divided by the square root of the second as the update direction. The step of each parameter is thereby normalized automatically, so parameters with persistently small gradients and those with large gradients update at similar speeds. Weight decay pulls the parameters a little towards 0 at every step, which acts as regularization.

explain.zh: **学习率的安排。** 学习率通常不是固定的。训练开始时先用几百到几千步从很小的值线性升到最大值，称为预热，之后按余弦曲线逐渐降低。预热的作用是让 Adam 的统计量在最初不稳定的阶段有时间积累，避免一开始就迈出过大的步子。
explain.en: **The learning-rate schedule.** The learning rate is usually not constant. Training starts by raising it linearly from a very small value to the maximum over a few hundred to a few thousand steps, called warm-up, and then lowers it gradually along a cosine curve. Warm-up gives the statistics of Adam time to accumulate during the unstable first phase and avoids overly large steps at the start.

caption.zh: 输入和目标是同一段文本错开一位。每个位置根据它左边的内容预测正下方的目标 token，一次前向得到五个训练信号。
caption.en: Input and target are the same text shifted by one position. Each position predicts the target token directly below it from what is on its left, and one forward pass yields five training signals.

note.zh: 对语料 $\mathcal{D}$ 中的文本片段求平均的逐 token 交叉熵。它就是 1.2 中由最大似然推出的损失，这里只是把数据换成了海量文本。
note.en: The per-token cross-entropy averaged over text spans of the corpus $\mathcal{D}$. It is the loss derived from maximum likelihood in 1.2, now applied to vast amounts of text.

note.zh: 每个训练样本由一段文本错开一位构成，不需要任何额外的标注。
note.en: Each training example is one span of text shifted by one position, with no extra annotation.

note.zh: 实际训练时无法对整个语料求期望，每一步随机取一小批样本估计梯度。$\eta$ 是学习率。下面的 AdamW 是对这个基本更新式的改进。
note.en: The expectation over the whole corpus cannot be computed in practice, so each step estimates the gradient from a small random batch. $\eta$ is the learning rate. AdamW below refines this basic update.

note.zh: 训练开始时模型的预测接近均匀分布，损失约为 $\ln V$。GPT-2 的词表下约为 10.82。这是检查训练代码是否正确的第一个数字。
note.en: At the start of training the predictions are close to uniform and the loss is about $\ln V$, roughly 10.82 for GPT-2's vocabulary. This is the first number to check when verifying training code.

source.text: Loshchilov & Hutter, Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization, arXiv:1711.05101

note.zh: 一阶矩，即梯度 $g_t$ 的指数滑动平均。它平滑了各个 batch 之间的噪声，相当于带惯性的梯度。常用 $\beta_1 = 0.9$。
note.en: The first moment, an exponential moving average of the gradient $g_t$. It smooths the noise between batches and acts as a gradient with momentum. A common value is $\beta_1 = 0.9$.
