a.en: The most probable text is often not the text people consider best. Holtzman and colleagues observed that decoding which maximizes likelihood yields bland, repetitive text, whereas human text does not choose the most likely word at every step. The repetition of greedy decoding is also visible in the output of exercise 2. For tasks such as translation, where the answer is fairly determined, high probability and high quality agree better and beam search remains common. Open-ended generation generally uses sampling with truncation.

q.zh: temperature 和 top-p 应该调哪一个？
q.en: Should temperature or top-p be adjusted?

a.zh: 两者都在控制随机性，但方式不同。温度改变整个分布的形状，top-p 直接去掉尾部。常见的建议是一次只调其中一个，否则两者的作用叠加，不容易判断效果来自哪里。需要稳定、可预期的输出时把温度调低，需要多样性时把温度调高或保持默认。具体的取值与模型有关，应以所用模型的文档为准。
a.en: Both control randomness, in different ways. Temperature changes the shape of the whole distribution, and top-p removes the tail directly. A common recommendation is to adjust only one of them at a time, since their effects otherwise combine and it becomes hard to tell where a change comes from. Lower the temperature for stable, predictable output, and raise it or keep the default for variety. Concrete values depend on the model, and the documentation of the model in use should be followed.

q.zh: 温度、top-k、top-p 同时设置时按什么顺序生效？
q.en: In what order do temperature, top-k and top-p apply when all are set?

a.zh: 常见的实现是先除以温度，再做 top-k，再做 top-p，然后归一化并采样，练习 1 采用的就是这个顺序。顺序会影响结果，因为温度改变了概率，top-p 保留的集合也随之改变。不同的库和服务在细节上可能不同。
a.en: A common implementation divides by the temperature first, then applies top-k, then top-p, and then normalizes and samples, which is the order used in exercise 1. The order affects the result, since temperature changes the probabilities and with them the set that top-p keeps. Libraries and services may differ in the details.

q.zh: seed 参数的作用是什么？
q.en: What does the seed parameter do?

a.zh: 采样需要随机数，seed 固定了随机数序列的起点。在本地运行时，相同的 seed、相同的模型和相同的环境会得到相同的采样结果，练习中的 `torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)` 就是这个作用。它只控制采样这一步的随机性，不能消除前面所说的数值差别，所以在线服务上固定 seed 也只能做到尽量一致。
a.en: Sampling needs random numbers, and the seed fixes the starting point of the random sequence. Run locally, the same seed, the same model and the same environment give the same sampled result, which is what `torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)` does in the exercises. It controls only the randomness of the sampling step and cannot remove the numerical differences described above, so fixing the seed on an online service achieves consistency only on a best-effort basis.

plain.zh: 模型在每一步给出的是一个各张奖券权重不同的抽奖箱。贪心解码每次都拿权重最大的那一张，结果稳定，却容易来回说同样的话。采样是真的去抽。温度相当于在抽之前调整各张奖券之间的差距，温度低时大奖更突出，温度高时各张更接近。top-k 和 top-p 是在抽之前先把明显不靠谱的小奖券扔掉。
plain.en: At every step the model presents a lottery box in which the tickets carry different weights. Greedy decoding takes the heaviest ticket every time, which is stable and tends to say the same thing over and over. Sampling really draws. The temperature adjusts the gaps between the tickets before the draw, making the top prize stand out more when low and the tickets more alike when high. Top-k and top-p throw away the clearly implausible small tickets before the draw.

summary.zh: 生成时怎样避免重复计算，推理为什么分成两个阶段，以及首 token 延迟和生成速度各由什么决定。
summary.en: How repeated computation is avoided during generation, why inference has two phases, and what determines time to first token and generation speed.

why.zh: 按照 0.1 中的写法，每生成一个 token 都要把整个序列重新算一遍，生成的长度翻倍，计算量会增加到数倍。实际的推理系统都使用 KV cache 来避免这种重复，它是大模型能够以可接受的速度逐字输出的前提。推理因此分成处理提示词和逐个生成两个阶段，两个阶段的计算特点不同。使用大模型时常见的几个现象，包括输出逐字出现、长提示词使回答开始得更慢、输出 token 的定价高于输入 token，都可以由这一机制解释。
why.en: Written as in 0.1, generating each token recomputes the whole sequence, and doubling the generated length multiplies the computation several times. Practical inference systems all use a KV cache to avoid this repetition, and it is a precondition for large models to produce text at an acceptable speed. Inference thereby splits into two phases, processing the prompt and generating token by token, with different computational characteristics. Several familiar observations about using large models, including text appearing piece by piece, long prompts delaying the start of an answer and output tokens being priced above input tokens, can be explained by this mechanism.

goals.zh: 能解释为什么缓存键和值不会改变结果
goals.en: Explain why caching keys and values does not change the result

goals.zh: 能比较有无缓存时的计算量并估算缓存占用的内存
goals.en: Compare the computation with and without the cache and estimate the memory the cache takes

goals.zh: 能说明首 token 延迟和生成速度分别由什么决定
goals.en: State what determines time to first token and generation speed

explain.zh: **重复在哪里。** 生成第 101 个 token 时，模型要对前 100 个 token 做一次完整的前向计算。生成第 102 个 token 时，又要对 101 个 token 再算一遍，其中前 100 个位置上的计算与上一次完全相同。原因在于因果掩码。每个位置只能看到它之前的 token，后面追加了什么并不影响它在任何一层的表示。
explain.en: **Where the repetition is.** To generate token 101 the model runs a full forward pass over the first 100 tokens. To generate token 102 it runs over 101 tokens again, and the computation at the first 100 positions is exactly that of the previous pass. The reason is the causal mask. Every position sees only the tokens before it, and whatever is appended later does not affect its representation in any layer.

explain.zh: **缓存什么。** 新 token 在每一层的注意力中，需要用自己的查询向量与所有先前位置的键做点积，再对它们的值做加权求和。先前位置的键和值不会再变，可以保存下来。于是每一步只需要让最新的一个 token 通过模型，计算它自己的查询、键和值，把键和值追加到缓存里。查询不需要缓存，因为旧位置的查询以后不会再用到。
explain.en: **What is cached.** In the attention of every layer the new token takes dot products of its own query vector with the keys of all earlier positions and forms a weighted sum of their values. The keys and values of earlier positions no longer change and can be stored. Each step then passes only the newest token through the model, computes its own query, key and value, and appends the key and value to the cache. Queries need not be cached, since the queries of old positions are never used again.

explain.zh: **两个阶段。** 提示词中的所有 token 都是已知的，可以在一次前向计算中并行处理，同时把缓存填满，这个阶段叫 prefill。之后的每个输出 token 都依赖于前一个输出，只能一个一个地算，这个阶段叫 decode。从发出请求到看到第一个 token 的时间叫首 token 延迟，它主要取决于 prefill，随提示词变长而增加。此后的速度用每秒生成的 token 数衡量，它取决于 decode 每一步的耗时。
explain.en: **Two phases.** All tokens of the prompt are known and can be processed in parallel in one forward pass that also fills the cache, a phase called prefill. Every output token after that depends on the previous output and can only be computed one at a time, a phase called decode. The time from sending a request to seeing the first token is the time to first token, which depends mainly on prefill and grows with the length of the prompt. The speed afterwards is measured in tokens generated per second and depends on the time of one decode step.

explain.zh: **一次实际的测量。** 练习 2 在 CPU 上用 GPT-2 测量。提示词从 50 个 token 增加到 800 个时，首 token 延迟从约 0.1 秒增加到约 1.1 秒。提示词为 800 个 token 时，不使用缓存的生成速度约为每秒 0.8 个 token，使用缓存后约为每秒 21 个，两种方式生成的 token 完全相同。使用缓存时，生成速度受提示词长度的影响很小。具体数值与机器有关，趋势是稳定的。
explain.en: **An actual measurement.** Exercise 2 measures with GPT-2 on a CPU. As the prompt grows from 50 to 800 tokens, the time to first token rises from about 0.1 to about 1.1 seconds. With a prompt of 800 tokens, generation runs at about 0.8 tokens per second without the cache and about 21 with it, and both ways produce exactly the same tokens. With the cache, the generation speed depends little on the length of the prompt. The concrete numbers depend on the machine, and the trend is stable.

explain.zh: **代价是内存。** 缓存要为每一层、每一个位置保存一个键向量和一个值向量。GPT-2 small 在 1024 个 token 时约占 75 MB。对于层数更多、维度更大、上下文更长的模型，一个序列的缓存可以达到几个 GB。在线服务要同时处理许多请求，缓存占用的显存因此成为能同时服务多少请求的主要限制之一。vLLM 等推理系统的一项核心工作就是更有效地管理这部分内存。
explain.en: **The price is memory.** The cache stores one key vector and one value vector for every layer and every position. For GPT-2 small at 1024 tokens this is about 75 MB. For models with more layers, larger dimensions and longer contexts the cache of one sequence can reach several GB. An online service handles many requests at once, so the memory taken by caches becomes one of the main limits on how many requests can be served simultaneously. A core task of inference systems such as vLLM is to manage this memory more efficiently.

caption.zh: 连续三步生成中各个位置的计算情况。没有缓存时，每一步都重新计算所有位置。有缓存时，每一步只计算最新的一个位置，其余位置的键和值从缓存中读取。
caption.en: What is computed at each position during three consecutive steps of generation. Without the cache every step recomputes all positions. With the cache every step computes only the newest position, and the keys and values of the others are read from the cache.

title.zh: 缓存为什么不改变结果
title.en: Why the cache does not change the result

note.zh: 因果掩码使第 $\ell$ 层第 $i$ 个位置的表示只依赖于前一层中位置 $1$ 到 $i$ 的表示。
note.en: The causal mask makes the representation of position $i$ in layer $\ell$ depend only on the representations of positions $1$ to $i$ in the layer below.

steps.tex: h_i^{(\ell)} \text{ depends only on } x_1, \dots, x_i \quad \text{for every layer } \ell

note.zh: 对层数做归纳即可得到。第 0 层是 token 嵌入加位置编码，只依赖 $x_i$ 本身和它的位置。在序列末尾追加新的 token，不会改变任何已有位置在任何一层的表示。
note.en: This follows by induction over the layers. Layer 0 is the token embedding plus the positional encoding and depends only on $x_i$ itself and its position. Appending new tokens at the end changes the representation of no existing position in any layer.

steps.tex: k_i^{(\ell)} = W_K^{(\ell)}\, \tilde h_i^{(\ell-1)},\qquad v_i^{(\ell)} = W_V^{(\ell)}\, \tilde h_i^{(\ell-1)}

note.zh: 键和值是该位置表示的线性变换（$\tilde h$ 表示经过归一化之后），因此同样不会再变，可以只算一次。
note.en: Keys and values are linear maps of the representation of the position ($\tilde h$ denotes the representation after normalization), so they do not change either and can be computed once.

note.zh: 新位置 $t$ 的注意力输出。它用到新算出的 $q_t$、$k_t$、$v_t$ 以及缓存中的 $k_{1:t-1}$、$v_{1:t-1}$。这里不需要掩码，因为缓存里只有过去的位置。
note.en: The attention output of the new position $t$. It uses the newly computed $q_t$, $k_t$, $v_t$ and the cached $k_{1:t-1}$, $v_{1:t-1}$. No mask is needed here, since the cache contains only past positions.

title.en: Computation with and without the cache

note.zh: 2.6 中得到的结果，一层 Transformer 对长度为 $t$ 的序列做一次前向计算的乘法次数。
note.en: The result of 2.6, the number of multiplications of one Transformer layer in one forward pass over a sequence of length $t$.

steps.tex: \text{no cache:}\quad \sum_{t=1}^{T} c(t) \approx 6\, T^{2} d^{2} + \tfrac{2}{3}\, T^{3} d

note.zh: 没有缓存时，生成到长度 $T$ 需要对长度 $1, 2, \dots, T$ 各做一次完整的前向计算。
note.en: Without the cache, generating up to length $T$ takes one full forward pass at each of the lengths $1, 2, \dots, T$.

steps.tex: \text{cache:}\quad \sum_{t=1}^{T} \big( 12\, d^{2} + 2\, t\, d \big) \approx 12\, T d^{2} + T^{2} d

note.zh: 有缓存时，每一步只处理一个位置。前馈层和各个投影的代价是 $12 d^2$，注意力只需要一个查询与 $t$ 个键、值运算，代价是 $2td$。
note.en: With the cache, every step processes one position. The feed-forward layer and the projections cost $12 d^2$, and attention needs only one query against $t$ keys and values, costing $2td$.

note.zh: 代入 GPT-2 small 的维度。缓存把生成 1000 个 token 的总计算量降到约五百分之一，比值大致为 $T/2$。这等于处理一次长度为 $T$ 的序列的代价，即有缓存的生成与一次完整的前向计算做的是同样多的运算。
note.en: With the dimension of GPT-2 small. The cache reduces the total computation of generating 1000 tokens to about one five-hundredth, a ratio of roughly $T/2$. The cached total equals the cost of processing one sequence of length $T$ once, so generation with the cache performs as many operations as a single full forward pass.

title.en: The memory taken by the cache

note.zh: 每一层、每一个位置保存一个键和一个值，各有 $d$ 个数（$n_{\text{head}} \times d_{\text{head}}$），每个数占 $b$ 个字节。
note.en: Every layer and every position stores one key and one value of $d$ numbers each ($n_{\text{head}} \times d_{\text{head}}$), with $b$ bytes per number.

note.zh: 练习 2 中把这个公式与实际缓存中张量的大小做了比较，两者完全一致。
note.en: Exercise 2 compares this formula with the sizes of the tensors in the actual cache, and the two agree exactly.

note.zh: 一个假设的较大模型在 16 位精度下，单个序列的缓存大小。许多较新的模型让多个注意力头共用一组键和值（分组查询注意力），缓存会按相应的比例减小。
note.en: The cache of a single sequence for a hypothetical larger model at 16-bit precision. Many newer models let several attention heads share one set of keys and values (grouped-query attention), which shrinks the cache by the corresponding factor.

q.zh: 为什么输出是一个 token 一个 token 返回的？
q.en: Why is output returned token by token?

a.zh: 因为它就是这样算出来的。每个输出 token 都要等前一个 token 确定之后才能计算，无法并行。服务端每算出一个 token 就立即发送给用户，这种方式叫流式输出。它不会让总时间变短，但用户可以在生成的同时开始阅读，等待的感受取决于首 token 延迟，不取决于总时间。
a.en: Because that is how it is computed. Every output token can be computed only after the previous one is fixed, and this cannot be parallelized. The server sends each token to the user as soon as it is computed, which is called streaming. It does not shorten the total time, but the user can begin reading while generation continues, and the perceived wait depends on the time to first token and not on the total time.

q.zh: 为什么输出 token 通常比输入 token 贵？
q.en: Why do output tokens usually cost more than input tokens?

a.zh: 从计算上看，输入 token 可以在一次前向计算中并行处理，硬件的利用率高。输出 token 必须逐个生成，每个都要单独做一次前向计算，并且在整个生成过程中一直占用缓存所需的显存。同样数量的 token，生成所占用的硬件时间明显更多。截至 2026 年 11 月，Anthropic 的定价页上各个模型的输出单价均为输入单价的 5 倍。需要说明的是，定价还受到商业因素的影响，计算成本只是其中一个原因。
a.en: Computationally, input tokens can be processed in parallel in one forward pass, which uses hardware efficiently. Output tokens must be generated one by one, each with its own forward pass, and the memory for the cache stays occupied throughout generation. For the same number of tokens, generation takes clearly more hardware time. As of November 2026 the pricing page of Anthropic lists an output price of 5 times the input price for every model. It should be added that pricing is also shaped by commercial considerations, and computational cost is only one of the reasons.

q.zh: 为什么提示词越长，回答开始得越慢？
q.en: Why does a longer prompt delay the start of the answer?

a.zh: 第一个输出 token 出现之前，模型要先完成 prefill，即对整个提示词做一次前向计算。这一步的计算量随提示词长度增长，其中注意力部分随长度的平方增长。在练习 2 的测量中，提示词从 50 个 token 增加到 800 个，首 token 延迟增加到约 10 倍。提示词缓存可以减轻这个问题。
a.en: Before the first output token appears the model must finish prefill, one forward pass over the whole prompt. The computation of this step grows with the length of the prompt, the attention part with its square. In the measurement of exercise 2 the time to first token grows about tenfold as the prompt goes from 50 to 800 tokens. Prompt caching can ease this.

q.zh: 提示词缓存和 KV cache 是一回事吗？
q.en: Is prompt caching the same as the KV cache?

a.zh: 两者基于同一个原理，作用范围不同。KV cache 在一次请求之内避免重复计算。提示词缓存是服务商提供的功能，它把一段提示词前缀的计算结果保留一段时间，后续请求如果以完全相同的前缀开头，就可以跳过这部分的 prefill。Anthropic 的文档说明，缓存要求前缀的内容完全一致，默认保留 5 分钟，读取缓存的价格是普通输入价格的十分之一或更低。要求前缀完全一致的原因正是因果性。前面的内容只要改动一处，后面所有位置的键和值都会变。因此应当把固定不变的内容（系统提示词、工具定义、长文档）放在前面，把每次变化的内容放在后面。
a.en: Both rest on the same principle and differ in scope. The KV cache avoids repeated computation within one request. Prompt caching is a feature offered by providers that keeps the computed results of a prompt prefix for some time, so that later requests starting with exactly the same prefix can skip that part of prefill. The documentation of Anthropic states that caching requires the prefix to be identical, that entries are kept for 5 minutes by default, and that reading from the cache costs one tenth of the normal input price or less. The reason an identical prefix is required is causality itself. One change anywhere earlier changes the keys and values of all later positions. Content that stays fixed (system prompt, tool definitions, long documents) should therefore come first and content that changes with every request last.

q.zh: 为什么只缓存键和值，不缓存查询？
q.en: Why are only keys and values cached and not queries?

a.zh: 查询只在计算它所属位置的输出时使用一次。旧位置的输出已经算完，它们的查询以后不会再被用到。键和值则不同，以后每一个新位置都要用自己的查询去与所有旧位置的键比较，并读取它们的值。
a.en: A query is used once, when the output of its own position is computed. The outputs of old positions are finished and their queries are never needed again. Keys and values are different. Every later position compares its own query with the keys of all old positions and reads their values.

q.zh: 使用缓存会改变输出吗？
q.en: Does using the cache change the output?

a.zh: 数学上不会，上面的推导说明两种算法计算的是同一个量。练习 1 中两者的 logits 在 $10^{-5}$ 的容差内一致，练习 2 中两者生成的 token 完全相同。由于运算顺序不同，两者的浮点结果可能有极微小的差别，这正是 5.1 中讨论的那类数值差别。
a.en: Mathematically it does not, and the derivation above shows that both procedures compute the same quantity. In exercise 1 the logits of the two agree within a tolerance of $10^{-5}$, and in exercise 2 the generated tokens are identical. Because the order of operations differs, the floating-point results of the two may differ very slightly, which is exactly the kind of numerical difference discussed in 5.1.

q.zh: 训练时也使用 KV cache 吗？
q.en: Is the KV cache also used in training?

a.zh: 不使用。训练时整个序列是已知的，一次前向计算就能并行地得到所有位置的预测（见 4.1 的 teacher forcing），不存在逐步生成造成的重复计算。Hugging Face 的文档也说明缓存只应在推理时使用。
a.en: No. In training the whole sequence is known and one forward pass yields the predictions at all positions in parallel (see teacher forcing in 4.1), so the repetition caused by step-by-step generation does not arise. The Hugging Face documentation likewise states that the cache should be used only for inference.

plain.zh: 像写一篇长文章。没有缓存时，每写一个新词都要把全文从头重读一遍。有了缓存，相当于对读过的每一段都做了笔记，写新词时只查笔记就够了。prefill 是动笔之前把题目和材料读一遍并做好笔记，所以材料越长，动笔越晚。decode 是一个词一个词地往下写。
plain.en: It is like writing a long essay. Without the cache the whole text is reread from the start for every new word. With the cache, notes have been taken on every passage read, and consulting the notes suffices for writing a new word. Prefill is reading the task and the material and taking notes before starting to write, so the longer the material, the later the writing begins. Decode is writing on word by word.

title.zh: 结构化输出与约束解码

summary.zh: 用状态机在每一步屏蔽不合法的 token，使输出保证符合给定的格式。
summary.en: Mask illegal tokens at every step with a state machine, so that the output is guaranteed to follow a given format.

why.zh: 程序调用大模型时，通常需要把输出交给代码继续处理，例如解析成 JSON、作为函数调用的参数。模型的输出是逐个 token 采样得到的文本，没有任何机制保证它恰好是合法的 JSON。少一个引号或多一句解释，下游程序就会出错。约束解码从生成过程本身解决这个问题，在每一步只允许选择不破坏格式的 token。它是各家 API 中结构化输出功能的基础，也是 7.3 中工具调用能够可靠工作的前提之一。
why.en: When a program calls a large model, the output usually has to be handed to code for further processing, for example parsed as JSON or used as the arguments of a function call. The output of a model is text sampled token by token, and no mechanism guarantees that it happens to be valid JSON. One missing quote or one extra sentence of explanation makes the downstream program fail. Constrained decoding solves this within the generation process itself by allowing, at every step, only tokens that do not break the format. It underlies the structured-output features of the various APIs and is one precondition for tool calling in 7.3 to work reliably.

goals.zh: 能解释约束解码怎样在采样之前屏蔽 token
goals.en: Explain how constrained decoding masks tokens before sampling

goals.zh: 能把一个简单的 JSON Schema 编译成字符级的状态机
goals.en: Compile a simple JSON Schema into a character-level state machine

goals.zh: 能区分约束解码保证的内容和不保证的内容
goals.en: Tell apart what constrained decoding guarantees and what it does not

explain.zh: **问题。** 让模型输出 JSON 的最简单办法是在提示词里提出要求并给出例子。这样做在多数情况下有效，但只是提高了概率。OpenAI 在介绍结构化输出时给出过一组数字。在其复杂 JSON 模式的评测中，仅靠模型本身的能力，较新的模型达到 93%，加上约束解码后达到 100%。对一个每天调用上百万次的程序来说，7% 的失败率是不可接受的。
explain.en: **The problem.** The simplest way to get JSON from a model is to ask for it in the prompt and give examples. This works in most cases, but it only raises a probability. OpenAI gave a set of numbers when introducing structured outputs. In its evaluation with complex JSON schemas a newer model reached 93% by its own ability and 100% once constrained decoding was added. For a program that makes a million calls a day, a failure rate of 7% is unacceptable.

explain.zh: **做法。** 约束解码不改变模型，只在 5.1 所说的选择环节增加一步。用一个状态机记录当前已经输出到格式的哪个位置。每一步先由状态机给出此刻允许的 token 集合，把其余 token 的 logit 设为负无穷，再照常做贪心或采样。被屏蔽的 token 概率为 0，无论如何不会被选中。选出 token 之后，状态机前进到新的状态。
explain.en: **The method.** Constrained decoding leaves the model unchanged and adds one step to the selection stage described in 5.1. A state machine records which point of the format the output has reached. At every step the state machine first provides the set of tokens allowed at this moment, the logits of all other tokens are set to minus infinity, and greedy decoding or sampling proceeds as usual. Masked tokens have probability 0 and cannot be chosen under any circumstances. After a token is chosen, the state machine advances to a new state.

explain.zh: **字符与 token 的对应。** 格式是按字符定义的，模型输出的却是 token，一个 token 往往包含多个字符。判断一个 token 是否允许，要把它的每个字符依次送进状态机，全部能走通才算允许。词表有几万个 token，每一步都这样检查会很慢。Willard 和 Louf 提出的办法是预先为状态机的每个状态算好允许的 token 集合并建立索引，生成时直接查表。练习 1 用按状态缓存的方式实现了同样的思路。
explain.en: **Characters and tokens.** A format is defined over characters, whereas a model outputs tokens, and one token often contains several characters. To decide whether a token is allowed, each of its characters is fed to the state machine in turn, and the token is allowed only if all of them can be followed. The vocabulary has tens of thousands of tokens, and checking them like this at every step would be slow. The approach proposed by Willard and Louf is to compute the allowed token set of every state of the state machine in advance and build an index, so that generation only looks it up. Exercise 1 implements the same idea by caching per state.

explain.zh: **从 JSON Schema 到状态机。** JSON Schema 是描述 JSON 数据结构的标准写法，规定有哪些字段、各是什么类型。练习 2 把它的一个小子集编译成状态机。固定的文本（括号、字段名）对应一串依次相连的状态。枚举值对应一棵前缀树。整数和字符串对应带长度上限的一串状态。实际系统支持嵌套的对象和数组，嵌套的层数不固定时，有限状态机不够用，需要上下文无关文法，原理仍然是每一步计算允许的 token 集合。
explain.en: **From JSON Schema to a state machine.** JSON Schema is the standard notation for describing the structure of JSON data, specifying which fields exist and what type each has. Exercise 2 compiles a small subset of it into a state machine. Fixed text (braces, field names) becomes a chain of consecutive states. Enumerated values become a prefix tree. Integers and strings become a chain of states with an upper bound on length. Practical systems support nested objects and arrays. When the depth of nesting is not fixed a finite-state machine is not enough and a context-free grammar is needed, while the principle of computing the allowed token set at every step stays the same.

explain.zh: **保证了什么，没有保证什么。** 练习 3 在 GPT-2 上比较了四种设置，每种 8 条评论。没有例子也没有约束时，格式错误率是 100%。加上约束后，格式错误率是 0%，但情感判断的正确率只有 50%，与随机猜测相同。约束保证的是输出符合格式，它不能让模型知道原本不知道的答案。练习 1 中也有同样的现象，被限制为只能回答 yes 或 no 的 GPT-2 对“月亮是奶酪做的吗”回答了 yes。另一方面，在提示词中给出两个例子后，这 8 条输出即使不加约束也都符合格式，正确率也有所提高。样本只有 8 条，这些百分比只能说明方向。合理的理解是，提示词负责让模型理解任务，约束负责在格式上兜底，两者配合使用。
explain.en: **What is guaranteed and what is not.** Exercise 3 compares four settings on GPT-2 with 8 reviews each. With neither examples nor constraints the format error rate is 100%. With constraints the format error rate is 0%, but the sentiment is correct in only 50% of cases, the same as random guessing. The constraint guarantees that the output follows the format, and it cannot make the model know an answer it did not know. The same appears in exercise 1, where a GPT-2 restricted to answering yes or no answers yes to whether the Moon is made of cheese. On the other hand, with two examples in the prompt all 8 outputs follow the format even without constraints, and correctness improves as well. With only 8 samples these percentages indicate no more than a direction. A reasonable reading is that the prompt makes the model understand the task and the constraint serves as a backstop for the format, and the two are used together.

caption.zh: 约束解码的一步。状态机根据当前状态给出允许的 token，其余 token 的 logit 被设为负无穷，然后照常选择。图中的状态机只接受 yes 或 no。
caption.en: One step of constrained decoding. The state machine provides the tokens allowed in the current state, the logits of the others are set to minus infinity, and selection proceeds as usual. The state machine shown accepts only yes or no.

source.text: Willard & Louf, Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models, arXiv:2307.09702

note.zh: 状态 $s$ 下允许的 token 集合。$\delta^{*}$ 表示从状态 $s$ 出发依次读入 token $v$ 的每个字符，能够走通的 token 才被允许。
note.en: The set of tokens allowed in state $s$. $\delta^{*}$ denotes reading the characters of token $v$ one after another starting from state $s$, and only tokens for which this succeeds are allowed.

note.zh: 掩码。不允许的 token 的 logit 被设为负无穷。
note.en: The mask. The logits of tokens that are not allowed are set to minus infinity.

note.zh: 对掩码后的 logits 做 softmax 得到的分布。它与 top-k、top-p 的形式完全相同，区别只在于保留哪些 token 是由格式决定的，而不是由概率决定的。
note.en: The distribution obtained by a softmax over the masked logits. It has exactly the form of top-k and top-p, the only difference being that the tokens to keep are determined by the format and not by the probabilities.

steps.tex: \text{index: } s \mapsto A(s) \ \text{ computed once},\qquad \text{per step: one lookup}

note.zh: 预先为每个状态计算 $A(s)$，代价与状态数乘以词表大小成正比，只需做一次。生成时每一步只查一次表，开销与词表大小无关。各家 API 文档中提到的“首次使用某个模式时有额外延迟”就来自这一步预计算。
note.en: $A(s)$ is computed for every state in advance, at a cost proportional to the number of states times the vocabulary size, and only once. During generation every step is a single lookup whose cost does not depend on the vocabulary size. The extra latency on first use of a schema mentioned in the documentation of the various APIs comes from this precomputation.

note.zh: 一个两步的例子。第一个 token 是 A 或 B。选 A 之后，模型原本只有 10% 的概率续写出合法的输出。选 B 之后，所有续写都合法。
note.en: A two-step example. The first token is A or B. After A the model would originally continue with a valid output with a probability of only 10%. After B every continuation is valid.

note.zh: 如果把模型原来的分布限制在合法输出上（相当于反复采样直到得到合法输出），以 A 开头的比例是 13%。
note.en: If the original distribution of the model is restricted to valid outputs (equivalent to sampling repeatedly until a valid output appears), the share starting with A is 13%.

note.zh: 约束解码在第一步不会屏蔽 A，因为 A 之后仍然存在合法的续写。于是它以 60% 的概率选 A，然后在第二步强制模型走进它原本很少走的那 10%。逐步屏蔽只看当前这一步是否还有路可走，不考虑后面的路在模型看来有多大的可能。
note.en: Constrained decoding does not mask A at the first step, since valid continuations after A still exist. It therefore chooses A with a probability of 60% and at the second step forces the model into the 10% it would rarely have taken. Step-wise masking considers only whether some path remains at the current step, and not how likely the later path is in the eyes of the model.

note.zh: 一般的写法。$Z_t$ 是每一步允许的 token 的概率之和，它随前缀而变，所以两者一般不相等。这可以解释约束有时会使输出质量下降的现象，也说明提示词仍然重要。提示词把格式说清楚之后，模型本来就倾向于合法的续写，$Z_t$ 接近 1，这种偏差就很小。
note.en: The general form. $Z_t$ is the total probability of the tokens allowed at each step and varies with the prefix, so the two are in general unequal. This can explain why constraints sometimes lower output quality and also shows that the prompt still matters. Once the prompt makes the format clear, the model already favours valid continuations, $Z_t$ is close to 1 and the deviation is small.

q.zh: 为什么输出的 JSON 有时格式不对？
q.en: Why is output JSON sometimes malformed?

a.zh: 因为在没有约束的情况下，JSON 的格式只是模型从训练数据中学到的一种统计规律，并不是生成过程中的硬性规则。每一步都是从概率分布中选择，即使每一步出错的概率很小，较长的输出累积起来也会有可观的出错机会。常见的错误包括漏掉引号或括号、在 JSON 前后添加解释性的文字、字段名或类型与要求不符，以及输出因达到长度上限而被截断。
a.en: Because without constraints the format of JSON is merely a statistical regularity the model learned from training data and not a hard rule of the generation process. Every step is a choice from a probability distribution, and even if the chance of an error per step is small, a longer output accumulates a considerable chance of going wrong. Common errors include missing quotes or brackets, explanatory text before or after the JSON, field names or types that deviate from the requirement, and output cut off at the length limit.

q.zh: 怎样保证格式正确？
q.en: How can a correct format be guaranteed?

a.zh: 使用约束解码，即所用 API 的结构化输出功能，或者在本地模型上使用 Outlines、llama.cpp 的文法等工具。它在每一步屏蔽会破坏格式的 token，输出在构造上就符合给定的模式。只在提示词中提出要求，或者解析失败后重试，都只能降低出错的概率。仍需注意两种例外。输出达到最大长度时会被截断，得到不完整的 JSON。模型拒绝回答时，返回的内容也可能不符合模式。OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的文档都列出了这两种情况，代码中应当检查停止原因。
a.en: Use constrained decoding, that is, the structured-output feature of the API in use, or tools such as Outlines or the grammars of llama.cpp for local models. It masks tokens that would break the format at every step, so the output conforms to the given schema by construction. Asking in the prompt alone, or retrying after a failed parse, only lowers the probability of errors. Two exceptions still need attention. Output that reaches the maximum length is cut off and leaves incomplete JSON. When the model refuses to answer, the returned content may not conform to the schema either. The documentation of both OpenAI and Anthropic lists these two cases, and code should check the stop reason.

q.zh: 格式正确是否意味着内容正确？
q.en: Does a correct format mean correct content?

a.zh: 不意味着。约束只限定输出的形式。字段的值是否正确，仍然取决于模型本身和提示词。练习 3 中，加上约束的 GPT-2 输出了格式完全正确的 JSON，其中的情感判断有一半是错的。OpenAI 的文档也指出，结构化输出不能防止合法 JSON 中出现错误的值。因此对内容的校验和评估仍然是必要的。
a.en: It does not. A constraint restricts only the form of the output. Whether the values of the fields are right still depends on the model itself and on the prompt. In exercise 3 the constrained GPT-2 produces JSON in a perfectly correct format in which half of the sentiment judgements are wrong. The documentation of OpenAI likewise notes that structured outputs do not prevent wrong values inside valid JSON. Validating and evaluating the content therefore remains necessary.

q.zh: 约束解码会降低输出质量吗？
q.en: Does constrained decoding lower output quality?

a.zh: 有可能，取决于用法。Tam 等人的研究发现，要求模型以 JSON 等结构化格式输出时，推理类任务的表现比自由回答时明显下降，并且格式限制越严，下降越多。上面第二个推导给出了一种机制上的解释，即逐步屏蔽会把模型推到它原本不太会走的路径上。实践中常见的缓解办法有两种。一是在模式中把用于推理的字段放在答案字段之前，让模型先写出推理过程。二是分两步进行，先让模型自由作答，再把答案整理成结构化的格式。这些做法的效果与任务和模型有关，需要在自己的数据上验证。
a.en: It can, depending on how it is used. The study of Tam and colleagues found that requiring models to answer in structured formats such as JSON lowers performance on reasoning tasks noticeably compared with free-form answers, and the more so the stricter the format restriction. The second derivation above offers a mechanistic explanation, namely that step-wise masking pushes the model onto paths it would rarely have taken. Two mitigations are common in practice. One is to place a field for reasoning before the answer field in the schema, so that the model writes out its reasoning first. The other is to proceed in two steps, letting the model answer freely and then arranging the answer into the structured format. How well these work depends on the task and the model and has to be checked on one's own data.

q.zh: JSON 模式和结构化输出有什么区别？
q.en: How do JSON mode and structured outputs differ?

a.zh: 按照 OpenAI 的说明，JSON 模式提高了输出是合法 JSON 的可能性，但不保证它符合某个特定的模式，例如字段可能缺失或类型不对。结构化输出则要求输出与开发者提供的 JSON Schema 一致，是通过把模式转换成文法并做约束解码实现的。不同服务商的功能名称和支持范围不同，使用前应查阅当前的文档。
a.en: According to OpenAI, JSON mode raises the likelihood that the output is valid JSON without guaranteeing that it matches a particular schema, so fields may be missing or of the wrong type. Structured outputs require the output to agree with the JSON Schema supplied by the developer and are implemented by converting the schema into a grammar and decoding under constraints. Feature names and the range of support differ between providers, and the current documentation should be consulted before use.

q.zh: 为什么只支持 JSON Schema 的一部分？
q.en: Why is only part of JSON Schema supported?

a.zh: 因为模式要被编译成可以逐 token 检查的文法，而 JSON Schema 中有些约束很难这样表达。例如“数值不小于 100”或“两个字段的值必须相等”，无法简单地转换成逐字符的规则。各家文档都列出了不支持的关键字。练习 2 中的编译器只支持四种取值类型，并且要求字段按固定顺序出现，原因是相同的。对于文法无法表达的约束，仍然需要在得到输出之后用代码校验。
a.en: Because the schema has to be compiled into a grammar that can be checked token by token, and some constraints of JSON Schema are hard to express that way. A value of at least 100, or two fields that must be equal, cannot be converted simply into character-level rules. The documentation of each provider lists the keywords that are not supported. The compiler of exercise 2 supports only four kinds of values and requires the fields in a fixed order for the same reason. Constraints a grammar cannot express still have to be validated in code after the output is obtained.

plain.zh: 像填一张格式固定的表单。出生日期一栏只能点选数字，根本没有输入字母的按键，所以无论怎样填，格式都不会错。约束解码就是在每一步把此刻不合法的 token 的按键禁用。但表单只能保证格式。在合法的日期栏里，仍然可以填进一个错误的生日。
plain.en: It is like filling in a form with a fixed format. The date of birth field accepts digits alone and offers no key for letters, so the format cannot go wrong however the form is filled in. Constrained decoding disables at every step the keys of the tokens that are not valid at that moment. A form guarantees the format alone, though. A wrong birthday can still be entered in a valid date field.

summary.zh: 通过 API 使用和下载权重自己运行有什么区别，怎样读懂一个模型的名称和规模，以及量化怎样让大模型装进有限的内存。
summary.en: How using an API differs from downloading weights and running them, how to read the name and size of a model, and how quantization fits a large model into limited memory.

asof.zh: 本模块中关于具体模型和许可证的信息截至 2026 年 11 月 25 日，取自各模型在 Hugging Face Hub 上的页面和许可证原文。这类信息变化较快，使用前请以官方页面为准。
asof.en: Information about specific models and licenses in this module is as of 25 November 2026 and taken from the model pages on the Hugging Face Hub and the license texts. Such information changes quickly, and the official pages should be checked before use.

why.zh: 前面各阶段讲的是一个模型内部怎样工作。实际使用时首先要决定用哪一个模型，以及以什么方式使用。可选的模型很多，更新也很快，但需要判断的问题比较固定，包括能否拿到权重、模型有多大、手头的硬件能否运行、精度降低后还剩多少能力。这些判断依赖于前面学过的参数量和计算量的知识。对机制分析的研究而言还有一层含义，阶段 9 的方法都需要读取模型内部的激活值，只有拿得到权重的模型才能做。
why.en: The earlier stages describe how one model works inside. In practice the first decision is which model to use and in what way. The choice is wide and changes quickly, yet the questions to be judged are fairly stable, including whether the weights are available, how large the model is, whether the hardware at hand can run it and how much ability remains at reduced precision. These judgements rest on what was learned earlier about parameter counts and computation. For research on mechanisms there is a further point. The methods of stage 9 all need to read the internal activations of a model, which is possible only for models whose weights are available.

goals.zh: 能说明通过 API 使用模型与持有权重在能做的事情上的区别
goals.en: State what can be done with a model through an API and with its weights in hand

goals.zh: 能从配置估算一个模型的参数量和不同精度下的内存占用
goals.en: Estimate the parameter count of a model from its config and its memory at different precisions

goals.zh: 能实现最简单的权重量化并解释 4 位量化为什么需要更细致的方法
goals.en: Implement the simplest weight quantization and explain why 4 bits need more careful methods

explain.zh: **两种使用方式。** 一类模型只通过 API 提供，使用者发送文本、收到文本，权重留在服务商那里，通常称为闭源模型。另一类模型公开发布权重文件，任何人可以下载后在自己的机器上运行，称为开放权重模型。两者的区别不在于模型的原理，前面各阶段的内容对两者同样适用，区别在于使用者能接触到模型的哪一层。
explain.en: **Two ways of use.** One kind of model is offered only through an API. The user sends text and receives text, and the weights stay with the provider. Such models are usually called closed. Another kind is published as weight files that anyone can download and run on their own machine, called open-weight models. The two do not differ in principle, and the content of the earlier stages applies to both. They differ in which layer of the model the user can reach.

explain.zh: **各自能做什么。** 通过 API 使用时，部署和扩容由服务商负责，不需要自己的硬件，通常也能用到规模很大的模型。代价是只能看到输入和输出，无法读取中间的激活值，无法修改权重，数据要发送到服务商，模型版本的更替也由对方决定。持有权重时，可以读取任意一层的激活值，可以微调和量化，数据可以不离开本机，同一份权重可以长期保存以便复现实验。代价是硬件和运维要自己承担。这是一种取舍，没有哪一种在所有情况下都更合适。
explain.en: **What each allows.** Through an API, deployment and scaling are handled by the provider, no hardware of one's own is needed, and very large models are usually within reach. The price is that only input and output are visible, intermediate activations cannot be read, weights cannot be modified, data are sent to the provider, and the provider decides when model versions are replaced. With the weights in hand, the activations of any layer can be read, the model can be fine-tuned and quantized, data need not leave the machine, and the same weights can be kept for a long time to reproduce experiments. The price is bearing the hardware and operations oneself. This is a trade-off, and neither way suits every situation better.

explain.zh: **开放权重不等于开源。** 开源促进会在 2024 年 10 月发布的开源 AI 定义 1.0 版要求提供三样东西，即关于训练数据的充分信息、用于训练和运行的完整代码，以及模型参数，并且要允许任何人出于任何目的使用、研究、修改和分享。多数公开发布的模型只提供了权重和推理代码，许可证也可能带有限制，因此“开放权重”是更准确的说法。许可证的差别在 6.2 讨论。
explain.en: **Open weights are not open source.** Version 1.0 of the Open Source AI Definition, published by the Open Source Initiative in October 2024, requires three things, namely sufficient information about the training data, the complete code for training and running, and the model parameters, and it requires that anyone may use, study, modify and share the system for any purpose. Most publicly released models provide only weights and inference code, and their licenses may carry restrictions, so open weights is the more accurate term. The differences between licenses are discussed in 6.2.

explain.zh: **读懂名称和模型卡。** 模型名称中的数字通常是参数量，例如 27B 表示约 270 亿个参数。带有 `it` 或 `Instruct` 的是经过指令微调、可以直接对话的版本。名称中同时出现两个数字的，例如 `1T-A52B`，一般是混合专家模型，前者是总参数量，后者是处理每个 token 时实际参与计算的参数量。`GGUF`、`FP8`、`qat` 等后缀表示量化后的版本。每个模型在 Hugging Face Hub 上的页面叫模型卡，它开头的元数据记录了许可证、基础模型等信息，选用模型时应当先读这一部分。
explain.en: **Reading names and model cards.** The number in a model name is usually the parameter count, so 27B means about 27 billion parameters. Names with `it` or `Instruct` are instruction-tuned versions that can converse directly. Names with two numbers, such as `1T-A52B`, generally denote mixture-of-experts models, the first being the total number of parameters and the second the number that takes part in computing each token. Suffixes such as `GGUF`, `FP8` and `qat` mark quantized versions. The page of a model on the Hugging Face Hub is called its model card, and the metadata at its top record the license, the base model and similar information, which should be read first when choosing a model.

explain.zh: **结构上的变化。** 较新的开放权重模型与本路线中反复使用的 GPT-2 相比，主体结构相同，细节上有几处常见的替换，都已在阶段 2 中介绍。归一化使用 RMSNorm，前馈层使用 SwiGLU，位置信息使用 RoPE，线性层不带偏置项。另外两处是新的。分组查询注意力让多个查询头共用一组键和值，减少了参数和 KV cache 的大小。混合专家结构在每一层准备多组前馈网络，每个 token 只经过其中少数几组，使总参数量可以很大而每个 token 的计算量保持适中。练习 1 按这种结构从配置出发数出了一个小模型的参数量，结果与 Hub 上报告的数字完全一致。
explain.en: **Changes in architecture.** Compared with GPT-2, which this roadmap uses throughout, newer open-weight models keep the overall structure and replace several details, all introduced in stage 2. Normalization uses RMSNorm, the feed-forward layer uses SwiGLU, position information uses RoPE, and linear layers carry no bias terms. Two further points are new. Grouped-query attention lets several query heads share one set of keys and values, which reduces the parameters and the size of the KV cache. Mixture-of-experts prepares several feed-forward networks in every layer and sends each token through only a few of them, so the total parameter count can be very large while the computation per token stays moderate. Exercise 1 counts the parameters of a small model of this kind from its config, and the result agrees exactly with the number reported on the Hub.

explain.zh: **内存与量化。** 权重占用的内存等于参数量乘以每个参数的位数。一个 270 亿参数的模型，以 16 位保存约需 56 GB，以 8 位保存约需 28 GB，以 4 位保存约需 14 GB，只有最后一种能放进一块 24 GB 的显卡。量化就是用更少的位数表示每个权重。最简单的做法是把权重除以一个缩放系数后四舍五入成整数。练习 2 在 GPT-2 上实现了这种做法。8 位时困惑度从 16.8 变为 18.0，改为每个输出通道使用各自的缩放系数后是 16.8，几乎没有损失。4 位时，整个矩阵共用一个缩放系数会使困惑度升到 2674，模型基本失效，每个通道各用一个缩放系数则是 23.3。原因是少数很大的权重决定了缩放系数，使其余大多数权重被舍入为零。实际使用的方法比这更细致。GPTQ 利用二阶信息逐层补偿舍入误差，其论文报告可以把权重压到 3 或 4 位而精度损失很小。llama.cpp 的 GGUF 格式提供多档量化，其文档中常用的 Q4_K_M 平均每个权重约 4.9 位。
explain.en: **Memory and quantization.** The memory taken by the weights equals the number of parameters times the bits per parameter. A model with 27 billion parameters needs about 56 GB at 16 bits, about 28 GB at 8 bits and about 14 GB at 4 bits, and only the last fits on a 24 GB GPU. Quantization represents every weight with fewer bits. The simplest way divides the weights by a scale and rounds to integers. Exercise 2 implements this on GPT-2. At 8 bits the perplexity changes from 16.8 to 18.0, and to 16.8 with a separate scale for every output channel, which is practically no loss. At 4 bits, one scale for a whole matrix raises the perplexity to 2674 and the model essentially stops working, while one scale per channel gives 23.3. The reason is that a few very large weights determine the scale and cause most of the other weights to be rounded to zero. Methods used in practice are more careful than this. GPTQ compensates the rounding error layer by layer with second-order information, and its paper reports compressing weights to 3 or 4 bits with little loss of accuracy. The GGUF format of llama.cpp offers many levels of quantization, among which the commonly used Q4_K_M averages about 4.9 bits per weight according to its documentation.

explain.zh: **当前的生态。** 提供闭源模型的主要是 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 等公司，具体的型号和价格更新很快，应以各自的官方页面为准。开放权重一侧，Hub 上近期发布过模型的机构包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen、Moonshot AI 的 Kimi、Z.ai 的 GLM、Google 的 Gemma、Meta 的 Llama、Mistral、MiniMax、OpenAI 的 gpt-oss 和 Microsoft。下面的表格列出了其中一些模型在 Hub 上登记的参数量。可以看到规模的跨度很大，从 1 亿多到 2 万亿以上，后者只能在大型集群上运行。本路线的练习使用 GPT-2，是因为它小到可以在 CPU 上几秒钟跑完，而机制与大模型相同。
explain.en: **The current ecosystem.** Closed models are offered mainly by companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Their concrete models and prices change quickly and the official pages of each should be consulted. On the open-weight side, organizations that have recently published models on the Hub include DeepSeek, Qwen of Alibaba, Kimi of Moonshot AI, GLM of Z.ai, Gemma of Google, Llama of Meta, Mistral, MiniMax, gpt-oss of OpenAI and Microsoft. The table below lists the parameter counts registered on the Hub for some of these models. The range of sizes is very wide, from just over 100 million to more than 2 trillion, the latter runnable only on large clusters. The exercises of this roadmap use GPT-2 because it is small enough to finish in seconds on a CPU while its mechanisms are those of the large models.

caption.zh: 4 位量化有 15 个可用的取值。上图中整个张量共用一个缩放系数，一个很大的权重把取值的间距拉得很宽，其余权重都被舍入到 0。下图中每个通道使用自己的缩放系数，没有异常值的通道得到了细得多的间距。
caption.en: Quantization to 4 bits offers 15 usable values. In the upper row the whole tensor shares one scale, a single very large weight stretches the spacing of the values and all other weights round to 0. In the lower row every channel has its own scale, and a channel without the outlier gets a far finer spacing.

caption.zh: 一些开放权重模型在 Hugging Face Hub 上登记的参数量和发布日期，读取于 2026 年 11 月 25 日。名称中带有 A 的数字按命名惯例表示每个 token 激活的参数量，Hub 的元数据中没有单独登记这一项。
caption.en: Parameter counts and release dates registered on the Hugging Face Hub for some open-weight models, read on 25 November 2026. A number with an A in a name denotes by naming convention the parameters active per token, which the Hub metadata do not record separately.

title.en: The parameter count of a Llama-style architecture

note.zh: 分组查询注意力中，键和值只有 $n_{kv}$ 个头，投影矩阵相应变窄。所有线性层都没有偏置。
note.en: In grouped-query attention keys and values have only $n_{kv}$ heads and their projection matrices are narrower accordingly. No linear layer has a bias.

note.zh: SwiGLU 有三个矩阵（见 2.5），$m$ 是中间维度。每个块有两个 RMSNorm，各有 $d$ 个缩放参数。RoPE 没有参数。
note.en: SwiGLU has three matrices (see 2.5), and $m$ is the intermediate dimension. Every block has two RMSNorms with $d$ scale parameters each. RoPE has no parameters.

note.zh: 总参数量。最后的 $d$ 是输出前的归一化。这里假设输出矩阵与嵌入矩阵共用，否则再加一个 $V d$。
note.en: The total. The final $d$ is the normalization before the output. The output matrix is assumed tied to the embedding matrix, otherwise another $V d$ is added.

note.zh: 代入 SmolLM2-135M 的配置（$V = 49152$，$d = 576$，$m = 1536$，$L = 30$，9 个查询头，3 个键值头，所以 $d_{kv} = 192$）。结果与 Hub 上登记的数字一致。
note.en: With the config of SmolLM2-135M ($V = 49152$, $d = 576$, $m = 1536$, $L = 30$, 9 query heads and 3 key-value heads, hence $d_{kv} = 192$). The result agrees with the number registered on the Hub.

note.zh: $N$ 是参数量，$b$ 是每个参数的位数。
note.en: $N$ is the number of parameters and $b$ the bits per parameter.

note.zh: 这只是权重本身。运行时还需要为激活值和 KV cache（见 5.2）留出空间，练习 1 中粗略地按 1.2 倍估算。
note.en: This is the weights alone. At run time room is also needed for activations and the KV cache (see 5.2), which exercise 1 estimates roughly with a factor of 1.2.

source.text: Quantization concept guide, Hugging Face Optimum documentation

steps.tex: q_{\max} = 2^{\,b-1} - 1,\qquad s = \frac{\max_i |w_i|}{q_{\max}},\qquad q_i = \operatorname{round}\!\Big( \frac{w_i}{s} \Big),\qquad \hat w_i = s\, q_i

note.zh: 对称量化。$b$ 位可以表示 $-q_{\max}$ 到 $q_{\max}$ 的整数，8 位时 $q_{\max} = 127$，4 位时 $q_{\max} = 7$。缩放系数 $s$ 也是相邻两个可表示的值之间的间距。
note.en: Symmetric quantization. $b$ bits represent the integers from $-q_{\max}$ to $q_{\max}$, with $q_{\max} = 127$ at 8 bits and $q_{\max} = 7$ at 4 bits. The scale $s$ is also the spacing between two neighbouring representable values.

note.zh: 四舍五入最多把一个权重移动半个间距。
note.en: Rounding moves a weight by at most half a spacing.

note.zh: 当间距远小于权重的分布范围时，舍入误差近似在 $[-s/2, s/2]$ 上均匀分布，其方差为 $s^2/12$。练习 2 在随机权重上验证了这个数值。
note.en: When the spacing is far smaller than the spread of the weights, the rounding error is approximately uniform on $[-s/2, s/2]$, with variance $s^2/12$. Exercise 2 verifies this number on random weights.

note.zh: 从 8 位降到 4 位，间距变为约 18 倍，误差的方差变为约 329 倍。一般地，每减少一位，间距大约加倍，误差方差变为约 4 倍。
note.en: Going from 8 to 4 bits makes the spacing about 18 times and the error variance about 329 times as large. In general each bit less roughly doubles the spacing and quadruples the error variance.

note.zh: 异常值的影响。缩放系数由绝对值最大的权重决定，绝对值小于半个间距的权重全部被舍入为 0。4 位时这个门槛是最大值的十四分之一。如果一个矩阵里有个别权重比其余的大几十倍，绝大多数权重就会消失。按通道分别设定缩放系数，可以把这种影响限制在异常值所在的那一个通道内。
note.en: The effect of outliers. The scale is set by the weight of largest magnitude, and all weights smaller in magnitude than half a spacing round to 0. At 4 bits this threshold is one fourteenth of the maximum. If a matrix contains single weights dozens of times larger than the rest, nearly all weights vanish. Setting the scale separately for every channel confines this effect to the one channel that contains the outlier.

q.zh: 开放权重模型是不是开源模型？
q.en: Is an open-weight model an open-source model?

a.zh: 通常不完全是。开源促进会的定义要求公开足够详细的训练数据信息、训练和推理的完整代码以及模型参数，并且不限制用途。只公开权重的模型可以下载、运行和微调，但使用者无法了解它是用什么数据、以怎样的方式训练出来的，许可证也可能限制商用或特定用途。日常交流中两个词经常混用，在写论文或做合规判断时宜使用“开放权重”，并注明具体的许可证。
a.en: Usually not fully. The definition of the Open Source Initiative requires sufficiently detailed information about the training data, the complete code for training and inference and the model parameters, without restricting the purpose of use. A model published as weights alone can be downloaded, run and fine-tuned, but the user cannot learn on what data and how it was trained, and its license may restrict commercial or particular uses. The two terms are often mixed in everyday use. In a paper or a compliance assessment it is advisable to say open weights and name the specific license.

q.zh: 闭源模型和开放权重模型应该怎样选？
q.en: How should one choose between closed and open-weight models?

a.zh: 取决于任务的要求，可以依次考虑几个问题。是否需要读取或修改模型内部，例如做探针、激活修补或微调，需要的话只能选开放权重模型。数据能否发送到第三方。是否需要长期固定同一个模型版本以保证实验可复现。手头的硬件能运行多大的模型。在这些条件都不构成限制时，再比较能力和成本。两种方式也可以结合，例如用开放权重的小模型做机制分析，用 API 上的大模型做对照实验。
a.en: It depends on what the task requires, and several questions can be considered in turn. Whether the inside of the model has to be read or modified, as for probes, activation patching or fine-tuning, in which case only open-weight models qualify. Whether data may be sent to a third party. Whether the same model version has to stay fixed for a long time so that experiments can be reproduced. How large a model the hardware at hand can run. When none of these is a constraint, capability and cost are compared. The two ways can also be combined, for example a small open-weight model for mechanism analysis and a large model behind an API for comparison experiments.

q.zh: 混合专家模型的总参数量和激活参数量分别决定什么？
q.en: What do the total and the active parameter counts of a mixture-of-experts model determine?

a.zh: 总参数量决定内存。所有专家的权重都要加载，因为事先不知道下一个 token 会用到哪几个。激活参数量决定每个 token 的计算量，从而影响速度。一个总参数量 1 万亿、激活参数量 520 亿的模型，占用的内存与 1 万亿参数的普通模型相同，每个 token 的计算量则接近一个 520 亿参数的模型。
a.en: The total determines memory. The weights of all experts have to be loaded, since it is not known in advance which ones the next token will use. The active count determines the computation per token and thereby the speed. A model with 1 trillion parameters in total and 52 billion active takes the memory of an ordinary model with 1 trillion parameters, while its computation per token is close to that of a model with 52 billion.

q.zh: 为什么 8 位量化几乎没有损失，4 位就需要专门的方法？
q.en: Why does 8-bit quantization lose almost nothing while 4 bits need dedicated methods?

a.zh: 8 位有 255 个可用的取值，间距足够细，舍入误差相对于权重本身很小。4 位只有 15 个取值，误差的方差大了三百多倍，而且个别很大的权重会使大多数权重被舍入为零。练习 2 中两种情况的困惑度分别是 18.0 和 2674。专门的方法从几个方向改进，包括按通道或按小块设定缩放系数、使用不均匀的取值、根据校准数据逐层补偿误差，以及在训练过程中就模拟量化。
a.en: 8 bits offer 255 usable values, the spacing is fine enough and the rounding error is small relative to the weights themselves. 4 bits offer only 15 values, the error variance is more than three hundred times larger, and single very large weights cause most weights to round to zero. In exercise 2 the perplexities of the two cases are 18.0 and 2674. Dedicated methods improve in several directions, including scales per channel or per small block, non-uniform values, layer-by-layer error compensation from calibration data, and simulating quantization during training.

q.zh: 量化之后模型会变快吗？
q.en: Does a model get faster after quantization?

a.zh: 不一定，取决于硬件和实现。量化首先节省的是内存，使原本装不下的模型可以运行。生成速度往往受限于从内存读取权重的速度，权重变小后读取更快，在很多情况下确实会加速。但如果所用的硬件或软件没有针对低位数运算做优化，也可能没有变化甚至变慢。练习 2 中的做法只是把权重舍入后仍以 32 位浮点数保存和计算，模拟的是精度损失，既不省内存也不加速。
a.en: Not necessarily. It depends on hardware and implementation. Quantization first of all saves memory and lets a model run that would not have fitted. Generation speed is often limited by how fast weights are read from memory, smaller weights are read faster, and in many cases this does speed things up. If the hardware or software in use is not optimized for low-bit arithmetic, nothing may change or things may even get slower. The procedure of exercise 2 rounds the weights and still stores and computes them as 32-bit floats, which simulates the loss of precision and neither saves memory nor speeds anything up.

q.zh: 同一个模型在不同平台上的表现为什么会不同？
q.en: Why can the same model behave differently on different platforms?

a.zh: 名称相同不代表运行的是完全相同的东西。可能的差别包括量化的位数和方法、对话模板的写法（见 4.2）、默认的采样参数（见 5.1）以及系统提示词。其中任何一项不同，输出都可能有可以察觉的差别。比较模型或复现他人的结果时，应当记录这些设置，并尽量使用发布者提供的原始权重和模板。
a.en: The same name does not mean that exactly the same thing is running. Possible differences include the bit width and method of quantization, the chat template (see 4.2), the default sampling parameters (see 5.1) and the system prompt. A difference in any one of them can change the output perceptibly. When comparing models or reproducing the results of others, these settings should be recorded, and the original weights and template of the publisher used where possible.

plain.zh: 闭源模型像去餐馆点菜，方便，不用自己准备锅灶，但进不了后厨，也不知道菜谱哪天会改。开放权重模型像拿到了菜谱和食材自己做，可以进后厨看每一步，想怎么改都行，但锅和火要自己准备。量化像把照片从高清压缩成小图，文件小了很多，轻度压缩几乎看不出差别，压得太狠就糊了。
plain.en: A closed model is like ordering at a restaurant. It is convenient and needs no kitchen of one's own, yet the kitchen is off limits and the recipe may change without notice. An open-weight model is like cooking with the recipe and the ingredients in hand. Every step in the kitchen can be watched and anything can be changed, but stove and pots have to be provided. Quantization is like compressing a high-resolution photo into a small image. The file is much smaller, light compression is barely visible, and heavy compression blurs the picture.

summary.zh: 能下载不等于能随意使用。几类常见的模型许可证各自允许什么、要求什么，以及怎样查到一个模型的许可证。
summary.en: Being able to download a model does not mean being free to use it in any way. What the common kinds of model licenses allow and require, and how to find the license of a model.

asof.zh: 本模块中关于具体模型和许可证的信息截至 2026 年 11 月 25 日，取自各模型在 Hugging Face Hub 上的页面和许可证原文。这类信息变化较快，使用前请以官方页面为准。
asof.en: Information about specific models and licenses in this module is as of 25 November 2026 and taken from the model pages on the Hugging Face Hub and the license texts. Such information changes quickly, and the official pages should be checked before use.

why.zh: 权重文件可以下载，并不说明可以用它做任何事。每个公开发布的模型都附带一份许可证，规定能否商用、能否再分发、微调后的模型如何命名和授权、有哪些用途被禁止。忽视这些条款可能使一个项目在后期无法发布或上线。对研究者而言，它关系到实验中使用的模型能否写进论文、微调得到的权重能否公开。许可证的判断不属于模型机制，但它是选用模型时无法绕开的一步，面试中也常被问到。
why.en: That weight files can be downloaded does not mean anything may be done with them. Every publicly released model comes with a license that determines whether commercial use and redistribution are allowed, how a fine-tuned model is to be named and licensed, and which uses are prohibited. Ignoring these terms can leave a project unable to publish or launch at a late stage. For researchers it bears on whether a model used in experiments can be reported in a paper and whether fine-tuned weights can be released. Judging licenses is not part of model mechanisms, but it is a step that cannot be skipped when choosing a model, and it is a common interview topic as well.

goals.zh: 能说出几类常见模型许可证的主要区别
goals.en: Name the main differences between the common kinds of model licenses

goals.zh: 能从模型卡的元数据中查到许可证并判断是否需要阅读原文
goals.en: Find the license in the metadata of a model card and judge whether the full text has to be read

goals.zh: 能对常见的使用情景做出初步判断并知道何时需要寻求专业意见
goals.en: Make a first judgement on common usage scenarios and know when professional advice is needed

explain.zh: **先说明一点。** 本模块的目的是帮助读者读懂许可证并形成初步判断，不构成法律意见。许可证的约束力以其原文为准，涉及商用或公开发布时，应当阅读原文，必要时咨询所在机构的法务或技术转移部门。
explain.en: **One note first.** This module aims to help readers read licenses and form a first judgement, and it is not legal advice. What binds is the text of the license itself. Where commercial use or public release is involved, the text should be read and, where necessary, the legal or technology-transfer office of one's institution consulted.

explain.zh: **宽松许可证。** 以 Apache 2.0 和 MIT 为代表，是软件领域通用的开源许可证。Apache 2.0 授予使用、修改和分发的权利，不限制商用，并附带专利授权。再分发时的条件主要是附上许可证副本、保留原有的声明、标明自己所做的修改。它不授予商标权，也不提供任何担保。MIT 的文本更短，条件类似，没有单独的专利条款。采用这类许可证的模型在使用上限制最少。
explain.en: **Permissive licenses.** Represented by Apache 2.0 and MIT, these are the open-source licenses common in software. Apache 2.0 grants the rights to use, modify and distribute, does not restrict commercial use and includes a patent grant. The conditions for redistribution are mainly to include a copy of the license, keep existing notices and mark one's own changes. It grants no trademark rights and gives no warranty. The MIT text is shorter with similar conditions and no separate patent clause. Models under such licenses are the least restricted in use.

explain.zh: **厂商自定义的许可证。** 一些模型使用发布者自己起草的协议，允许商用，但附加了条件。以 Llama 3.3 的社区许可协议为例，它授予使用、复制、分发和修改的权利，同时要求再分发时附上协议副本并在显著位置标注 Built with Llama，使用该模型或其输出训练并发布的模型，名称必须以 Llama 开头，使用者须遵守其可接受使用政策，月活跃用户超过 7 亿的公司需要另行向 Meta 申请许可。Gemma 3 所用的 Gemma 使用条款是另一个例子，它要求再分发者把使用限制传递给下游用户，并保留了 Google 对违规使用进行限制的权利。这类协议的条款各不相同，没有通用的结论，只能逐份阅读。
explain.en: **Custom licenses of vendors.** Some models use agreements drafted by the publisher that allow commercial use under added conditions. The community license agreement of Llama 3.3 is an example. It grants the rights to use, reproduce, distribute and modify, and requires that redistribution include a copy of the agreement and prominently display Built with Llama, that a model trained with the model or its outputs and then distributed carry a name beginning with Llama, that users comply with its acceptable use policy, and that companies with more than 700 million monthly active users request a separate license from Meta. The Gemma Terms of Use, which apply to Gemma 3, are another example. They require redistributors to pass the use restrictions on to downstream users and reserve the right of Google to restrict usage that violates them. The terms of such agreements differ from one to the next, no general conclusion holds, and each has to be read.

explain.zh: **非商用和研究许可证。** 这类许可证只允许非商业用途。CC BY-NC 4.0 允许分享和改编，条件是署名并且不得用于商业目的，其说明页把商业目的描述为主要为了获取商业利益或金钱报酬的用途。Mistral 研究许可证只允许个人、科学或学术性质的研究用途，明确排除了员工在日常工作中的使用、以创收为目的的活动（包括测试和概念验证）以及商业分发，商用需要另行向 Mistral 取得许可。
explain.en: **Non-commercial and research licenses.** Licenses of this kind allow only non-commercial use. CC BY-NC 4.0 allows sharing and adapting on the conditions of attribution and no use for commercial purposes, which its deed describes as uses primarily intended for commercial advantage or monetary compensation. The Mistral AI Research License allows only research of a personal, scientific or academic nature and explicitly excludes use by employees in their daily tasks, revenue-generating activities (including testing and proofs of concept) and commercial distribution. Commercial use requires a separate license from Mistral.

explain.zh: **同一个系列的许可证可能不同。** 下面的表格是练习 1 在 2026 年 11 月 25 日从 Hub 读取的结果，从中可以看到三种情况。同一系列的不同代次可能使用不同的许可证，Gemma 3 使用自定义的 Gemma 条款，Gemma 4 改为 Apache 2.0。同一代中不同规模的模型也可能不同，Qwen3.8-27B 是 Apache 2.0，同一代中最大的模型使用自定义许可证，GLM-5.3 与 GLM-5.3-Flash 的情况类似。还有的模型没有在元数据中登记许可证，例如 DeepSeek-V3，这时需要到仓库中查找许可证文件。结论是许可证要按具体的模型逐个确认，不能根据厂商或系列的名称推断。
explain.en: **Licenses can differ within one family.** The table below is what exercise 1 read from the Hub on 25 November 2026, and three situations can be seen in it. Different generations of one family may use different licenses. Gemma 3 uses the custom Gemma terms, and Gemma 4 moved to Apache 2.0. Models of different sizes within one generation may differ as well. Qwen3.8-27B is under Apache 2.0, the largest model of the same generation uses a custom license, and GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash are a similar case. Some models declare no license in their metadata, such as DeepSeek-V3, in which case the license file has to be looked up in the repository. The conclusion is that a license has to be confirmed for each specific model and cannot be inferred from the name of a vendor or a family.

explain.zh: **怎样查。** Hub 上每个模型的许可证登记在模型卡的元数据里。`license` 字段是一个标识符，例如 `apache-2.0`。标识符为 `other` 时表示使用自定义的许可证，名称在 `license_name` 字段中，全文在仓库里的 LICENSE 文件中。有些模型还设置了访问申请，使用者要先登录并同意条款才能下载，称为受限访问模型。微调或量化得到的模型通常通过 `base_model` 字段指向它的基础模型，这类衍生模型一般仍然受基础模型许可证的约束。
explain.en: **How to look it up.** The license of every model on the Hub is declared in the metadata of its model card. The field `license` is an identifier such as `apache-2.0`. The identifier `other` marks a custom license, whose name is in the field `license_name` and whose full text is in the LICENSE file of the repository. Some models also require an access request, where the user has to log in and agree to terms before downloading, and are called gated models. A fine-tuned or quantized model usually points to its base model through the field `base_model`, and such derived models generally remain bound by the license of the base model.

explain.zh: **闭源模型。** 通过 API 使用的模型没有权重许可证，约束来自服务商的服务条款和使用政策，内容包括哪些用途被禁止、输入和输出的数据如何处理、输出的权利归属等。这些条款同样需要阅读，尤其是在处理他人的数据或把输出用于训练其他模型时。欧盟《人工智能法》对通用模型提供者和部署者的义务在 8.3 介绍。
explain.en: **Closed models.** Models used through an API have no weight license. The constraints come from the terms of service and usage policies of the provider, covering which uses are prohibited, how input and output data are handled and who holds rights in the output. These terms need reading as well, especially when handling other people's data or using outputs to train other models. The obligations of the EU AI Act for providers and deployers of general-purpose models are introduced in 8.3.

caption.zh: 一些模型在 Hugging Face Hub 元数据中登记的许可证，读取于 2026 年 11 月 25 日。“类别”是练习 1 中的粗略分类，只用于初步了解。标识符为 other 的都需要阅读许可证原文。
caption.en: Licenses declared in the Hugging Face Hub metadata of some models, read on 25 November 2026. The category is the coarse classification of exercise 1 and serves only as a first orientation. Every identifier other requires reading the license text.

q.zh: 做学术研究可以使用非商用许可证的模型吗？
q.en: May a model under a non-commercial license be used for academic research?

a.zh: 学术研究一般正是这类许可证允许的用途，例如 Mistral 研究许可证把个人、科学或学术性质的研究列为许可的目的。仍有几种情况需要留意。研究由企业资助或与企业合作时，是否仍属于非商业用途需要确认。计划公开微调后的权重时，衍生模型通常要沿用同样的限制。研究成果以后转化为产品时，需要另行取得商用许可。论文中应当写明所用模型的确切名称和许可证。
a.en: Academic research is generally the very purpose such licenses allow. The Mistral AI Research License, for example, lists research of a personal, scientific or academic nature as the permitted purpose. A few situations still call for attention. When research is funded by or conducted with a company, it has to be confirmed whether it still counts as non-commercial. When fine-tuned weights are to be released, the derived model usually has to carry the same restrictions. When results are later turned into a product, a commercial license has to be obtained separately. A paper should state the exact name and license of the model used.

q.zh: 微调之后的模型，许可证由谁决定？
q.en: Who decides the license of a model after fine-tuning?

a.zh: 首先由基础模型的许可证决定能做什么。Apache 2.0 允许对自己的修改部分另行设定许可条款，前提是对原有部分仍然遵守 Apache 2.0 的条件。自定义的许可证常有更具体的要求，例如 Llama 3.3 的协议要求公开发布的衍生模型名称以 Llama 开头并附上协议副本。非商用许可证下的衍生模型一般同样不能商用。发布微调模型时，应在模型卡中用 `base_model` 标明来源，并写明适用的许可证。
a.en: The license of the base model decides first what may be done. Apache 2.0 allows separate license terms for one's own modifications, provided the conditions of Apache 2.0 are still met for the original part. Custom licenses often have more specific requirements. The agreement of Llama 3.3, for example, requires a publicly distributed derived model to carry a name beginning with Llama and to include a copy of the agreement. Derived models under non-commercial licenses generally cannot be used commercially either. When releasing a fine-tuned model, the model card should state the origin with `base_model` and name the applicable license.

q.zh: 模型生成的内容归谁，可以自由使用吗？
q.en: Who owns what a model generates, and may it be used freely?

a.zh: 这取决于具体的许可证或服务条款，各家的写法不同。例如 Gemma 使用条款写明 Google 不对使用者生成的输出主张权利，使用者对输出及其使用自行负责。Llama 3.3 的协议不禁止使用输出，但规定用输出训练并发布的模型须以 Llama 开头命名。此外，生成内容在各国版权法下的地位本身也没有统一的结论。用于正式发表或商业用途之前，应当查阅所用模型的条款。
a.en: That depends on the specific license or terms of service, which are worded differently by each party. The Gemma Terms of Use, for example, state that Google claims no rights in the outputs users generate and that users are responsible for outputs and their use. The agreement of Llama 3.3 does not prohibit the use of outputs but provides that a model trained on outputs and then distributed must be named beginning with Llama. Moreover, the status of generated content under the copyright law of different countries is itself not settled uniformly. The terms of the model in use should be consulted before formal publication or commercial use.

q.zh: 受限访问的模型是什么意思？
q.en: What does a gated model mean?

a.zh: 发布者在 Hub 上开启了访问申请。使用者需要登录账号，在模型页面上同意条款并提交申请，用户名和邮箱会提供给发布者。申请可以是自动批准，也可以由发布者逐个审核。在脚本中下载这类模型需要使用访问令牌。受限访问是一种分发上的控制，与许可证的宽严没有必然的对应关系，模型的元数据在未获批准时也可以读取，练习 1 就读取了几个受限模型的许可证信息。
a.en: The publisher has enabled access requests on the Hub. A user has to log in, agree to the terms on the model page and submit a request, and the username and email are shared with the publisher. Requests may be approved automatically or reviewed one by one by the publisher. Downloading such a model in a script requires an access token. Gating is a control over distribution and does not necessarily correspond to how strict the license is. The metadata of a model can be read without approval, and exercise 1 reads the license information of several gated models.

q.zh: Apache 2.0 和 MIT 有什么区别？
q.en: How do Apache 2.0 and MIT differ?

a.zh: 两者都是宽松许可证，都允许商用、修改和再分发。主要区别在于 Apache 2.0 包含明确的专利授权，贡献者把实现其贡献所必需的专利许可给使用者，并且规定对该作品提起专利诉讼的一方将失去这项授权。它对再分发时的声明和修改标注也写得更详细。MIT 的文本很短，只要求保留版权声明和许可声明。对多数使用者而言，两者在实际使用上的差别不大。
a.en: Both are permissive licenses and both allow commercial use, modification and redistribution. The main difference is that Apache 2.0 contains an explicit patent grant, by which contributors license to users the patents necessary to practise their contributions, and provides that a party filing patent litigation over the work loses this grant. It also spells out notices and the marking of changes on redistribution in more detail. The MIT text is very short and requires only that the copyright and permission notices be kept. For most users the practical difference between the two is small.

q.zh: 元数据里的许可证标识可以直接相信吗？
q.en: Can the license identifier in the metadata be trusted as it stands?

a.zh: 它是一个方便的入口，不是最终依据。元数据由发布者填写，可能缺失，也可能只写了 `other`。第三方上传的转换版或量化版，其元数据不一定与原始模型一致。稳妥的做法是先看标识符做初步筛选，再到原始发布者的仓库或官方网站阅读许可证全文。
a.en: It is a convenient entry point and not the final authority. The metadata are filled in by the publisher and may be missing or say only `other`. For converted or quantized versions uploaded by third parties, the metadata do not necessarily agree with those of the original model. The prudent procedure is to screen by the identifier first and then read the full license in the repository of the original publisher or on the official website.

plain.zh: 许可证像租房合同。有的房子可以随意居住和改造，只要求保留房东的署名，Apache 和 MIT 属于这一类。有的只允许自住，不许用来开店，也就是禁止商用。有的允许开店，但营业额超过一定数目就要另外商谈。下载模型之前先读合同，是因为能下载不等于能随意使用。
plain.en: A licence is like a tenancy agreement. Some houses may be lived in and altered freely with only the name of the landlord to be kept, which is the kind Apache and MIT belong to. Some may be lived in and not used as a shop, meaning that commercial use is prohibited. Some allow a shop, with separate terms once turnover exceeds some amount. The agreement is read before a model is downloaded because being able to download is not the same as being free to use.

title.zh: 提示工程与上下文学习

summary.zh: 不改动权重，只靠提示词中的示例和推理步骤改变模型的行为。它为什么有效，又在什么时候不可靠。
summary.en: Changing the behaviour of a model without touching its weights, through examples and reasoning steps in the prompt alone. Why this works and when it is unreliable.

why.zh: 模型训练完成后，使用者能直接控制的只有输入的文本。提示词怎样写，在很大程度上决定了同一个模型表现的好坏，这也是成本最低的改进手段。它背后有一个值得弄清的机制问题，即模型在不更新任何参数的情况下，怎样从提示词里的几个示例中“学会”一个任务。
why.en: Once a model is trained, the only thing a user controls directly is the input text. How a prompt is written determines to a large extent how well the same model performs, and it is the cheapest means of improvement. Behind it lies a question of mechanism worth clarifying, namely how a model learns a task from a few examples in the prompt without updating any parameter.

goals.zh: 能构造少样本提示词，并用标签词的 logit 完成分类
goals.en: Build few-shot prompts and classify with the logits of label words

goals.zh: 能解释示例和逐步推理各自起作用的原因
goals.en: Explain why examples and step-by-step reasoning each help

goals.zh: 能设计实验区分模型是依据示例作答还是依据已有知识作答
goals.en: Design an experiment that separates answering from the examples and answering from prior knowledge

explain.zh: **上下文学习。** 在提示词里放入几个输入与输出配对的示例，再接上要处理的新输入，模型往往就能按示例的方式给出输出。不提供示例称为零样本，提供少量示例称为少样本。整个过程中没有梯度，权重没有任何变化，示例只是输入序列的一部分。从模型的角度看，它做的仍然是预测下一个 token，只不过前文恰好呈现出某种规律。这种能力叫上下文学习。
explain.en: **In-context learning.** A few examples of inputs paired with outputs are placed in the prompt, followed by the new input to be handled, and the model often produces an output in the manner of the examples. Giving no examples is called zero-shot and giving a few is called few-shot. No gradient is involved in the whole process, the weights do not change at all, and the examples are merely part of the input sequence. From the point of view of the model it is still predicting the next token, with a preceding text that happens to show a regularity. This ability is called in-context learning.

explain.zh: **示例提供了什么。** Min 等人发现，把示例中的标签随机替换，分类任务的表现只有很小的下降。他们的结论是，示例的作用主要不在于教给模型输入和标签之间的对应关系，而在于展示三样东西，即标签有哪些取值、输入文本大致是什么样子，以及整个序列的格式。Wei 等人进一步发现这与模型的规模有关。把示例的标签全部颠倒时，小模型基本无视示例，仍按自己预训练得到的知识作答，大模型则能够按颠倒后的对应关系作答。
explain.en: **What examples provide.** Min and colleagues found that replacing the labels of the examples at random lowers performance on classification tasks only slightly. They conclude that the role of examples is mainly not to teach the model the correspondence between inputs and labels but to show three things, namely which values the labels take, what the input text roughly looks like, and the format of the whole sequence. Wei and colleagues found further that this depends on model size. When the labels of the examples are all flipped, small models largely ignore the examples and answer from what they learned in pretraining, whereas large models are able to answer by the flipped correspondence.

explain.zh: **一次实际的测量。** 练习 2 在一个 5 亿参数的模型上重复了这个实验，统计模型的回答有多大比例遵循示例所展示的对应关系。使用真实标签时是 100%。把标签颠倒后，4 个示例时是 0%，8 个示例时是 6%，模型几乎完全按自己对“正面”和“负面”的理解作答。把标签换成没有含义的 A 和 B 后，模型只能从示例中学习，两种情况下都是 88%。换成 foo 和 bar 时，4 个示例是 50%，与随机相同，8 个示例上升到 88%。这组数字说明，模型同时受到两种信息的影响，一种来自提示词，一种来自预训练。两者一致时效果好，两者冲突时这个小模型偏向后者。
explain.en: **An actual measurement.** Exercise 2 repeats this experiment on a model with 0.5 billion parameters and counts what share of its answers follows the correspondence shown in the examples. With true labels it is 100%. With flipped labels it is 0% for 4 examples and 6% for 8, so the model answers almost entirely by its own understanding of positive and negative. With the labels replaced by the meaningless A and B the model can learn only from the examples, and the share is 88% in both cases. With foo and bar it is 50% for 4 examples, the same as chance, and rises to 88% for 8. These numbers show that the model is influenced by two kinds of information at once, one from the prompt and one from pretraining. When the two agree the result is good, and when they conflict this small model leans towards the latter.

explain.zh: **措辞的影响。** 练习 1 让 GPT-2 用五种不同的问法判断同样的 16 条评论。零样本的正确率从 50% 到 94% 不等，加入 4 个示例后顺序又发生了变化。当 4 个示例全部标为正面时，16 条测试评论全部被判为正面。这种不稳定并非小模型独有。Sclar 等人在更大的模型上发现，仅仅改变提示词的格式，正确率的差别最高可达 76 个百分点，并且在模型更大、示例更多时依然存在。由此得出的做法是，报告结果时应当给出多种写法下的范围，不宜只报告一种写法的数字。
explain.en: **The effect of wording.** Exercise 1 has GPT-2 judge the same 16 reviews with five different ways of asking. Zero-shot accuracy ranges from 50% to 94%, and the order changes again once 4 examples are added. When all 4 examples are labelled positive, all 16 test reviews are judged positive. This instability is not peculiar to small models. Sclar and colleagues found on larger models that changing only the format of the prompt can shift accuracy by up to 76 percentage points, and that this persists with larger models and more examples. The practice that follows is to report a range over several formulations and not the number of a single one.

explain.zh: **逐步推理。** 让模型在给出答案之前先写出中间步骤，称为思维链。练习 3 用 8 道两步的算术应用题测试同一个 5 亿参数的模型。要求直接给出答案时 8 道全错，要求先逐步推理再作答时 8 道全对。一种机制上的解释是，一次前向计算的层数是固定的，直接作答意味着全部计算要在这固定的深度内完成。逐步推理把中间结果写成了 token，后面的每一步都可以通过注意力读取这些结果，再经过完整的一遍前向计算，相当于把计算串联了起来。
explain.en: **Step-by-step reasoning.** Having the model write out intermediate steps before the answer is called chain-of-thought. Exercise 3 tests the same model of 0.5 billion parameters on 8 two-step arithmetic word problems. Asked for the answer directly it gets all 8 wrong, and asked to reason step by step first it gets all 8 right. A mechanistic explanation is that one forward pass has a fixed number of layers, and answering directly means the whole computation has to fit within that fixed depth. Step-by-step reasoning writes intermediate results as tokens, and every later step can read them through attention and pass through a full forward pass again, which chains computations in series.

explain.zh: **需要保留的谨慎。** 逐步推理写出的文字不一定是模型得出答案的真实原因。Turpin 等人在输入中加入会影响答案的线索，例如把多选题的正确选项全部排在 A，模型的答案明显受到影响，写出的解释却没有提到这一线索，并且会为错误的答案编出看似合理的理由。因此思维链可以用来提高正确率，但不能直接当作对模型内部过程的忠实描述。怎样检验这种忠实性，是阶段 9 的主题之一。
explain.en: **A caution to keep.** The text written in step-by-step reasoning is not necessarily the true reason for the answer of the model. Turpin and colleagues added cues to the input that influence the answer, for example reordering multiple-choice options so that the correct one is always A. The answers of the models were clearly affected, while the written explanations did not mention the cue and gave plausible-looking justifications for wrong answers. Chain-of-thought can therefore be used to raise accuracy but cannot be taken directly as a faithful description of the internal process of a model. How to test such faithfulness is one of the topics of stage 9.

caption.zh: 练习 2 的结果。纵轴是模型的回答遵循示例中对应关系的比例。标签与模型已有的理解一致时完全遵循，相反时几乎完全不遵循，标签没有含义时只能从示例中学习。
caption.en: The result of exercise 2. The vertical axis is the share of answers that follow the correspondence in the examples. Labels that agree with what the model already understands are followed fully, opposite labels almost not at all, and labels without meaning can be learned only from the examples.

title.zh: 上下文学习与用 logit 分类
title.en: In-context learning and classification by logits

steps.tex: p_\theta\big(y \mid x_1, y_1, \dots, x_k, y_k, x\big)

note.zh: 少样本提示的形式。$k$ 个示例和新输入 $x$ 拼成一个序列，模型给出下一个 token 的分布。参数 $\theta$ 始终不变，变化的只是条件。
note.en: The form of a few-shot prompt. The $k$ examples and the new input $x$ form one sequence, and the model gives the distribution of the next token. The parameters $\theta$ never change, only the condition does.

note.zh: 做分类时不需要生成文本。取最后一个位置的 logits，只比较各个标签词的第一个 token 对应的值。$\mathcal{C}$ 是标签集合。这种读法没有采样的随机性，也不需要解析输出。
note.en: Classification needs no generated text. Take the logits at the last position and compare only the values of the first token of each label word. $\mathcal{C}$ is the label set. Reading the answer this way involves no randomness of sampling and no parsing of output.

note.zh: 只在标签集合内归一化，可以得到各个标签的概率。它与 5.3 的约束解码是同一件事，即只允许标签词被选中。
note.en: Normalizing within the label set alone gives the probability of each label. This is the same thing as constrained decoding in 5.3, where only label words may be chosen.

title.zh: 逐步推理为什么能做更多的计算
title.en: Why step-by-step reasoning can compute more

steps.tex: p(a \mid q) = \sum_{r} p(r \mid q)\ p(a \mid q, r)

note.zh: $q$ 是问题，$a$ 是答案，$r$ 是写出的推理过程。直接作答要求模型在一次前向计算内得到左边。思维链先生成一个 $r$，再在它的条件下生成 $a$。
note.en: $q$ is the question, $a$ the answer and $r$ the written reasoning. Answering directly requires the model to obtain the left-hand side within one forward pass. Chain-of-thought first generates one $r$ and then generates $a$ conditioned on it.

steps.tex: \text{direct: depth } L \qquad\qquad \text{with } n \text{ reasoning tokens: up to } n \times L \text{ layers in series}

note.zh: 每生成一个 token 都要完整地经过 $L$ 层，并且可以读取此前写下的全部内容。中间结果一旦写成 token，后面的步骤就不必重新计算它。这是一种直观的解释，不是严格的定理。
note.en: Generating each token passes through all $L$ layers and can read everything written before. Once an intermediate result is written as a token, later steps need not recompute it. This is an intuitive explanation and not a rigorous theorem.

source.text: Wang et al., Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models, arXiv:2203.11171

steps.tex: \hat a = \operatorname{mode}\{ a_1, \dots, a_n \},\qquad (r_i, a_i) \sim p(\cdot \mid q)

note.zh: 用采样（温度大于 0）生成 $n$ 条不同的推理路径，取出现次数最多的答案。
note.en: Generate $n$ different reasoning paths by sampling (temperature above 0) and take the most frequent answer.

steps.tex: P(\text{majority correct}) = \sum_{k > n/2} \binom{n}{k}\, p^{k} (1 - p)^{n - k}

note.zh: 一个简化的模型。假设每条路径独立地以概率 $p$ 得到正确答案，并且只有对错两种结果。
note.en: A simplified model. Assume that each path reaches the correct answer independently with probability $p$ and that there are only two outcomes, right and wrong.

note.zh: 单条路径的正确率高于一半时，投票会放大这个优势。实际中错误答案往往彼此不同，正确答案更容易成为多数，效果通常比这个二元模型更好。代价是计算量变为 $n$ 倍。$p$ 低于一半时投票没有帮助。
note.en: When a single path is right more than half the time, voting amplifies the advantage. In practice wrong answers tend to differ from one another, the correct answer becomes the majority more easily, and the effect is usually better than in this binary model. The price is $n$ times the computation. With $p$ below one half voting does not help.

q.zh: 为什么 few-shot 会提升效果？
q.en: Why do few-shot examples help?

a.zh: 示例把任务用模型最熟悉的方式表达了出来，即一段有规律的文本。按照 Min 等人的分析，示例主要展示了标签的取值范围、输入文本的样子和整个序列的格式，模型据此把输出限制在合适的范围内。输入与标签之间的具体对应关系在多数分类任务上贡献较小，对较大的模型和标签没有固定含义的任务则更重要。练习 1 也显示了另一面，示例选得不平衡时会引入偏向，效果可能比零样本更差。
a.en: Examples express the task in the way most familiar to a model, as a text with a regularity. By the analysis of Min and colleagues, examples mainly show the range of label values, what the input text looks like and the format of the whole sequence, from which the model confines its output to a suitable range. The specific correspondence between inputs and labels contributes less on most classification tasks and matters more for larger models and for tasks whose labels have no fixed meaning. Exercise 1 also shows the other side. Unbalanced examples introduce a bias, and the result can be worse than zero-shot.

q.zh: 为什么 CoT 会提升效果？
q.en: Why does chain-of-thought help?

a.zh: 需要多步推理的问题，很难在一次固定深度的前向计算中完成。让模型把中间步骤写出来，这些结果就进入了上下文，后续的计算可以直接读取，每一步只需要完成一小段推理。练习 3 中，同一个模型在直接作答时 8 道题全错，逐步推理时全对。Wei 等人在三个大模型上报告了算术、常识和符号推理任务上的提升。对于一步就能答出的问题，逐步推理帮助不大，还会增加输出的长度和成本。
a.en: Problems that need several reasoning steps are hard to complete within one forward pass of fixed depth. When the model writes out intermediate steps, these results enter the context, later computation can read them directly, and each step only has to perform a small piece of reasoning. In exercise 3 the same model gets all 8 problems wrong when answering directly and all right when reasoning step by step. Wei and colleagues report gains on arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning tasks for three large models. For questions answerable in one step, step-by-step reasoning helps little and adds output length and cost.

q.zh: 为什么同一个问题换个说法结果差很多？
q.en: Why does rephrasing a question change the answer so much?

a.zh: 模型计算的是给定前文时下一个 token 的条件概率，前文的任何变化都会改变这个条件。不同的措辞在训练数据中出现的场合不同，后面跟随的内容也不同，模型由此得到的分布会有差别。Zhao 等人把少样本提示的不稳定归因于模型对某些答案的偏向，例如靠近提示词末尾的答案和预训练数据中常见的答案。练习 1 中五种问法的正确率相差 44 个百分点。实践中的应对办法是准备一个评测集，用数据比较不同的写法，并在报告结果时说明所用的提示词。
a.en: A model computes the conditional probability of the next token given the preceding text, and any change in that text changes the condition. Different wordings occur in different settings in the training data and are followed by different content, so the distributions the model derives from them differ. Zhao and colleagues attribute the instability of few-shot prompting to biases of the model towards certain answers, such as answers near the end of the prompt and answers common in the pretraining data. In exercise 1 the accuracies of five ways of asking differ by 44 percentage points. The practical response is to prepare an evaluation set, compare formulations with data and state the prompt used when reporting results.

q.zh: 模型是在从示例中学习，还是在调用已有的知识？
q.en: Is the model learning from the examples or recalling what it already knows?

a.zh: 两者都有，比例取决于模型的规模以及示例与已有知识是否一致。练习 2 的结果是，标签与模型已有的理解相反时，这个 5 亿参数的模型几乎完全按已有的理解作答。标签没有含义时，它能够从示例中学到对应关系。Wei 等人报告，覆盖已有知识的能力随模型规模增大而出现。这一点对使用者有直接的含义。当提示词中提供的信息与模型的先验冲突时，不能默认模型会采用提示词中的信息，需要通过实验确认。
a.en: Both, in proportions that depend on the size of the model and on whether the examples agree with what it knows. The result of exercise 2 is that when the labels oppose the existing understanding of the model, this model of 0.5 billion parameters answers almost entirely by that understanding. When the labels carry no meaning it is able to learn the correspondence from the examples. Wei and colleagues report that the ability to override prior knowledge appears as models grow. This has a direct implication for users. When information supplied in the prompt conflicts with the prior of the model, it cannot be assumed that the model will adopt the information in the prompt, and this has to be confirmed by experiment.

q.zh: 写出来的推理过程就是模型真实的思考过程吗？
q.en: Is the written reasoning the real thinking process of the model?
