Article 51 provides that a model whose cumulative training compute exceeds $10^{25}$ floating-point operations is presumed to have high-impact capabilities. This compute is exactly the quantity estimated as $6ND$ in 4.6, and the derivation below gives an example of the order of magnitude.

explain.zh: **对研究和开放权重模型的例外。** 第 2 条规定，专为科学研究与开发的唯一目的而开发并投入使用的人工智能系统和模型，不在该法的适用范围之内。系统或模型在投放市场或投入使用之前的研究、测试和开发活动同样不适用该法，但在真实环境条件下的测试不在此例外之内。对于以自由和开源许可证发布的人工智能系统，该法原则上不适用，除非它们作为高风险系统、被禁止的系统或者负有第 50 条透明度义务的系统投放市场或投入使用。对于通用模型，第 53 条第 2 款规定，以自由和开源许可证发布、并且公开了参数、结构信息和使用信息的模型，免除技术文档和向下游提供信息这两项义务，版权政策和训练内容摘要两项仍须履行，具有系统性风险的模型不享受这项免除。由此可见，例外是有条件的。研究成果一旦作为产品或服务提供给他人，或者用于真实环境中的决策，身份和义务就会改变。
explain.en: **Exceptions for research and for open-weight models.** Article 2 provides that AI systems and models developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development are outside the scope of the Act. Research, testing and development of a system or model before it is placed on the market or put into service are likewise not covered, though testing in real-world conditions is excluded from this exception. For AI systems released under free and open-source licences the Act does not apply in principle, unless they are placed on the market or put into service as high-risk systems, as prohibited systems or as systems subject to the transparency obligations of Article 50. For general-purpose models, Article 53(2) provides that models released under a free and open-source licence, with parameters, information on the architecture and information on usage made public, are exempt from the two obligations of technical documentation and information to downstream providers. The copyright policy and the summary of training content remain required, and models with systemic risk do not enjoy the exemption. The exceptions are thus conditional. Once research results are offered to others as a product or service, or used for decisions in a real environment, roles and obligations change.

explain.zh: **透明度义务与罚则。** 第 50 条对四种情形规定了告知或标注的义务。与人直接交互的系统，提供者须使人知道自己在与人工智能系统交互，情形显而易见时除外。生成合成的音频、图像、视频或文本的系统，提供者须以机器可读的方式标记输出。情绪识别和生物特征分类系统的部署者须告知受影响的人。深度伪造内容的部署者须披露内容是人工生成或篡改的。罚则方面，第 99 条规定的上限为，违反禁止性规定的最高 3500 万欧元或全球年营业额的 7%，违反包括第 50 条在内的多数其他义务的最高 1500 万欧元或 3%，向主管机构提供不实信息的最高 750 万欧元或 1%。对一般企业取两者中较高的一个，对中小企业取较低的一个。
explain.en: **Transparency obligations and penalties.** Article 50 lays down duties to inform or to mark for four situations. For systems that interact directly with people, the provider has to make sure that people know they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious. For systems that generate synthetic audio, image, video or text, the provider has to mark the output in a machine-readable way. Deployers of emotion recognition and biometric categorisation systems have to inform the people exposed. Deployers of deepfake content have to disclose that the content is artificially generated or manipulated. As to penalties, the ceilings of Article 99 are up to 35 million euros or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for violating the prohibitions, up to 15 million euros or 3% for violating most other obligations, including Article 50, and up to 7.5 million euros or 1% for supplying incorrect information to authorities. For undertakings in general the higher of the two applies and for small and medium-sized enterprises the lower.

explain.zh: **生效时间。** 各项规则分阶段适用，见下表。原定于 2026 年 8 月适用的高风险义务被 2026 年 7 月生效的数字综合法案推迟，附件三用途的义务推迟到 2027 年 12 月 2 日，嵌入受监管产品的系统推迟到 2028 年 8 月 2 日。该法案还新增了一项禁止，针对生成未经同意的色情内容和儿童性虐待材料的系统，于 2026 年 12 月起适用。法规仍在调整之中，使用本模块的内容时应当核对最新的官方信息。
explain.en: **Dates of application.** The rules apply in stages, see the table below. The high-risk obligations originally due in August 2026 were postponed by the Digital Omnibus on AI, in force since July 2026, to 2 December 2027 for uses of Annex III and to 2 August 2028 for systems embedded in regulated products. The same act added a prohibition directed at systems that generate non-consensual sexual content and child sexual abuse material, applying from December 2026. The regulation is still being adjusted, and the latest official information should be checked when using the content of this module.

caption.zh: 欧盟人工智能法各项规则的适用日期，依据欧盟委员会页面 2026 年 10 月 19 日的版本。
caption.en: Dates of application of the rules of the EU AI Act, following the version of the European Commission page of 19 October 2026.

title.zh: 系统性风险的算力门槛有多高
title.en: How high the compute threshold for systemic risk is

source.text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 51 (as reproduced at artificialintelligenceact.eu)

note.zh: 4.6 中的估算。$N$ 是参数量，$D$ 是训练的 token 数，$C$ 是训练所需的浮点运算次数。
note.en: The estimate of 4.6. $N$ is the number of parameters, $D$ the number of training tokens and $C$ the floating-point operations needed for training.

note.zh: 一个 1000 亿参数的稠密模型训练 15 万亿个 token，计算量约为 $9 \times 10^{24}$，略低于 $10^{25}$ 的门槛。
note.en: A dense model with 100 billion parameters trained on 15 trillion tokens takes about $9 \times 10^{24}$, just under the threshold of $10^{25}$.

note.zh: 本路线使用的 GPT-2 small，即使训练 100 亿个 token，也只有门槛的约一百万分之一。在个人电脑或单块显卡上进行的训练和微调，与这个门槛相差许多个数量级。对于混合专家模型，每个 token 只经过一部分参数，$6ND$ 中的 $N$ 应当取激活的参数量，这是一个粗略的估算。
note.en: GPT-2 small, used in this roadmap, even trained on 10 billion tokens, takes only about one millionth of the threshold. Training and fine-tuning on a personal computer or a single GPU are many orders of magnitude below it. For a mixture-of-experts model each token passes through only part of the parameters, and the $N$ in $6ND$ should be the active parameters, which is a rough estimate.

title.en: Computing the ceiling of a fine

source.text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 99 (as reproduced at artificialintelligenceact.eu)

note.zh: $F$ 是固定金额，$r$ 是比例。违反禁止性规定时 $F$ 为 3500 万欧元、$r$ 为 7%。
note.en: $F$ is the fixed amount and $r$ the percentage. For violating the prohibitions $F$ is 35 million euros and $r$ is 7%.

note.zh: 全球年营业额为 20 亿欧元的企业，上限由比例决定，为 1.4 亿欧元。这是上限，实际金额由主管机构根据具体情节确定。
note.en: For an undertaking with a worldwide annual turnover of 2 billion euros the ceiling is set by the percentage, at 140 million euros. This is a ceiling, and the actual amount is determined by the authority according to the circumstances of the case.

q.zh: 我在高校做研究，这部法律适用于我吗？
q.en: I do research at a university. Does this law apply to me?

a.zh: 多数纯粹的研究活动不在其适用范围之内。第 2 条把专为科学研究与开发的唯一目的而开发并投入使用的系统和模型排除在外，投放市场之前的研究、测试和开发也不适用。需要留意三种会改变情况的情形。把模型或系统公开发布、供他人使用时，可能成为提供者。在真实环境条件下进行测试，不在上述例外之内。所在机构把某个系统用于实际的管理或教学决策时，例如自动评定学生的考试成绩，机构是部署者，而这类用途属于附件三列出的高风险领域。遇到这些情形时，应当向所在机构的法务或数据保护部门确认。
a.en: Most purely research activities are outside its scope. Article 2 excludes systems and models developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development, and research, testing and development before placing on the market are not covered either. Three situations change the picture and need attention. Releasing a model or system publicly for others to use may make one a provider. Testing in real-world conditions is not within the exceptions above. When the institution uses a system for actual administrative or teaching decisions, for example to grade the exams of students automatically, the institution is a deployer and such a use belongs to the high-risk areas listed in Annex III. In such situations the legal or data protection office of the institution should be consulted.

q.zh: 开放权重的模型是否免于监管？
q.en: Are open-weight models exempt from regulation?

a.zh: 只有部分免除，并且附带条件。对于通用模型，免除的是技术文档和向下游提供信息这两项义务，条件是模型以自由和开源许可证发布，允许获取、使用、修改和分发，并且公开了参数、结构信息和使用信息。版权政策和训练内容摘要两项义务不在免除之列，具有系统性风险的模型也不享受免除。这里还要回到 6.2 的内容，带有使用限制的自定义许可证是否符合“自由和开源许可证”的条件，需要逐个判断，不能因为权重可以下载就认为适用例外。
a.en: Only in part and under conditions. For general-purpose models the exemption covers the two obligations of technical documentation and information to downstream providers, on condition that the model is released under a free and open-source licence that allows access, use, modification and distribution, with parameters, information on the architecture and information on usage made public. The obligations of a copyright policy and a summary of training content are not exempted, and models with systemic risk do not enjoy the exemption. The content of 6.2 matters here too. Whether a custom licence with use restrictions meets the condition of a free and open-source licence has to be judged case by case, and it cannot be assumed that the exception applies merely because the weights can be downloaded.

q.zh: 做一个聊天机器人需要满足什么要求？
q.en: What does building a chatbot require?

a.zh: 取决于它的用途。一般用途的聊天机器人属于有透明度风险的一级，主要的要求是让用户知道自己在与人工智能系统交互，情形显而易见时可以例外。它生成的合成内容，提供者须以机器可读的方式标记。如果聊天机器人被用于附件三中的用途，例如筛选求职者或评估学生，它就成为高风险系统，要满足风险管理、数据质量、日志记录、技术文档、人工监督以及稳健性和准确性等要求。如果它的用途落入禁止之列，例如在工作场所识别员工的情绪，则不得提供。可见决定义务轻重的是用途，同一个底层模型可以落在不同的等级。
a.en: That depends on its use. A chatbot for general use belongs to the level of transparency risk, and the main requirement is to let users know that they are interacting with an AI system, with an exception where this is obvious. The synthetic content it generates has to be marked by the provider in a machine-readable way. If the chatbot is used for a purpose of Annex III, for example screening job applicants or assessing students, it becomes a high-risk system and has to meet requirements on risk management, data quality, logging, technical documentation, human oversight, and robustness and accuracy. If its use falls under the prohibitions, for example recognizing the emotions of employees at the workplace, it may not be offered. What determines the weight of the obligations is thus the use, and one underlying model can fall into different levels.

q.zh: 提供者和部署者的区别为什么重要？
q.en: Why does the difference between provider and deployer matter?

a.zh: 因为两者承担的义务不同，提供者的义务通常重得多。以高风险系统为例，提供者要负责风险评估、数据质量、技术文档和合格评定，部署者主要负责按说明使用、安排人工监督和监测运行情况。以第 50 条为例，告知用户正在与人工智能交互以及标记合成内容是提供者的义务，披露深度伪造内容则是部署者的义务。一个团队在已有模型的基础上搭建应用并对外提供时，它对这个应用而言是提供者，对所用的底层模型而言是下游的使用方。
a.en: Because the two bear different obligations, and those of the provider are usually far heavier. For a high-risk system, the provider is responsible for risk assessment, data quality, technical documentation and conformity assessment, while the deployer mainly has to use the system according to its instructions, arrange human oversight and monitor operation. Under Article 50, informing users that they interact with AI and marking synthetic content are duties of the provider, and disclosing deepfake content is a duty of the deployer. A team that builds an application on an existing model and offers it to others is a provider with respect to the application and a downstream user with respect to the underlying model.

q.zh: 模型卡与这部法律是什么关系？
q.en: How do model cards relate to this law?

a.zh: 模型卡是 Mitchell 等人在 2018 年提出的做法，用一份简短的文档说明模型的预期用途、评估方法和在不同人群上的表现，它本身是自愿的。人工智能法对通用模型提供者提出的技术文档和面向下游的信息，在内容上与模型卡有相当的重合，例如能力与局限、训练和评估的情况。但法定的文档有规定的内容和格式，委员会的行为准则为此提供了专门的模型文档表格，一份普通的模型卡并不等于履行了这些义务。练习 2 的检查清单度量的是文档是否具备几个基本的部分，属于良好实践的范畴，不是合规性的判定。
a.en: Model cards are a practice proposed by Mitchell and colleagues in 2018, a short document that states the intended uses of a model, how it was evaluated and how it performs across groups of people, and they are voluntary in themselves. The technical documentation and the information for downstream providers that the AI Act requires of providers of general-purpose models overlap considerably with model cards in content, for example capabilities and limitations and the facts of training and evaluation. The statutory documents have prescribed content and form, however, for which the Code of Practice of the Commission provides a dedicated Model Documentation Form, and an ordinary model card does not amount to fulfilling these obligations. The checklist of exercise 2 measures whether a document has a few basic parts, which is a matter of good practice and not a determination of compliance.

q.zh: 这些规则现在是否已经生效？
q.en: Are these rules already in effect?

a.zh: 部分已经适用。截至 2026 年 11 月，前八项禁止性规定、人工智能素养义务、通用模型提供者的义务和第 50 条的透明度义务已经适用。高风险系统的义务尚未适用，附件三用途的义务自 2027 年 12 月 2 日起适用，嵌入受监管产品的系统自 2028 年 8 月 2 日起适用。练习 1 把这些日期写成了一张表，可以查询任意一天有哪些义务已经适用。时间表在 2026 年 7 月调整过一次，以后仍有可能变化。
a.en: In part. As of November 2026 the first eight prohibitions, the AI literacy obligations, the obligations of providers of general-purpose models and the transparency obligations of Article 50 apply. The obligations for high-risk systems do not apply yet. Those for uses of Annex III apply from 2 December 2027 and those for systems embedded in regulated products from 2 August 2028. Exercise 1 writes these dates as a table from which the obligations applying on any given day can be looked up. The timetable was adjusted once in July 2026 and may change again.

caption.zh: 人工智能法的四个风险等级及欧盟委员会给出的例子。
caption.en: The four risk levels of the AI Act with examples given by the European Commission.

plain.zh: 可以类比药品和食品的分级管理。口香糖几乎不管，保健品要求如实标注，处方药要经过严格的审批，毒品直接禁止。欧盟的做法与此相似，按用途的风险把 AI 系统分成四级，风险越高，义务越重。同一个模型，用来写诗和用来筛选求职者，属于不同的等级。
plain.en: The graded regulation of food and medicines offers a comparison. Chewing gum is barely regulated, supplements have to be labelled truthfully, prescription drugs pass strict approval, and narcotics are banned outright. The approach of the European Union is similar. AI systems are sorted into four levels by the risk of their use, with heavier obligations at higher risk. One and the same model falls into different levels when it writes poems and when it screens job applicants.

title.en: Regulation in China and the United States

summary.zh: 中国按服务类型分别制定规章，美国没有联邦层面的综合立法而以行政令和州法为主。两者与欧盟的做法怎样对照。
summary.en: China issues separate rules by type of service, and the United States has no comprehensive federal statute and relies on executive orders and state laws. How the two compare with the approach of the European Union.

asof.zh: 本模块的内容截至 2026 年 11 月 25 日。中国部分依据国家网信办等部门公布的规章原文和新华社发布的法律修改决定，美国部分依据《联邦公报》刊载的行政令、NIST 和科罗拉多州议会的页面。加利福尼亚州、得克萨斯州和纽约州的州法未能读取官方文本，相关表述取自多份公开的法律跟踪资料并已在正文中注明。两国的规则都在较快地变化。内容用于学习，不构成法律意见。
asof.en: The content of this module is as of 25 November 2026. The part on China follows the texts of the rules published by the Cyberspace Administration and other ministries and the amendment decision published by Xinhua. The part on the United States follows the executive orders printed in the Federal Register and the pages of NIST and of the Colorado General Assembly. The official texts of the state laws of California, Texas and New York could not be read, and statements about them are taken from several public legal trackers and marked as such in the text. The rules of both countries change fairly quickly. The content is for learning and is not legal advice.

why.zh: 8.3 只介绍了欧盟。一个模型或产品在哪里提供服务，就受哪里的规则约束，中国和美国是另外两个主要的法域，三者的思路差别很大。对求职而言，面向国内公司的面试会问到备案和内容标识，面向美国公司的面试会问到联邦与州的关系以及前沿模型的透明度要求。对研究而言，需要知道三地对科研活动各自留出了怎样的空间。本模块按与 8.3 相同的方式，只写有原文可查的内容，并注明每一条的出处。
why.en: Module 8.3 covers the European Union alone. A model or product is bound by the rules of the place where it is offered, and China and the United States are the other two major jurisdictions, with very different approaches among the three. For job seekers, interviews at companies in China ask about filing and content labeling, and interviews at American companies ask about the relation between federal and state law and about transparency requirements for frontier models. For researchers it matters what room each of the three leaves for scientific work. This module proceeds as 8.3 does, stating only what can be checked against a text and naming the source of each point.

goals.zh: 能说出中国现行的几部主要规章各自管什么
goals.en: Say what each of the main rules currently in force in China covers

goals.zh: 能说明美国联邦层面与州层面的现状以及两者之间的争议
goals.en: Describe the current state at the federal and the state level in the United States and the dispute between the two

goals.zh: 能就同一个产品比较三个法域的主要要求
goals.en: Compare the main requirements of the three jurisdictions for one and the same product

explain.zh: **中国的总体做法。** 中国没有采用一部综合性法律加风险分级的做法，而是针对不同类型的服务陆续制定部门规章，主要由国家互联网信息办公室牵头。截至 2026 年 11 月，综合性的人工智能法尚未出台。国务院 2026 年度立法工作计划提出加快推进人工智能健康发展综合性立法，公开报道中未见草案提请全国人大常委会审议。法律层面的变化是，修改后的《网络安全法》自 2026 年 1 月 1 日起施行，新增的第二十条规定国家支持人工智能基础理论研究和算法等关键技术研发，推进训练数据资源、算力等基础设施建设，完善伦理规范，加强风险监测评估和安全监管。这是人工智能第一次被写入国家层面的法律，条文是原则性的，具体义务仍然来自下面几部规章。
explain.en: **The overall approach of China.** China has not adopted one comprehensive statute with risk levels. It has issued departmental rules for different types of services one after another, mainly led by the Cyberspace Administration of China. As of November 2026 no comprehensive AI law has been enacted. The 2026 legislative work plan of the State Council calls for accelerating comprehensive legislation on the healthy development of AI, and public reports show no draft submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. At the level of statute, the amended Cybersecurity Law has applied since 1 January 2026, and its new Article 20 provides that the state supports basic research in AI and the development of key technologies such as algorithms, advances infrastructure such as training data resources and computing power, improves ethical norms, and strengthens risk monitoring, assessment and safety supervision. This is the first time AI has been written into a national statute. The provision is one of principle, and concrete obligations still come from the rules below.

explain.zh: **生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法。** 自 2023 年 8 月 15 日起施行，是与大模型关系最直接的一部。它适用于利用生成式人工智能技术向中国境内公众提供文本、图片、音频、视频等内容的服务。企业、教育和科研机构等研发、应用这类技术而未向境内公众提供服务的，不适用该办法。主要要求包括，不得生成法律法规禁止的内容，采取措施防止歧视，提高生成内容的准确性和可靠性。训练数据须来源合法，不得侵害知识产权，涉及个人信息的须取得同意或符合其他法定情形。发现违法内容时须停止生成、消除并整改，再向主管部门报告。提供具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的服务的，须开展安全评估并履行算法备案手续。据公开资料，截至 2026 年 4 月底累计有 868 款服务完成了备案。
explain.en: **The Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services.** In force since 15 August 2023, these are the rules most directly concerned with large models. They apply to services that use generative AI to provide text, images, audio, video and other content to the public within China. Enterprises, educational and research institutions and others that develop or apply such technology without offering services to the public in China are not covered. The main requirements are that content prohibited by laws and regulations must not be generated, that measures are taken against discrimination, and that the accuracy and reliability of generated content are improved. Training data must come from lawful sources and must not infringe intellectual property, and where personal information is involved consent or another legal basis is required. When unlawful content is found, generation has to stop, the content has to be removed and the service rectified, and the authority informed. Services with public opinion attributes or the capacity for social mobilization have to undergo a security assessment and complete algorithm filing. According to public sources, 868 services had completed filing by the end of April 2026.

explain.zh: **内容标识。** 《人工智能生成合成内容标识办法》自 2025 年 9 月 1 日起施行，并配有一项强制性国家标准。它区分两种标识。显式标识以文字、声音、图形等方式呈现，用户能够明显感知。对于文本，应当在起始、末尾或中间适当位置添加文字提示。隐式标识通过技术措施写入文件数据，不易被用户察觉。服务提供者应当在文件元数据中添加隐式标识，内容包括生成合成内容的属性信息、服务提供者的名称或编码、内容编号。传播平台须核验元数据，并按三种情形提示用户，即元数据标明为生成内容的、用户声明为生成内容的，以及检测到生成痕迹而疑似为生成内容的。任何组织和个人不得恶意删除、篡改、伪造或隐匿标识。练习 1 实现了这套逻辑的一个简化版本。这项规定与欧盟第 50 条关于以机器可读方式标记合成内容的要求相对应，中国的规定在标识的形式和各环节的责任上写得更具体。
explain.en: **Content labeling.** The Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content have applied since 1 September 2025 and are accompanied by a mandatory national standard. They distinguish two kinds of labels. Explicit labels are presented as text, sound, graphics and the like and are clearly perceptible to users. For text, a notice is to be added at the start, at the end or at a suitable place in between. Implicit labels are written into the data of the file by technical means and are not easily noticed by users. Service providers are to add an implicit label to the file metadata, containing the attribute information of the generated content, the name or code of the provider and a content number. Distribution platforms have to check the metadata and notify users in three situations, namely where the metadata mark the content as generated, where the user declares it as generated, and where traces of generation are detected and the content is suspected to be generated. No organization or individual may maliciously delete, alter, forge or conceal labels. Exercise 1 implements a simplified version of this logic. The rule corresponds to the requirement of Article 50 in the European Union to mark synthetic content in a machine-readable way, with the Chinese rule being more specific about the form of labels and the responsibilities at each stage.

explain.zh: **其他相关规章。** 《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》自 2023 年 1 月 10 日起施行，针对生成或编辑文本、图像、音频、视频的技术，规定了使用者真实身份认证、内容标识、算法备案、安全评估和内容管理等义务，编辑人脸、人声等生物识别信息的，应当提示使用者取得被编辑者的单独同意。《人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法》自 2026 年 7 月 15 日起施行，针对模拟自然人的人格特征和沟通风格、提供持续情感互动的服务。它要求采取有效措施提示用户正在与人工智能服务而非自然人进行互动，用户连续使用每满两小时须提醒使用时长，不得向未成年人提供虚拟亲密关系服务，注册用户达到 100 万或月活跃用户达到 10 万时须开展安全评估。智能客服、知识问答、工作助手、学习教育和科学研究等不涉及持续情感互动的服务不在其适用范围之内。个人信息的处理另受《个人信息保护法》约束。
explain.en: **Other relevant rules.** The Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis of Internet Information Services have applied since 10 January 2023. They address technology that generates or edits text, images, audio and video and lay down duties of real-identity verification of users, content labeling, algorithm filing, security assessment and content management, and where biometric information such as faces or voices is edited, users are to be prompted to obtain the separate consent of the person concerned. The Interim Measures for the Management of Anthropomorphic AI Interaction Services have applied since 15 July 2026 and address services that simulate the personality traits and communication style of a natural person and provide ongoing emotional interaction. They require effective measures to indicate to users that they are interacting with an AI service and not a natural person, a reminder of usage time after every two hours of continuous use, no virtual intimate relationship services for minors, and a security assessment once a service reaches 1 million registered users or 100,000 monthly active users. Services without ongoing emotional interaction, such as customer service, knowledge question answering, work assistants, education and scientific research, are outside their scope. The processing of personal information is additionally governed by the Personal Information Protection Law.

explain.zh: **美国的联邦层面。** 截至 2026 年 11 月，美国没有一部规范人工智能开发和使用的综合性联邦法律，联邦层面的政策主要通过行政令表达。2023 年 10 月的第 14110 号行政令曾要求采取一系列安全方面的措施，它被 2025 年 1 月 23 日签署的第 14179 号行政令撤销。后者以保持和增强美国在人工智能领域的全球主导地位为政策目标，要求在 180 天内制定行动计划，并审查依据前一行政令采取的各项措施。2025 年 12 月 11 日签署的第 14365 号行政令提出建立“负担最小的全国性政策框架”，指示司法部成立工作组，对被认为与这一政策不一致的州法提起诉讼，要求商务部评估各州的相关法律，并要求准备一份由联邦统一立法、优先于与之冲突的州法的立法建议，建议中不应包括对儿童安全保护等类州法的排除。行政令本身不是国会立法，多份法律分析指出它不能自动使州法失效，截至 2026 年 11 月各州的法律仍然有效。这一问题目前仍在争论和诉讼之中。
explain.en: **The federal level in the United States.** As of November 2026 the United States has no comprehensive federal statute regulating the development and use of AI, and federal policy is expressed mainly through executive orders. Executive Order 14110 of October 2023 had required a series of safety measures and was revoked by Executive Order 14179, signed on 23 January 2025. The latter sets sustaining and enhancing the global AI dominance of the United States as its policy goal, calls for an action plan within 180 days and orders a review of the measures taken under the earlier order. Executive Order 14365, signed on 11 December 2025, proposes a minimally burdensome national policy framework, directs the Department of Justice to set up a task force to challenge state laws considered inconsistent with this policy, has the Department of Commerce evaluate the relevant laws of the states, and asks for a legislative recommendation for a uniform federal framework that preempts conflicting state laws, which should not propose preempting state laws on matters such as child safety protections. An executive order is not an act of Congress, several legal analyses point out that it cannot by itself invalidate state laws, and as of November 2026 the laws of the states remain in effect. The matter is still being debated and litigated.

explain.zh: **自愿性框架。** 美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）在 2023 年 1 月发布了人工智能风险管理框架 1.0 版，供各机构自愿采用，它把风险管理的工作归为治理、映射、度量和管理四项功能。2024 年 7 月又发布了针对生成式人工智能的配套文件。该框架没有法律约束力，但被许多企业用作内部治理的依据，也被一些州法引用。NIST 的页面显示，这一框架正在按白宫的人工智能行动计划进行修订。
explain.en: **A voluntary framework.** In January 2023 the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) released version 1.0 of the AI Risk Management Framework for voluntary use, which groups the work of risk management into four functions, govern, map, measure and manage. A companion profile for generative AI followed in July 2024. The framework is not legally binding, yet many companies use it as the basis of their internal governance and some state laws refer to it. The NIST page states that the framework is being revised under the AI Action Plan of the White House.

explain.zh: **美国的州层面。** 具体的义务主要来自各州，各州的规定互不相同。科罗拉多州在 2026 年 5 月 14 日签署了 SB 26-189，以它取代了此前从未实际适用过的 2024 年人工智能法。新法规范用于“重大决定”的自动化决策技术，重大决定指关于一个人能否获得教育、就业、住房、金融服务、保险、医疗或基本政府服务的决定。开发者自 2027 年 1 月 1 日起须向部署者提供技术文档，内容包括预期用途、训练数据的类别、已知的局限和人工复核的说明。部署者须在使用时告知消费者，并在作出不利决定后 30 天内说明该技术所起的作用，消费者可以要求更正数据和人工复核。以下三部州法未能读取官方文本，根据多份公开的法律跟踪资料，加利福尼亚州的 SB 53 自 2026 年 1 月 1 日起施行，针对训练计算量超过 $10^{26}$ 次运算的前沿模型的开发者，要求公布安全框架并报告重大安全事件。得克萨斯州的 TRAIGA 自 2026 年 1 月 1 日起施行。纽约州的 RAISE 法定于 2027 年 1 月 1 日起施行。
explain.en: **The state level in the United States.** Concrete obligations come mainly from the states, whose rules differ from one another. Colorado signed SB 26-189 on 14 May 2026, replacing its 2024 AI Act, which had never actually applied. The new law regulates automated decision-making technology used in consequential decisions, meaning decisions about a person's access to education, employment, housing, financial services, insurance, health care or essential government services. From 1 January 2027 developers have to give deployers technical documentation covering intended uses, categories of training data, known limitations and instructions for human review. Deployers have to notify consumers at the point of use and, within 30 days after an adverse decision, describe the role the technology played, and consumers may request correction of data and human review. The official texts of the following three state laws could not be read. According to several public legal trackers, SB 53 of California has applied since 1 January 2026 and addresses developers of frontier models trained with more than $10^{26}$ operations, requiring them to publish a safety framework and report critical safety incidents. TRAIGA of Texas has applied since 1 January 2026. The RAISE Act of New York is due to apply from 1 January 2027.

explain.zh: **三者的对照。** 三个法域的切入点不同。欧盟以一部法规覆盖各类用途，按风险等级规定义务。中国按服务类型分别立规，重点在面向公众的服务的内容管理、标识和事前的备案与评估。美国联邦层面以行政令设定政策方向并提供自愿性框架，有约束力的规则分散在各州。三者也有共同之处。面向公众的服务普遍要求让用户知道内容或对话来自人工智能。科研活动在欧盟和中国的主要规章中都被明确排除在适用范围之外。对能力最强的模型，欧盟和加利福尼亚州都以训练计算量作为门槛之一，数值分别是 $10^{25}$ 和 $10^{26}$。下表按几个方面做了整理。
explain.en: **The three compared.** The three jurisdictions start from different points. The European Union covers all kinds of uses with one regulation and sets obligations by risk level. China makes separate rules by type of service, with the emphasis on content management, labeling, and prior filing and assessment for services offered to the public. The United States sets policy direction through executive orders at the federal level and offers a voluntary framework, while binding rules are scattered across the states. The three also have points in common. Services offered to the public are generally required to let users know that content or a conversation comes from AI. Scientific research is explicitly excluded from the scope of the main instruments in both the European Union and China. For the most capable models, both the European Union and California use training compute as one threshold, at $10^{25}$ and $10^{26}$ respectively. The table below arranges this by several aspects.

q.zh: 中国有人工智能法吗？
q.en: Does China have an AI law?

a.zh: 截至 2026 年 11 月还没有一部综合性的人工智能法。现行的规则由几部分构成。法律层面有《网络安全法》《数据安全法》和《个人信息保护法》，其中修改后的《网络安全法》自 2026 年 1 月 1 日起新增了关于人工智能的原则性条款。规章层面有针对算法推荐、深度合成、生成式人工智能服务、生成合成内容标识和拟人化互动服务的几部专门规定。综合性立法已被列入国务院 2026 年度立法工作计划，公开报道中未见草案提请审议。因此不能把没有统一的法律理解为没有监管，面向公众的生成式服务目前已有可以直接适用的要求。
a.en: As of November 2026 there is no comprehensive AI law. The rules in force have several parts. At the level of statute there are the Cybersecurity Law, the Data Security Law and the Personal Information Protection Law, of which the amended Cybersecurity Law has contained a provision of principle on AI since 1 January 2026. At the level of rules there are dedicated instruments on algorithmic recommendation, deep synthesis, generative AI services, the labeling of generated content and anthropomorphic interaction services. Comprehensive legislation is on the 2026 legislative work plan of the State Council, and public reports show no draft submitted for deliberation. The absence of a single statute should therefore not be taken as an absence of regulation, and requirements that apply directly to generative services offered to the public already exist.

q.zh: 在中国上线一个大模型产品需要做什么？
q.en: What does launching a large-model product in China involve?

a.zh: 以面向境内公众的生成式服务为例，依据《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》，主要有四个方面。内容方面，不得生成法律法规禁止的内容，发现后要处置、整改并报告。数据方面，训练数据来源须合法，涉及个人信息的须有合法依据。标识方面，对生成内容添加显式标识和隐式标识。程序方面，服务具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的，上线之前须完成安全评估和算法备案。产品如果属于提供持续情感互动的拟人化服务，还要满足相应办法中关于提示、时长提醒和未成年人保护的要求。面试中被问到这个问题时，按这四个方面回答并说出对应的文件名称，通常就足够了。实际办理时应以主管部门的最新要求为准。
a.en: Take a generative service offered to the public in China. Under the Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services there are four main aspects. On content, nothing prohibited by laws and regulations may be generated, and what is found has to be handled, rectified and reported. On data, training data must come from lawful sources and personal information needs a legal basis. On labeling, generated content receives explicit and implicit labels. On procedure, a service with public opinion attributes or the capacity for social mobilization has to complete a security assessment and algorithm filing before launch. If the product is an anthropomorphic service providing ongoing emotional interaction, the requirements of the corresponding measures on disclosure, usage reminders and the protection of minors apply as well. When asked this in an interview, answering by these four aspects and naming the corresponding instruments is usually sufficient. For an actual launch the current requirements of the authorities are what counts.

q.zh: 在中国做大模型研究受这些规章约束吗？
q.en: Do these rules bind research on large models in China?

a.zh: 《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》明确规定，企业、教育和科研机构等研发、应用生成式人工智能技术而未向境内公众提供服务的，不适用该办法。因此在实验室内训练、微调和评测模型本身不在它的范围之内。有两点需要留意。一旦把模型做成面向公众的服务，办法即适用。此外，研究中处理个人信息仍受《个人信息保护法》约束，涉及人的研究还可能需要所在机构的伦理审查。这与 8.3 中欧盟的情形相似，即例外针对的是研究活动本身，而不是研究者这一身份。
a.en: The Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services state explicitly that enterprises, educational and research institutions and others that develop or apply generative AI without offering services to the public in China are not covered. Training, fine-tuning and evaluating models in a laboratory is therefore not within their scope. Two points need attention. Once a model is turned into a service for the public, the measures apply. In addition, the processing of personal information in research remains subject to the Personal Information Protection Law, and research involving people may also require ethics review by one's institution. This resembles the situation in the European Union described in 8.3, in that the exception attaches to the research activity and not to the status of being a researcher.

q.zh: 美国为什么没有联邦层面的人工智能法，州法现在有效吗？
q.en: Why is there no federal AI law in the United States, and are state laws currently valid?

a.zh: 国会至今没有通过综合性的人工智能立法，联邦政策主要通过行政令表达，而行政令会随政府更替而改变，第 14110 号行政令在 2025 年 1 月被撤销就是一例。现任政府主张建立统一的、负担最小的全国性框架，并通过第 14365 号行政令推动由联邦立法优先于与之冲突的州法。支持这一方向的理由是避免企业面对各州互不相同的规则。反对的一方认为在联邦立法缺位的情况下，州法是现有的主要保护手段，多个州的检察长曾联名要求国会不要排除州法。就现状而言，行政令不能自行使州法失效，公开资料显示截至 2026 年 11 月没有联邦法律排除州的人工智能立法，各州的法律仍可执行，相关诉讼尚在进行。这是一个正在变化的问题，使用时应核对最新情况。
a.en: Congress has so far passed no comprehensive AI legislation, and federal policy is expressed mainly through executive orders, which change with administrations, the revocation of Executive Order 14110 in January 2025 being one example. The current administration favours a uniform, minimally burdensome national framework and, through Executive Order 14365, promotes federal legislation that would preempt conflicting state laws. The argument for this direction is to spare companies differing rules in every state. The opposing side holds that in the absence of federal legislation state laws are the main protection available, and the attorneys general of many states have jointly asked Congress not to preempt them. As things stand, an executive order cannot by itself invalidate state laws, public sources show no federal statute preempting state AI legislation as of November 2026, the laws of the states remain enforceable, and litigation is under way. The matter is changing, and the latest state of affairs should be checked before relying on it.

q.zh: NIST 人工智能风险管理框架有强制力吗？
q.en: Is the NIST AI Risk Management Framework binding?

a.zh: 没有。NIST 的页面写明它供自愿采用。它的作用在于提供一套通用的工作方法，把风险管理分为治理、映射、度量和管理四项功能，并为生成式人工智能提供了专门的配套文件。它之所以重要，是因为许多企业以它作为内部流程的依据，在面向美国公司的面试中被问到如何管理模型风险时，按这四项功能组织回答是常见的做法。本路线中 8.1 的评测和 8.2 的检测方法，大体对应其中的度量。
a.en: No. The NIST page states that it is intended for voluntary use. Its role is to provide a common way of working, dividing risk management into the four functions govern, map, measure and manage, with a dedicated companion profile for generative AI. It matters because many companies base their internal processes on it, and when asked in an interview at an American company how model risk is managed, arranging the answer by these four functions is common practice. The evaluation of 8.1 and the detection methods of 8.2 in this roadmap correspond broadly to the function measure.

q.zh: 同一个聊天产品在三个法域分别要注意什么？
q.en: What does one and the same chat product have to mind in the three jurisdictions?

a.zh: 在欧盟，一般用途的聊天产品属于有透明度风险的一级，提供者须让用户知道自己在与人工智能交互，并以机器可读的方式标记生成的内容。用途如果落入附件三，则按高风险系统对待。在中国，面向境内公众提供服务即适用《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》，要满足内容、训练数据和标识方面的要求，具有舆论属性或社会动员能力的还要完成安全评估和算法备案。产品如果提供持续的情感陪伴，另受拟人化互动服务办法约束。在美国，没有统一的联邦要求，需要逐州查看。例如在科罗拉多州，产品如果被用于关于就业、住房、贷款等事项的重大决定，自 2027 年起部署者须告知消费者并在不利决定后作出说明。三地的共同点是告知义务，差别主要在上线之前是否需要办理手续，以及义务由谁承担。
a.en: In the European Union a chat product for general use belongs to the level of transparency risk. The provider has to let users know that they are interacting with AI and mark generated content in a machine-readable way, and a use that falls under Annex III is treated as a high-risk system. In China, offering the service to the public brings it under the Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services, with their requirements on content, training data and labeling, plus a security assessment and algorithm filing where the service has public opinion attributes or the capacity for social mobilization. A product that provides ongoing emotional companionship is additionally subject to the measures on anthropomorphic interaction services. In the United States there is no uniform federal requirement and each state has to be checked. In Colorado, for example, if the product is used for consequential decisions on matters such as employment, housing or lending, deployers have to notify consumers from 2027 and explain after an adverse decision. What the three have in common is the duty to inform. They differ mainly in whether a procedure has to be completed before launch and in who bears the obligations.

plain.zh: 三个法域的思路可以用三种管理方式来记。欧盟像制定一部统一的交通法，按车型分级规定。中国像针对出租车、货车、网约车分别出台管理办法，出现了哪一类服务就管哪一类。美国联邦层面像只发布了一份驾驶建议，具体的交规由各州自己制定，各州之间还不一样。这只是帮助记忆的粗略说法，细节以正文和法规原文为准。
plain.en: The approaches of the three jurisdictions can be remembered as three styles of regulation. The European Union is like one unified traffic code with rules graded by type of vehicle. China is like separate measures for taxis, lorries and ride-hailing, issued as each kind of service appears. The federal level of the United States is like having published driving recommendations alone, with the actual traffic rules written by each state and differing between states. This is a rough aid to memory, and the details are in the text and in the original rules.

summary.zh: 怎样取出注意力权重并画成热图，怎样据此找出行为特定的注意力头，以及注意力权重为什么不足以单独作为解释。
summary.en: How attention weights are extracted and drawn as heatmaps, how heads with a specific behaviour are found from them, and why attention weights alone are not sufficient as an explanation.

why.zh: 注意力权重是模型内部最容易取出、也最容易看懂的量，它直接回答了每个位置在读取哪些位置。想知道模型有没有读取检索到的文档或工具返回的结果，通常最先查看的就是它。它也是最容易被过度解读的量。权重高只说明某个头读取了某个位置，不说明读到的内容怎样影响了输出。本模块先学会提取和绘制注意力，再用一个已被充分研究的例子说明怎样从观察走向因果检验。这种从观察、假设到干预的工作方式贯穿整个阶段 9。
why.en: Attention weights are the internal quantity that is easiest to extract and easiest to read, since they answer directly which positions each position reads. Whether a model has read a retrieved document or the result returned by a tool is usually examined through them before anything else. They are also the quantity most easily over-interpreted. A high weight shows that a head read a position and does not show how what was read affected the output. This module covers extracting and drawing attention and then uses a well-studied example to show how one moves from observation to a causal test. This way of working, from observation through hypothesis to intervention, runs through the whole of stage 9.

goals.zh: 能从 GPT-2 中取出全部注意力权重并检查它的基本性质
goals.en: Extract all attention weights from GPT-2 and check their basic properties

goals.zh: 能用打分函数找出前一 token 头和归纳头，并用消融检验它们的作用
goals.en: Find previous-token heads and induction heads with scoring functions and test their role by ablation

goals.zh: 能说明注意力权重作为解释的局限，以及需要补充什么证据
goals.en: State the limits of attention weights as an explanation and what further evidence is needed

explain.zh: **取出的是什么。** 2.2 中每个注意力头在每个位置上计算一组权重，表示该位置从各个位置读取信息的比例。GPT-2 small 有 12 层，每层 12 个头，对一段长度为 $T$ 的输入，全部权重构成一个形状为 $12 \times 12 \times T \times T$ 的张量。第 $i$ 行是位置 $i$ 的读取分布，各项非负且和为 1。由于因果掩码，对角线以上的项都是 0，第一个位置只能读取自身。练习 1 取出这个张量并逐项检查这些性质。画成热图时，行是读取信息的位置，列是被读取的位置。
explain.en: **What is extracted.** In 2.2 every attention head computes at every position a set of weights giving the share of information the position reads from each position. GPT-2 small has 12 layers of 12 heads, and for an input of length $T$ all weights form a tensor of shape $12 \times 12 \times T \times T$. Row $i$ is the reading distribution of position $i$, with non-negative entries that sum to 1. Because of the causal mask the entries above the diagonal are 0, and the first position can read only itself. Exercise 1 extracts this tensor and checks these properties one by one. In a heatmap the rows are the positions that read and the columns the positions that are read.

explain.zh: **常见的几种模式。** 对句子 The cat sat on the mat because it was tired，144 个头的行为差别很大。有的头几乎把全部权重放在前一个位置上，例如第 4 层第 11 个头，它在各个位置上的平均熵接近 0。有的头把权重分散到所有位置，第 11 层第 0 个头的平均熵为 1.42 奈特，接近均匀分布的 1.51。还有很大一部分权重落在第一个 token 上，在这个句子里对所有头和位置取平均是 0.65。Clark 等人在 BERT 中观察到大量注意力集中在分隔符上，并推测这相当于一种不读取信息的默认状态，GPT-2 中第一个 token 可能起类似的作用，这里没有对此做检验。在这个句子里，第 4 层第 3 个头从 it 读取 cat 的权重是 0.84。单独一个句子上的观察不足以说明这个头负责指代关系，它只是一个值得进一步检验的线索。
explain.en: **Some common patterns.** For the sentence The cat sat on the mat because it was tired, the 144 heads behave very differently. Some put nearly all weight on the previous position, such as head 11 of layer 4, whose mean entropy over the positions is close to 0. Some spread the weight over all positions, and head 0 of layer 11 has a mean entropy of 1.42 nats, close to the 1.51 of a uniform distribution. A large share of the weight also falls on the first token, 0.65 on average over all heads and positions in this sentence. Clark et al. observed in BERT that much attention concentrates on the separator tokens and conjectured that this acts as a default state in which nothing is read. The first token may play a similar part in GPT-2, which is not tested here. In this sentence head 3 of layer 4 puts a weight of 0.84 on cat when reading from it. An observation on a single sentence does not establish that this head handles coreference. It is a lead worth testing further.

explain.zh: **归纳头。** 有一类头的行为可以用人工构造的输入精确地检验。把 20 个随机 token 重复两遍，前面加上起始符。第一遍的内容无法预测，第二遍的每个 token 却都可以从第一遍中查到。GPT-2 small 在第一遍上的平均损失是 13.03 奈特，比均匀猜测的 10.82 还高，在第二遍上降到 0.89。这说明模型在没有任何训练更新的情况下利用了上下文中的重复，这是上下文学习最简单的一种形式。完成这件事的头叫归纳头。当前 token 是 A，而 A 在前文出现过并且后面跟着 B 时，归纳头读取前文中的那个 B，使 B 更可能被预测为下一个 token。练习 2 据此定义归纳得分，即第二遍中的每个位置读取“上一次出现的同一 token 的后一个位置”的平均权重。在 5 条随机序列上取平均，得分最高的头是第 5 层第 5 个头（0.93），其后是第 6 层第 9 个头（0.89）、第 7 层第 10 个头（0.88）和第 5 层第 1 个头（0.87）。144 个头中有 8 个得分超过 0.5，它们都在第 5 层及以上，前 4 层的最高得分不到 0.2。
explain.en: **Induction heads.** The behaviour of one class of heads can be tested precisely with a constructed input. Twenty random tokens are repeated twice after a start token. The first copy cannot be predicted, whereas every token of the second copy can be looked up in the first. GPT-2 small has a mean loss of 13.03 nats on the first copy, even above the 10.82 of uniform guessing, and 0.89 on the second. The model thus exploits the repetition in its context without any training update, which is the simplest form of in-context learning. The heads that do this are called induction heads. When the current token is A, and A occurred earlier followed by B, an induction head reads that earlier B and makes B more likely as the next token. Exercise 2 defines an induction score from this, the mean weight with which each position of the second copy reads the position after the previous occurrence of the same token. Averaged over 5 random sequences, the head with the highest score is head 5 of layer 5 (0.93), followed by head 9 of layer 6 (0.89), head 10 of layer 7 (0.88) and head 1 of layer 5 (0.87). Eight of the 144 heads score above 0.5, all of them in layer 5 or above, and the highest score in the first 4 layers is below 0.2.

explain.zh: **两个头的配合。** 归纳头为什么都出现在中间层以上，Elhage 等人和 Olsson 等人给出了解释。归纳头要找的是“前一个 token 等于当前 token”的位置，而一个位置本身的表示里原本只有它自己的 token。因此需要较早的一层先把前一个 token 的信息写进每个位置，这由前一 token 头完成。之后归纳头用当前 token 作为查询，与各位置中“前一个 token 是什么”的信息匹配，读取匹配位置上的 token 并把它写向输出。前一 token 头在下层，归纳头在上层，两者通过残差流配合，这样由多个组件共同完成一项功能的结构称为回路。图的左半部分画出了这一过程，右半部分是实测的归纳得分。练习 2 找到的前一 token 头是第 4 层第 11 个头，得分 1.00，正好位于各归纳头之下。
explain.en: **Two heads working together.** Why induction heads all appear in the middle layers and above was explained by Elhage et al. and Olsson et al. An induction head looks for positions whose previous token equals the current token, while the representation of a position initially holds only its own token. An earlier layer therefore has to write the information about the previous token into every position, which a previous-token head does. The induction head then uses the current token as its query, matches it against the information in each position about which token came before, reads the token at the matching position and writes it toward the output. The previous-token head sits in a lower layer and the induction head in a higher one, and the two cooperate through the residual stream. A structure in which several components jointly perform one function is called a circuit. The left half of the figure shows the process and the right half the measured induction scores. The previous-token head found in exercise 2 is head 11 of layer 4 with a score of 1.00, directly below the induction heads.

explain.zh: **从相关到因果。** 以上都是从注意力权重读出来的，它们说明这些头在看哪里，没有说明模型的预测是否依赖它们。检验的办法是消融，即把一个头的输出置零，再看损失怎样变化。练习 3 用钩子实现这一操作。钩子是 PyTorch 提供的机制，可以在不修改模型代码的情况下读取或改写某个模块的输入和输出，阶段 9 的各种干预都以它为基础。在 5 条重复序列上，完整模型第二遍的平均损失是 1.00。去掉得分最高的 3 个归纳头后升到 1.34，去掉最高的 6 个后升到 5.65。作为对照，随机去掉 6 个其他的头，10 次抽取的平均损失是 1.31，范围在 1.00 到 2.15 之间。去掉 6 个归纳头的影响明显大于对照，这支持它们承担了重复序列上的预测。
explain.en: **From correlation to causation.** All of the above was read from attention weights, which show where these heads look and not whether the prediction of the model depends on them. The test is ablation, setting the output of a head to zero and observing how the loss changes. Exercise 3 implements this with hooks. A hook is a mechanism of PyTorch for reading or rewriting the input and output of a module without changing the code of the model, and all interventions of stage 9 build on it. Over 5 repeated sequences the intact model has a mean loss of 1.00 on the second copy. Removing the 3 highest-scoring induction heads raises it to 1.34 and removing the top 6 to 5.65. As a control, removing 6 random other heads gives a mean loss of 1.31 over 10 draws, ranging from 1.00 to 2.15. Removing the 6 induction heads has a clearly larger effect than the control, which supports that they carry the prediction on repeated sequences.

explain.zh: **实验中不那么整齐的部分。** 同一个实验里有三个结果需要如实说明。其一，只去掉 3 个归纳头的效果（1.34）与随机去掉 6 个头的平均效果（1.31）相当，单独去掉任何一个归纳头的损失变化都在 $-0.14$ 到 $+0.32$ 之间，得分 0.88 的第 7 层第 10 个头被去掉后损失反而略有下降。多个头承担着相同的功能，去掉一部分时其余的可以补上，所以单个头的消融会低估它的作用。其二，单独去掉第 4 层第 11 个头，损失没有变化，尽管按上面的回路它是必需的。第 2 层和第 3 层另有得分为 0.60 和 0.42 的前一 token 头，它们可能提供了同样的信息，这一点这里没有检验。其三，在一段普通的英文文本上去掉这 6 个头，损失从 2.40 升到 4.41。这些头在普通文本上也有作用，也可能是置零使后面各层收到了与训练时差别很大的输入，这个实验无法区分两种解释。注意力得分高与因果作用大是两件需要分别测量的事。
explain.en: **The less tidy parts of the experiment.** Three results of the same experiment have to be reported as they are. One is that removing only 3 induction heads (1.34) has about the effect of removing 6 random heads (1.31 on average), and removing any single induction head changes the loss by between $-0.14$ and $+0.32$, with the loss even falling slightly when head 10 of layer 7, score 0.88, is removed. Several heads carry the same function and the rest can compensate when some are removed, so ablating a single head underestimates its role. Another is that removing head 11 of layer 4 alone does not change the loss, although the circuit above requires it. Layers 2 and 3 contain further previous-token heads with scores of 0.60 and 0.42 that may supply the same information, which is not tested here. The last is that removing the 6 heads on a passage of ordinary English raises the loss from 2.40 to 4.41. These heads may matter on ordinary text as well, or zeroing may give the later layers inputs unlike those seen in training, and this experiment cannot separate the two readings. A high attention score and a large causal effect are two things that have to be measured separately.

explain.zh: **注意力是不是解释。** Jain 和 Wallace 在多个文本分类任务上发现，注意力权重与基于梯度的特征重要性往往相关性很低，并且可以构造出差别很大的注意力分布而得到几乎相同的预测，他们据此认为不应把注意力权重当作对预测的解释。Wiegreffe 和 Pinter 回应说，结论取决于怎样定义解释，并提出了几种更严格的检验办法，他们认为已有的工作并不能否定注意力对可解释性的用处。就本模块的内容而言，可以指出三个具体的原因。权重只说明从哪里读，读到的内容经过值矩阵和输出矩阵之后是什么、有多大，权重并不包含，推导 1 写出了这一点。在较高的层，位置 $j$ 的表示已经混入了其他位置的信息，读取位置 $j$ 不等于读取第 $j$ 个 token。此外模型中存在冗余，一个头的读取即使被去掉也可能由别的头补上。比较稳妥的用法是把注意力图当作提出假设的工具，再用消融或 9.3 的激活修补去检验假设。
explain.en: **Whether attention is explanation.** Jain and Wallace found on several text classification tasks that attention weights often correlate weakly with gradient-based measures of feature importance, and that very different attention distributions can be constructed that give nearly the same prediction. They concluded that attention weights should not be treated as an explanation of the prediction. Wiegreffe and Pinter replied that the conclusion depends on how explanation is defined and proposed several stricter tests, arguing that the earlier work does not rule out the usefulness of attention for explainability. For the content of this module three concrete reasons can be named. The weights show only where a head reads. What the content read becomes after the value and output matrices, and how large it is, is not contained in them, as derivation 1 spells out. In higher layers the representation at position $j$ already mixes in information from other positions, so reading position $j$ is not the same as reading token $j$. The model is also redundant, and what one head reads may be supplied by another when the head is removed. A cautious use is to treat attention maps as a tool for forming hypotheses and to test the hypotheses by ablation or by the activation patching of 9.3.

explain.zh: **工具。** 练习用 matplotlib 画热图，这对理解数据的形状已经足够。需要交互式地浏览所有层和头时可以使用 BertViz，它在 Jupyter 或 Colab 中运行，支持 Hugging Face 的大多数模型。9.3 将介绍的 TransformerLens 把取出和改写各种内部量的操作封装成了统一的接口。
explain.en: **Tools.** The exercises draw heatmaps with matplotlib, which is enough for understanding the shape of the data. For browsing all layers and heads interactively there is BertViz, which runs in Jupyter or Colab and supports most Hugging Face models. TransformerLens, introduced in 9.3, wraps the reading and rewriting of internal quantities in a uniform interface.

title.zh: 一个注意力头向残差流写入了什么
title.en: What an attention head writes into the residual stream

source.text: Elhage et al., A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits (2021)

steps.tex: a_{ij} = \operatorname{softmax}_j\!\left( \frac{(W_Q x_i)^\top (W_K x_j)}{\sqrt{d_h}} \right) = \operatorname{softmax}_j\!\left( \frac{x_i^\top W_Q^\top W_K\, x_j}{\sqrt{d_h}} \right)

note.zh: $x_i$ 是位置 $i$ 上经过 LayerNorm 的残差流。权重只通过乘积 $W_Q^\top W_K$ 依赖于参数，这个矩阵称为 QK 回路，它决定从哪里读。
note.en: $x_i$ is the residual stream at position $i$ after LayerNorm. The weights depend on the parameters only through the product $W_Q^\top W_K$, called the QK circuit, which decides where to read.

steps.tex: o_i = W_O \sum_{j \le i} a_{ij}\, W_V x_j = \sum_{j \le i} a_{ij}\, W_O W_V\, x_j

note.zh: 头的输出是各位置的值向量按权重求和，再乘以输出矩阵。$W_O W_V$ 称为 OV 回路，它决定读到的内容以什么形式写入残差流。在 GPT-2 中 $W_O$ 是 c_proj 的权重里对应这个头的那 64 列。
note.en: The output of the head is the weighted sum of the value vectors, multiplied by the output matrix. $W_O W_V$ is called the OV circuit and decides in what form the content read is written into the residual stream. In GPT-2, $W_O$ is the 64 columns of the weight of c_proj that belong to this head.

steps.tex: o_i = \sum_{j \le i} c_{ij}, \qquad c_{ij} = a_{ij}\, W_O W_V\, x_j, \qquad \lVert c_{ij} \rVert = a_{ij}\, \lVert W_O W_V\, x_j \rVert

note.zh: 位置 $j$ 对输出的贡献 $c_{ij}$ 的大小是权重与 $\lVert W_O W_V x_j \rVert$ 的乘积。权重高而后一项很小时，贡献仍然很小。注意力图只画出了 $a_{ij}$。
note.en: The size of the contribution $c_{ij}$ of position $j$ is the product of the weight and $\lVert W_O W_V x_j \rVert$. With a high weight and a small second factor the contribution is still small. An attention map shows $a_{ij}$ alone.

note.zh: 贡献的方向同样重要。$w_v$ 是词表中 token $v$ 的输出向量，$g$ 和 $\sigma$ 来自最后的 LayerNorm（见 9.2 的推导 2）。$c_{ij}$ 与 $w_v$ 接近正交时，即使它的范数很大，对 token $v$ 的 logit 也没有直接影响。它还可以通过后面的层间接地起作用，这部分只能用干预来测量。
note.en: The direction of the contribution matters as well. $w_v$ is the output vector of token $v$ in the vocabulary, and $g$ and $\sigma$ come from the final LayerNorm (see derivation 2 of 9.2). When $c_{ij}$ is nearly orthogonal to $w_v$, it has no direct effect on the logit of $v$ even with a large norm. It can also act indirectly through later layers, a part that can be measured by intervention alone.

q.zh: 注意力权重高，是否说明模型使用了那个位置的信息？
q.en: Does a high attention weight show that the model used the information at that position?

a.zh: 不能直接这样推断。权重高说明这个头从那个位置读取了内容。读到的内容写入残差流时有多大、朝哪个方向，以及后面的层是否用到它，权重都没有说明。反过来，权重低也不说明那个位置不重要，信息可能已经被较早的层搬到了别的位置。要回答模型是否使用了某个信息，需要做干预，例如消融这个头，或者替换那个位置的内容后观察输出是否改变。
a.en: Not directly. A high weight shows that the head read content from that position. How large the content is when written into the residual stream, in which direction it points and whether later layers use it are not shown by the weight. Conversely a low weight does not show that a position is unimportant, since earlier layers may already have moved its information elsewhere. Answering whether the model used some information takes an intervention, such as ablating the head or replacing the content at that position and observing whether the output changes.

q.zh: 什么是归纳头，它与上下文学习有什么关系？
q.en: What is an induction head, and how does it relate to in-context learning?

a.zh: 归纳头是完成“前文出现过 A B，再次遇到 A 时预测 B”的注意力头，它依赖较早层中的前一 token 头。Olsson 等人提出，归纳头可能是大型 Transformer 中上下文学习的主要机制。他们的依据包括训练早期上下文学习能力的突然提升与归纳头的形成发生在同一时期，以及主要在小模型上进行的消融实验。作者自己说明这些证据是间接的，对大模型更弱。本模块在 GPT-2 small 上的结果与这一说法一致，范围仅限于重复随机序列这一种任务。
a.en: An induction head is an attention head that performs the step of predicting B on meeting A again after A B occurred earlier, and it relies on a previous-token head in an earlier layer. Olsson et al. proposed that induction heads may be the main mechanism of in-context learning in large Transformers. Their grounds include that the sudden improvement of in-context learning early in training coincides with the formation of induction heads, and ablation experiments carried out mainly on small models. The authors themselves state that this evidence is indirect and weaker for large models. The results of this module on GPT-2 small agree with the proposal, within the single task of repeated random sequences.

q.zh: 为什么这么多头都把权重放在第一个 token 上？
q.en: Why do so many heads put their weight on the first token?

a.zh: softmax 要求每一行的权重和为 1，一个头在当前位置没有需要读取的内容时，也必须把权重放在某处。一种常见的解释是，模型学会了把第一个位置当作默认的去处，并使从那里读到的内容对输出几乎没有影响。Clark 等人对 BERT 中的分隔符给出过类似的推测。本模块没有检验这一解释。它提示在看热图时，落在第一个 token 上的权重通常不宜解读为模型在关注句子的开头。
a.en: The softmax forces the weights of every row to sum to 1, so a head with nothing to read at the current position still has to put its weight somewhere. A common account is that the model learns to use the first position as a default destination and makes the content read from there nearly irrelevant to the output. Clark et al. conjectured something similar for the separator tokens in BERT. This module does not test the account. It suggests that weight on the first token in a heatmap should usually not be read as the model attending to the start of the sentence.

q.zh: 消融时应当置零，还是换成别的值？
q.en: Should ablation set the output to zero or to something else?

a.zh: 常见的做法有三种。置零最简单，本模块用的就是它，缺点是一个头的输出如果有一个固定的偏移量被后面的层当作常数使用，置零会连它一起去掉。均值消融把输出换成它在一批数据上的平均值，保留了这个偏移量。重采样消融把输出换成同一个头在另一条输入上的输出。三种做法都可能使后面的层收到不常见的输入，结论最好在不止一种做法下都成立。9.3 的激活修补可以看作更有针对性的重采样。
a.en: Three variants are common. Zero ablation is the simplest and is used in this module. Its drawback is that if the output of a head contains a fixed offset that later layers use as a constant, zeroing removes that as well. Mean ablation replaces the output by its mean over a batch of data and keeps the offset. Resample ablation replaces the output by the output of the same head on another input. All three can give later layers unusual inputs, and a conclusion is best checked under more than one variant. The activation patching of 9.3 can be seen as a more targeted form of resampling.

q.zh: GPT-2 small 上的这些发现能推广到今天的大模型吗？
q.en: Do these findings on GPT-2 small carry over to the large models of today?

a.zh: 方法可以照搬，具体结论需要逐个模型重新验证。取出注意力、打分和消融的做法与模型大小无关。哪一层哪个头是归纳头、去掉之后损失变化多少，则只对 GPT-2 small 成立。Olsson 等人在更大的模型中也找到了归纳头，同时说明大模型上的因果证据较弱。大模型的头更多，冗余更强，单个头的消融往往看不到效果，这也是后来的研究转向 9.3 的修补方法和成组分析的原因之一。
a.en: The methods carry over as they are, while concrete findings have to be verified again for each model. Extracting attention, scoring and ablating do not depend on the size of the model. Which head of which layer is an induction head, and by how much the loss changes on removing it, holds for GPT-2 small alone. Olsson et al. found induction heads in larger models too and stated that the causal evidence there is weaker. Larger models have more heads and more redundancy, so ablating a single head often shows no effect, which is one reason later work turned to the patching methods of 9.3 and to analysing groups of components.

caption.zh: 左，归纳回路的三个步骤，以序列 A B C A B 为例。右，GPT-2 small 的 144 个头在 5 条重复随机序列上的平均归纳得分，由练习 2 的参考实现算出。得分高的头都在第 5 层及以上。
caption.en: Left, the three steps of the induction circuit for the sequence A B C A B. Right, the mean induction score of the 144 heads of GPT-2 small over 5 repeated random sequences, computed with the reference solution of exercise 2. The heads with high scores all sit in layer 5 or above.

plain.zh: 注意力图像一份记录谁在看谁的视线图。它能说明开会时小王一直盯着小李，却不能说明小王听进去了多少，有没有照小李说的去做。要知道小李的话是否真的起了作用，得做实验，例如请小李这次不发言（消融），再看会议的结论有没有改变。
plain.en: An attention map is like a record of who is looking at whom. It can show that in a meeting Wang kept looking at Li, and cannot show how much Wang took in or whether Wang acted on what Li said. Knowing whether the words of Li really mattered takes an experiment, such as asking Li to stay silent this time (ablation) and seeing whether the conclusion of the meeting changes.

title.zh: Logit lens 与直接 logit 归因
title.en: The logit lens and direct logit attribution

summary.zh: 残差流是各层输出之和。把中间层的残差流直接解码成词表上的分布，可以看到预测怎样逐层形成，把最终的 logit 拆开，可以看到每个组件直接贡献了多少。
summary.en: The residual stream is the sum of the outputs of all layers. Decoding it at an intermediate layer into a distribution over the vocabulary shows how a prediction forms layer by layer, and splitting the final logit shows how much each component contributes directly.

why.zh: 9.1 观察的是信息从哪个位置流向哪个位置，本模块观察的是信息在深度方向上怎样积累。两种方法都只需要一次前向计算，不需要训练任何东西，是分析一个新问题时成本最低的入手方式。它们回答的问题很具体，包括答案从第几层开始可以被读出来，哪些层把它推高，哪些层把它压低。本模块同样需要认清方法的边界。它们显示的是中间状态在输出空间里的投影，以及各组件的直接作用，间接作用要留给 9.3。
why.en: Module 9.1 observes from which position to which position information flows, and this module observes how information accumulates along the depth. Both methods take a single forward pass and require no training, which makes them the cheapest way into a new question. The questions they answer are specific, including from which layer on the answer can be read out, which layers push it up and which push it down. The boundaries of the methods have to be recognized here as well. They show the projection of intermediate states onto the output space and the direct effect of each component, and indirect effects are left to 9.3.

goals.zh: 能用钩子取出每一层之后的残差流，并正确地解码成 logits
goals.en: Capture the residual stream after every layer with hooks and decode it correctly into logits

goals.zh: 能把两个 token 的 logit 差分解为各组件的直接贡献并验证其和
goals.en: Split the logit difference of two tokens into the direct contributions of the components and verify the sum

goals.zh: 能说明 logit lens 和直接归因各自不能回答什么
goals.en: State what the logit lens and direct attribution each cannot answer

explain.zh: **残差流是一个和。** 2.5 中每个子层的输出都是加到输入上的。从嵌入开始逐层展开，最后一层之后的残差流等于 token 嵌入与位置嵌入之和，加上 12 个注意力子层的输出和 12 个前馈子层的输出，一共 25 项。每个子层从残差流中读取，再把结果加回去，没有任何一项被覆盖。推导 1 写出了这个展开，练习 2 用钩子取出这 25 项并验证它们的和与模型实际的残差流一致。这种加法结构是本模块两种方法的共同基础。
explain.en: **The residual stream is a sum.** In 2.5 the output of every sublayer is added to its input. Unrolled from the embedding upward, the residual stream after the last layer equals the sum of token and position embedding plus the outputs of the 12 attention sublayers and of the 12 feed-forward sublayers, 25 terms in all. Every sublayer reads from the residual stream and adds its result back, and no term is overwritten. Derivation 1 writes out this expansion, and exercise 2 captures the 25 terms with hooks and verifies that their sum agrees with the actual residual stream of the model. This additive structure is the common basis of both methods of this module.

explain.zh: **Logit lens。** 模型的输出是把最后的残差流经过最终的 LayerNorm，再乘以输出矩阵得到的。Logit lens 把同样的两步用在中间某一层之后的残差流上，得到一组 logits，可以理解为计算如果在这一层停止，模型会预测什么。这等价于把之后所有子层的输出都置零。这个做法由 nostalgebraist 在 2020 年提出，不需要训练，只多做一次矩阵乘法。练习 1 对 13 个状态（嵌入之后以及 12 个块各自之后）逐一解码，并检查最后一个状态解码的结果与模型输出的 logits 完全相同。
explain.en: **The logit lens.** The output of the model is obtained by passing the last residual stream through the final LayerNorm and multiplying by the output matrix. The logit lens applies the same two steps to the residual stream after some intermediate layer and obtains a set of logits, which can be read as what the model would predict if the computation stopped at that layer. This is equivalent to zeroing the outputs of all later sublayers. The method was proposed by nostalgebraist in 2020 and requires no training, only one more matrix multiplication. Exercise 1 decodes the 13 states (after the embedding and after each of the 12 blocks) one by one and checks that decoding the last state gives exactly the logits the model outputs.

explain.zh: **一个例子。** 对提示 The Eiffel Tower is located in the city of，正确答案 Paris 在嵌入之后排在第 22947 位，第 1 至第 5 层之后解码出的第一名都是 the。它的名次随后逐层上升，第 6 层之后为第 255 位，第 9 层之后为第 13 位，此时第一名是 Rome。第 10 层之后 Paris 升到第 2 位，第一名是 London，第 11 层之后成为第一名并保持到输出。图中的第一行画出了这一过程。从中可以看到三个阶段，较低的层解码出来的是常见的功能词，中间的层出现了类别正确的词（城市名），最后两三层才确定具体的城市。
explain.en: **An example.** For the prompt The Eiffel Tower is located in the city of, the correct answer Paris ranks 22947th after the embedding, and the top token decoded after each of layers 1 to 5 is the. Its rank then rises layer by layer, to 255th after layer 6 and 13th after layer 9, where the top token is Rome. After layer 10 Paris is second with London on top, and after layer 11 it is first and stays so until the output. The first row of the figure shows this course. Three phases can be seen. The lower layers decode to frequent function words, the middle layers bring up words of the right category (names of cities), and the specific city is settled in the last two or three layers alone.

explain.zh: **不同的预测在不同的深度确定。** 练习 1 还比较了几条不同类型的提示。在 in the city of New 之后预测 York，从第 1 层之后起就是第一名，这是一个固定搭配，几乎只需要当前 token。在 Apple was founded by Steve 之后预测 Jobs，第 7 层之后成为第一名。关于 Brandenburg Gate 所在城市的事实、星期的顺序和日本的货币，都在第 10 层之后才成为第一名。句子 When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to 需要判断两个名字中哪一个没有重复出现，答案 Mary 要到第 11 层之后才成为第一名。这些都是单条提示上的观察，每种类型只有一两个例子，不足以得出一般性的规律。它们与文献中的一个常见说法相符，即越依赖上下文和组合的预测确定得越晚。
explain.en: **Different predictions settle at different depths.** Exercise 1 also compares several prompts of different kinds. Predicting York after in the city of New is top from layer 1 on, a fixed collocation that needs hardly more than the current token. Predicting Jobs after Apple was founded by Steve is top after layer 7. The fact about the city of the Brandenburg Gate, the order of the weekdays and the currency of Japan all become top after layer 10 only. The sentence When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to requires deciding which of the two names was not repeated, and the answer Mary becomes top after layer 11 only. These are observations on single prompts with one or two examples per kind and do not support a general rule. They agree with a common statement in the literature that predictions depending more on context and composition settle later.

explain.zh: **最后一层做了什么。** 有两条提示的结果值得注意。对 The Colosseum is located in the city of，Rome 在第 9、10、11 层之后都是第一名，经过最后一层后却降到第 5 位，模型实际输出的是一个不完整的词片 P。对 The language spoken in Spain is，Spanish 在第 10 和第 11 层之后是第一名，最终输出的却是 very。在 Eiffel 的例子中，Paris 的概率在第 10 层之后是 0.19，最终只有 0.06，名次没有变而概率下降了。在这几个例子里，正确的内容在倒数第二层已经可以读出，最后一层却把概率重新分配给了更泛化的续写。这说明模型内部可以读出的信息与它最终输出的内容可能不一致。最后一层为什么这样做，这里的实验没有给出答案。
explain.en: **What the last layer does.** The results of two prompts deserve attention. For The Colosseum is located in the city of, Rome is top after layers 9, 10 and 11 and falls to 5th after the last layer, and what the model actually outputs is the incomplete word piece P. For The language spoken in Spain is, Spanish is top after layers 10 and 11, while the final output is very. In the Eiffel example the probability of Paris is 0.19 after layer 10 and only 0.06 at the end, with the rank unchanged and the probability lower. In these examples the correct content can already be read out one layer before the end, and the last layer redistributes probability toward more generic continuations. Information that can be read out inside the model may thus disagree with what the model finally outputs. Why the last layer does this is not answered by the experiments here.

explain.zh: **一个容易出错的地方。** 在 transformers 的 GPT-2 实现中，`output_hidden_states=True` 返回的 13 个状态里，前 12 个是 LayerNorm 之前的残差流，最后一个则已经经过了最终的 LayerNorm。对最后一个状态再做一次 LayerNorm 会得到错误的结果，在准备本模块时就遇到了这个问题，解码出来的第一名变成了 the。练习 1 因此改用钩子直接从各个块的输出取值，并用最后一行必须等于模型输出这一条件来检验。使用任何库取中间状态时，都值得先做这样一次核对。
explain.en: **A place where mistakes are easy.** In the GPT-2 implementation of transformers, of the 13 states returned with `output_hidden_states=True` the first 12 are the residual stream before LayerNorm, while the last has already passed through the final LayerNorm. Applying LayerNorm to the last state once more gives a wrong result. This happened while this module was being prepared, with the as the top decoded token. Exercise 1 therefore takes the values directly from the outputs of the blocks with hooks and tests them with the condition that the last row has to equal the output of the model. A check of this kind is worth making whenever a library is used to take intermediate states.

explain.zh: **直接 logit 归因。** 既然最后的残差流是 25 项之和，而从残差流到 logits 的映射在固定 LayerNorm 的缩放系数之后是线性的，那么任何一个 logit，以及任何两个 token 的 logit 之差，都可以写成 25 项各自的贡献之和，另加一个来自 LayerNorm 偏置的常数。推导 2 给出了这个分解。通常考察的是正确答案与一个竞争答案的 logit 差，因为对所有 logit 加上同一个数不改变 softmax 的结果，只有差值才有意义。对 Eiffel 的提示，Paris 与 London 的 logit 差是 0.32，各项贡献之和为 0.85，常数为 $-0.52$。贡献最大的三项是第 9、11、10 层的前馈子层，分别为 $+0.42$、$+0.34$ 和 $+0.30$。全部前馈子层合计 $+1.17$，全部注意力子层合计 $-0.32$。对 The opposite of hot is，cold 与 hot 的 logit 差是 1.40，最大的两项是第 8 层的前馈子层（$+0.59$）和第 9 层的注意力子层（$+0.37$）。
explain.en: **Direct logit attribution.** Since the last residual stream is a sum of 25 terms, and the map from residual stream to logits is linear once the scaling factor of LayerNorm is held fixed, any logit and any difference between the logits of two tokens can be written as the sum of the contributions of the 25 terms plus a constant from the bias of LayerNorm. Derivation 2 gives this decomposition. What is usually examined is the logit difference between the correct answer and a competing one, because adding the same number to all logits leaves the softmax unchanged and only differences are meaningful. For the Eiffel prompt the logit difference between Paris and London is 0.32, the contributions sum to 0.85 and the constant is $-0.52$. The three largest contributions are the feed-forward sublayers of layers 9, 11 and 10 with $+0.42$, $+0.34$ and $+0.30$. All feed-forward sublayers together give $+1.17$ and all attention sublayers $-0.32$. For The opposite of hot is, the logit difference between cold and hot is 1.40, and the two largest terms are the feed-forward sublayer of layer 8 ($+0.59$) and the attention sublayer of layer 9 ($+0.37$).

explain.zh: **直接作用不是全部作用。** 上面的数字不能读成注意力层对 Eiffel 这道题没有帮助。直接归因只计算一个组件的输出经由最后的 LayerNorm 和输出矩阵到达 logit 的那一部分。一个组件的输出还会被后面的组件读取，并通过它们影响结果，这一部分没有算在它名下，而是算在了后面的组件名下。Geva 等人对事实回忆的研究认为，主语位置的表示先由较低层的前馈子层充实，再由注意力头把相关属性取到最后一个位置。按这种说法，注意力层的作用主要是间接的。本模块的结果只涉及一条提示、一个竞争答案和 GPT-2 small，既不能证实也不能否定这一说法。测量间接作用需要改变某个组件的输出后重新计算其后的全部层，这是 9.3 的内容。
explain.en: **The direct effect is not the whole effect.** The numbers above cannot be read as the attention layers not helping with the Eiffel question. Direct attribution counts only the part of the output of a component that reaches the logit through the final LayerNorm and the output matrix. The output of a component is also read by later components and affects the result through them, a part that is credited to the later components and not to the component itself. The study of factual recall by Geva et al. holds that the representation at the subject position is first enriched by feed-forward sublayers in lower layers, and that attention heads then fetch the relevant attribute to the last position. On this account the role of the attention layers is mainly indirect. The results of this module involve one prompt, one competing answer and GPT-2 small, and can neither confirm nor refute the account. Measuring indirect effects requires changing the output of a component and recomputing all later layers, which is the subject of 9.3.

explain.zh: **Logit lens 的局限。** Logit lens 假定中间层的残差流与最后一层使用同一套坐标，输出矩阵才能直接读懂它。这个假定在靠后的层大致成立，在靠前的层往往不成立，那里解码出的 the 更可能反映坐标不一致，不一定表示模型此时在预测 the。Belrose 等人提出的 tuned lens 为每一层训练一个仿射变换，先把该层的残差流变换到最后一层的坐标再解码，论文摘要称 logit lens 有用但往往不稳定，tuned lens 的预测更可靠。代价是需要训练，并且训练出的变换本身可能引入模型原本没有的计算。还应注意，能从某一层读出答案，只说明答案的信息以输出矩阵可读的形式存在于那里，不说明模型后面的计算用到了它。
explain.en: **Limits of the logit lens.** The logit lens assumes that the residual stream of an intermediate layer uses the same coordinates as that of the last layer, so that the output matrix can read it directly. The assumption holds roughly in the later layers and often fails in the early ones, where a decoded the more likely reflects a mismatch of coordinates and need not mean that the model is predicting the at that point. The tuned lens of Belrose et al. trains an affine map for every layer that first transforms the residual stream of the layer into the coordinates of the last layer and then decodes it, and the abstract of the paper calls the logit lens useful yet often brittle and the predictions of the tuned lens more reliable. The price is training, and the trained map may itself add computation the model does not perform. It should also be kept in mind that an answer being readable at some layer shows that its information is present there in a form the output matrix can read, and does not show that the later computation of the model uses it.

title.en: The additive decomposition of the residual stream

source.text: Elhage et al., A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits (2021)

note.zh: 第 0 个状态是 token 嵌入与位置嵌入之和。以下都指同一个位置上的向量。
note.en: State 0 is the sum of token embedding and position embedding. Everything below refers to the vector at one position.

note.zh: Pre-Norm 结构下，第 $\ell$ 个块先加上注意力子层的输出 $A^{(\ell)}$，再加上前馈子层的输出 $F^{(\ell)}$。两个子层的输入都先经过 LayerNorm，输出则直接相加。
note.en: With Pre-Norm, block $\ell$ first adds the output $A^{(\ell)}$ of the attention sublayer and then the output $F^{(\ell)}$ of the feed-forward sublayer. The inputs of both sublayers pass through LayerNorm, and the outputs are added directly.

note.zh: 把上一步对 $\ell = 0, \dots, L-1$ 依次代入即得。$L = 12$ 时共有 $1 + 2 \times 12 = 25$ 项。
note.en: This follows by substituting the previous step for $\ell = 0, \dots, L-1$ in turn. For $L = 12$ there are $1 + 2 \times 12 = 25$ terms.

note.zh: 第 $k$ 个状态是前 $1 + 2k$ 项的和。Logit lens 解码 $x^{(k)}$，相当于在完整的和中把 $\ell \ge k$ 的各项置零。各项本身并不独立，$A^{(\ell)}$ 和 $F^{(\ell)}$ 的取值依赖于它们之前的所有项。
note.en: State $k$ is the sum of the first $1 + 2k$ terms. Decoding $x^{(k)}$ with the logit lens amounts to zeroing the terms with $\ell \ge k$ in the full sum. The terms themselves are not independent, since the values of $A^{(\ell)}$ and $F^{(\ell)}$ depend on all terms before them.

title.zh: 固定 LayerNorm 后 logit 差的线性分解
title.en: Linear decomposition of the logit difference with LayerNorm held fixed

source.text: Nanda, A Comprehensive Mechanistic Interpretability Explainer & Glossary

note.zh: 最终的 LayerNorm。$g$ 和 $b$ 是学到的缩放和偏置。减去均值是线性运算，除以 $\sigma(x)$ 不是。
note.en: The final LayerNorm. $g$ and $b$ are the learned scale and bias. Subtracting the mean is a linear operation, dividing by $\sigma(x)$ is not.

note.zh: $w_a$ 是输出矩阵中 token $a$ 对应的行。GPT-2 的输出层没有偏置。
note.en: $w_a$ is the row of the output matrix for token $a$. The output layer of GPT-2 has no bias.

note.zh: $x$ 是 25 个分量 $x_c$ 之和。均值对加法是线性的，所以可以对每个分量分别去均值。
note.en: $x$ is the sum of the 25 parts $x_c$. The mean is linear in sums, so every part can be centred separately.

steps.tex: u^\top \operatorname{LN}(x) = \sum_c \underbrace{u^\top \Big( g \odot \frac{x_c - \mu(x_c)}{\sigma} \Big)}_{\text{contribution of } c} + \; u^\top b, \qquad \sigma = \sigma(x) \text{ held fixed}

note.zh: 把 $\sigma$ 取为完整残差流算出的值并视为常数，每个分量就有了一个确定的贡献，各贡献之和加上常数 $u^\top b$ 严格等于模型的 logit 差。练习 2 的测试检查了这一等式。把 $\sigma$ 视为常数是一种约定。某个分量如果被去掉，$\sigma$ 也会随之改变，所以贡献值描述的是当前这次计算中的分摊，不等于去掉该分量后 logit 差的变化量。
note.en: With $\sigma$ taken as the value computed from the full residual stream and treated as a constant, every part has a definite contribution, and the contributions plus the constant $u^\top b$ equal the logit difference of the model exactly. The tests of exercise 2 check this equality. Treating $\sigma$ as a constant is a convention. If a part were removed, $\sigma$ would change as well, so a contribution describes the split within the present computation and is not the change of the logit difference on removing the part.

q.zh: Logit lens 看到的是模型在中间层的“想法”吗？
q.en: Does the logit lens show what the model is thinking at an intermediate layer?

a.zh: 这个说法需要加上限定。它显示的是中间层的残差流在输出矩阵下的投影，也就是假如此时停止计算会得到的预测。模型并不在中间层做预测，中间层的表示是为后面的层准备的，其中有些信息以输出矩阵读不出来的形式存在，logit lens 看不到它们。靠后的层与输出比较接近，结果较为可信，靠前的层则需要谨慎对待。9.4 的探针是一种补充，它另行训练一个分类器去读取中间表示，因而不受输出坐标的限制，同时带来了分类器自身可能学到东西这一新的问题。
a.en: The statement needs a qualification. The lens shows the projection of the residual stream of an intermediate layer under the output matrix, which is the prediction that would result if computation stopped there. The model does not make predictions at intermediate layers. Their representations are prepared for the later layers, and some of the information is present in a form the output matrix cannot read and stays invisible to the lens. The later layers are close to the output and the results there are fairly trustworthy, while the early layers call for caution. The probes of 9.4 are a complement. They train a separate classifier to read intermediate representations and are therefore not bound to the output coordinates, while raising the new problem that the classifier may learn things itself.

q.zh: 为什么解码之前要先经过最终的 LayerNorm？
q.en: Why is the final LayerNorm applied before decoding?

a.zh: 因为输出矩阵是与它一起训练的，它只见过经过这个 LayerNorm 的向量。残差流的范数随层数增长，在 Eiffel 的例子中从嵌入之后的 4.7 增长到最后一个块之后的 444，不做归一化就直接乘以输出矩阵，得到的 logits 的尺度没有可比性。归一化只能做一次。练习 1 的测试说明了做两次的后果。
a.en: Because the output matrix was trained together with it and has seen only vectors that passed through this LayerNorm. The norm of the residual stream grows with depth, in the Eiffel example from 4.7 after the embedding to 444 after the last block, so multiplying by the output matrix without normalization gives logits on scales that cannot be compared. The normalization is to be applied once. The tests of exercise 1 show what applying it twice leads to.

q.zh: 为什么分析 logit 差，而不分析概率？
q.en: Why analyse logit differences and not probabilities?

a.zh: 有两个原因。logit 对残差流是（近似）线性的，可以按组件相加，概率经过 softmax 之后不再具有这种可加性。另外，对所有 logit 同时加上一个常数不改变任何概率，一个组件如果把所有 token 的 logit 一起抬高，实际上什么也没有改变。取两个候选答案的差可以消去这种无关的成分，剩下的才是使模型在两者之间作出选择的部分。
a.en: For two reasons. Logits are (approximately) linear in the residual stream and add up over components, whereas probabilities lose this additivity after the softmax. Moreover, adding a constant to all logits at once changes no probability, so a component that raises the logits of all tokens together changes nothing in effect. Taking the difference between two candidate answers removes such irrelevant parts and leaves what makes the model choose between the two.

q.zh: 直接归因为负的组件，是不是在妨碍模型答对？
q.en: Is a component with a negative direct attribution hindering the correct answer?

a.zh: 不一定。负的直接贡献表示这个组件写入残差流的向量在 $w_a - w_b$ 方向上的分量为负。它可能确实在支持竞争答案，也可能在做别的事情，例如为后面的组件准备输入，而这个向量恰好在该方向上有一个负的分量。直接归因看不到它经由后面各层产生的作用。要判断一个组件对答案的净作用，需要 9.3 的激活修补。
a.en: Not necessarily. A negative direct contribution means that the vector the component writes into the residual stream has a negative component along $w_a - w_b$. The component may indeed support the competing answer, or it may be doing something else, such as preparing input for later components, with a vector that happens to have a negative component in that direction. Direct attribution does not see the effect it has through later layers. Judging the net effect of a component on the answer takes the activation patching of 9.3.

q.zh: 为什么靠前的层解码出来的词看上去没有意义？
q.en: Why do the tokens decoded from early layers look meaningless?

a.zh: 嵌入之后直接解码，第一名通常是一个与输入无关的 token，在 Eiffel 的例子中是 destro。GPT-2 的输入嵌入与输出矩阵共享权重，加上位置嵌入并经过 LayerNorm 之后，得到的并不是当前 token 本身。之后几层的第一名多为 the 这样的高频词。nostalgebraist 在最初的文章中已经指出，输入在最初几层就被转换成了与输入差别很大的表示。靠前各层的表示主要服务于后续的计算，不是为了被输出矩阵读取，这正是 tuned lens 想要处理的问题。
a.en: Decoded directly after the embedding, the top token is usually unrelated to the input, destro in the Eiffel example. GPT-2 shares weights between input embedding and output matrix, yet after adding the position embedding and applying LayerNorm the result is not the current token itself. The top tokens of the next few layers are mostly frequent words such as the. nostalgebraist already noted in the original post that the input is converted within the first few layers into a representation very different from the input. The representations of the early layers mainly serve the later computation and are not meant to be read by the output matrix, which is the problem the tuned lens sets out to handle.

caption.zh: 六条提示上答案 token 在各层解码结果中的名次，由练习 1 的参考实现在 GPT-2 small 上算出。固定搭配在第 1 层之后即可读出，关于具体实体的事实要到第 10 层前后，需要比较两个名字的句子要到第 11 层。
caption.en: The rank of the answer token in the decoded result of every layer for six prompts, computed with the reference solution of exercise 1 on GPT-2 small. A fixed collocation can be read out after layer 1, facts about specific entities around layer 10, and the sentence that requires comparing two names at layer 11.

plain.zh: 把模型的 12 层想成一条有 12 道工序的装配线，正常情况下只能看到最后下线的成品。logit lens 相当于在每道工序之后把半成品直接送到出厂检验台，看一看如果现在就出厂，它会是什么。于是可以看到答案是在哪几道工序上成形的。直接归因则是统计每个工位各自往成品上添了多少。
plain.en: Think of the 12 layers of the model as an assembly line with 12 stations, of which normally only the finished product at the end is seen. The logit lens sends the half-finished product after every station straight to the final inspection desk to see what it would be if it left the factory now. This shows at which stations the answer takes shape. Direct attribution tallies how much each station added to the finished product.

summary.zh: 在两次只差一处的运行之间交换内部激活，测量每个位置、每一层和每个注意力头对输出的因果作用，并用梯度做快速近似。
summary.en: Swapping internal activations between two runs that differ in one place, to measure the causal effect of every position, layer and attention head on the output, with a fast approximation by gradients.

asof.zh: 本模块关于 TransformerLens 的内容截至 2026 年 11 月 25 日，对应 4.4.1 版。该库在 4.0 版更换了入口接口，较早的教程中的写法需要相应调整。
asof.en: The content of this module on TransformerLens is as of 25 November 2026 and refers to version 4.4.1. The library changed its entry interface in version 4.0, and code from earlier tutorials has to be adapted accordingly.

why.zh: 9.1 的注意力图和 9.2 的 logit lens 都是观察，它们提示某个组件可能重要，却不能证明。9.1 的消融是一种干预，但置零会把模型推到训练时没有见过的状态，而且它去掉的是一个组件的全部作用，无法只针对某一项具体的信息。激活修补解决这两个问题。它准备两条只在关键信息上不同的输入，把其中一次运行的某个内部激活换到另一次运行中，再看输出朝哪边移动。这样测到的是该激活所携带的那一项信息的因果作用，模型在整个过程中都处于正常的工作状态。它是目前定位模型内部计算时使用较广的因果方法。
why.en: The attention maps of 9.1 and the logit lens of 9.2 are observations. They suggest that a component may matter and cannot prove it. The ablation of 9.1 is an intervention, yet zeroing pushes the model into states not seen in training, and it removes the whole effect of a component without targeting one specific piece of information. Activation patching addresses both problems. Two inputs are prepared that differ in the key information alone, an internal activation of one run is moved into the other run, and the direction in which the output moves is observed. What is measured is the causal effect of the one piece of information that the activation carries, with the model in a normal working state throughout. It is currently a widely used causal method for locating computation inside a model.

goals.zh: 能用原生钩子实现对残差流和注意力头的激活修补
goals.en: Implement activation patching of the residual stream and of attention heads with raw hooks
